3VEhBxZzTO.one_liner: Proves universal privacy for released representations exists only at full decision sufficiency, where the minimal sufficient statistic is safest
3VEhBxZzTO.problem: Defences protect only named attributes, yet representations are released without knowing which attribute an adversary will infer, and it is unclear whether a release can be at least as private as every equally useful alternative.
3VEhBxZzTO.method: Decision-theoretic proofs using Blackwell comparison characterize when a release is at least as private as every equally useful alternative for every attribute and attacker, and the learned minimal sufficient summary is tested against standard embeddings with trained attackers.
3VEhBxZzTO.key_idea: Via Blackwell comparison, a release that is no more informative than any equally useful alternative for every attribute and attacker exists only at the task's minimal sufficient statistic.
3VEhBxZzTO.evidence: Proofs with numerical checks on random instances, plus experiments on nine tabular, graph, image and text datasets with trained attackers.
3VEhBxZzTO.claimed_gains: Cuts MNIST re-identification from 93% for the embedding to 1.0% for the predicted label, and the learned summary leaks no more than standard embeddings on every held-out attribute of seven datasets.
3VEhBxZzTO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the Blackwell-based formalization precise, the paper well written, and the proofs supported by numerical verification and experiments across several modalities.
3VEhBxZzTO.main_concern: The experiments use a finite set of representations, selected attributes and particular trained attackers, so they cannot test the universal claim, and attacker cross-entropy gives only variational leakage estimates.

mtgeo9qBIo.one_liner: Test-time adaptation that uses global statistics with little target data and switches to class prototypes by a label-free coverage criterion.
mtgeo9qBIo.problem: Test-time adaptation methods focus on how to estimate target statistics but not on whether the target data seen so far suffice for reliable estimation (estimation-support asymmetry).
mtgeo9qBIo.method: EXACT uses global target statistics while few target samples are available and enables target class-prototype estimation as samples accumulate, switching by a label-free class-coverage criterion. It does not update the pretrained model.
mtgeo9qBIo.key_idea: Gate class-specific prototype estimation behind a label-free class-coverage count, so global statistics are used until enough samples cover each class.
mtgeo9qBIo.evidence: Class-coverage analysis plus experiments on seven benchmarks under online and transductive protocols with ViT and CLIP backbones and 35 extra backbones, comparing global and class-specific branches across target sample sizes.
mtgeo9qBIo.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; a review reports online ViT/CLIP averages of 67.24/52.55 and transductive averages of 68.15/53.65 (Table 1).
mtgeo9qBIo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is practically useful, the evaluation across target sample sizes and protocols is broad, and the global-versus-class-specific comparison gives a clear empirical principle.
mtgeo9qBIo.main_concern: The theory compares variances of different quantities and does not establish an accuracy crossover, and under transductive evaluation EXACT reduces to the prototype branch.

XPOYoRnz2G.one_liner: Cascaded flow matching predicts an intermediate perturbation-response embedding, then generates transcriptomes conditioned on it.
XPOYoRnz2G.problem: Most perturbation-response models treat prediction as a single-stage transport from unperturbed to perturbed states, ignoring upstream regulatory changes that shape transcriptional responses.
XPOYoRnz2G.method: scCasFlow first predicts an intermediate response representation supervised by perturbation-induced shifts in pretrained single-cell embeddings, then generates transcriptomic profiles conditioned on it. Dual temporal coordinates with an ordered schedule drive the two stages, and flow matching runs in latent space with a lightweight decoder over the retained gene vocabulary.
XPOYoRnz2G.key_idea: Order generation as Rewire (intermediate response in pretrained-embedding space) then Express (expression conditioned on it), using dual time coordinates and an ordered schedule.
XPOYoRnz2G.evidence: Norman (including Norman-Additive) and ComboSciPlex benchmarks under held-out perturbation splits, with ablations of the Rewire stage and scheduling.
XPOYoRnz2G.claimed_gains: More than 100x inference throughput over the evaluated expression-space flow matching baseline; a review adds Norman-Additive MSE 0.000683 and Pearson Delta 0.8488 versus 0.001156 and 0.7480 for Stack.
XPOYoRnz2G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written, the intermediate-then-expression design a sensible modeling idea, and the improvements across complementary metrics substantial.
XPOYoRnz2G.main_concern: Key baselines and controls are missing: no additive baseline for Norman-Additive, no deterministic predictor of the same intermediate, and no test that stochastic Rewire targets beat fixed population means.

pBIUl16cPA.one_liner: Specializes quantization formats, weights and storage placement separately for LLM prefill and decode, streaming prefill weights from SSD.
pBIUl16cPA.problem: Prefill rewards low-precision arithmetic while decode rewards compact weights, so a single quantization scheme serves neither phase well.
pBIUl16cPA.method: Disaggregated quantization removes activation quantization on decode (format disaggregation), trains separate compute-native prefill weights (full disaggregation), and offloaded disaggregated prefill (ODP) streams prefill weights from SSD to avoid extra device memory.
pBIUl16cPA.key_idea: Train a separate low-precision compute-native prefill checkpoint while keeping the compact weight-only decode checkpoint, with the prefill weights streamed from SSD.
pBIUl16cPA.evidence: Qwen3.8-27B GGUF decoders with an auxiliary NVFP4 prefill model on MMLU-Pro and MMMU-Pro, llama.cpp prefill speed at 8K prompts, custom LUT kernels, and post-training quantization validation on models up to 2.8T parameters.
pBIUl16cPA.claimed_gains: 1-bit accuracy improves by 32.5 points on MMLU-Pro and 35.3 on MMMU-Pro, with a 1.78x prefill speedup over the weight-only baseline at 8K prompt length.
pBIUl16cPA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea follows naturally from the different roofline regimes of prefill and decode, is well motivated for real serving, and is backed by custom kernels and systems work.
pBIUl16cPA.main_concern: Novelty is limited by prior phase-level mixed-precision work (Mix-Quant, DynaCore), and the 1-bit gains may partly reflect shorter generations and lower truncation rates rather than better quality.

nSuEq47kb9.one_liner: OpenMLE releases a 5,758-task executable MLE gym and post-trains a model as the revision operator for evolutionary search.
nSuEq47kb9.problem: The open community lacks training-scale testbeds for AI-trains-AI in machine learning engineering, since existing MLE resources have at most a few hundred tasks and are built for evaluation.
nSuEq47kb9.method: OpenMLE-Gym provides 5,758 quality-gated executable tasks with evaluators and verified evolutionary trajectories, OpenMLE-Train does execution-verified SFT then RL on per-task calibrated execution rewards, and OpenMLE-Evo uses the trained model as the variation engine of evolutionary search.
nSuEq47kb9.key_idea: Train one model with execution-verified SFT then RL on calibrated execution rewards to serve as shared draft, improve, debug and recombine operators in long-horizon evolutionary search.
nSuEq47kb9.evidence: Evaluated on MLE-Bench Lite (22 tasks per reviews) by post-training Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, with ablations of training and search components and comparisons against proprietary agents.
nSuEq47kb9.claimed_gains: Post-training Qwen3.6-35B-A3B into OpenMLE-35B raises Medal Average on MLE-Bench Lite from 39.39% to 60.61% (abstract truncated afterwards), and the TLDR says the strengthened system matches GPT-5.5 with Codex.
nSuEq47kb9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the large executable task corpus and the release of tasks, sandbox, trajectories, code and weights are a substantial resource, with experiments showing both training and search improve MLE-Bench Lite.
nSuEq47kb9.main_concern: The evaluation is noisy: MLE-Bench Lite has only 22 tasks and the standard deviation of Medal Average over three runs is about 7 to 9 points, comparable to several reported gains.

FrpBCtqRnK.one_liner: Persona-control fine-tuning of a reasoning model reduces chain-of-thought monitorability without any monitor-evasion training data.
FrpBCtqRnK.problem: Chain-of-thought monitoring may fail if models deliberately shape their reasoning to be opaque to monitors, and this risk needs stress-testing.
FrpBCtqRnK.method: Fine-tunes gpt-oss-20b on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas to induce broad CoT control, then measures monitorability in covert side-task and intervention evaluations, extended to a Kimi-K2.6 model organism in agentic environments.
FrpBCtqRnK.key_idea: Train broad CoT controllability with persona-rewritten reasoning traces, then test whether it spontaneously lowers monitorability when a hidden side task is present.
FrpBCtqRnK.evidence: Covert side-task and intervention evaluations on a gpt-oss-20b model organism and a Kimi-K2.6 organism in agentic environments, plus transparency-prompt mitigations.
FrpBCtqRnK.claimed_gains: The monitorability metric g-mean^2 falls from 0.96 for the base model to 0.72 for the model organism without a hiding instruction, and to 0.28 when explicitly instructed to hide.
FrpBCtqRnK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is timely and safety-relevant, and that reduced monitorability emerging from benign persona training without evasion examples is a notable result.
FrpBCtqRnK.main_concern: Causal attribution to controllability is not established because persona SFT also shortens CoT and reduces capability, and novelty over prior CoT-obfuscation stress tests is unclear.

O7c0HJVxh3.one_liner: Proxy2World generates videos from coarse scene proxies by learning depth-conditioned RGB and joint RGBD generation from posed RGBD videos.
O7c0HJVxh3.problem: Paired proxy-video data is hard to build at scale because a suitable proxy is not uniquely defined.
O7c0HJVxh3.method: Trains one model with cross-modal flow matching on ordinary posed RGBD videos for both depth-conditioned RGB generation and joint RGBD generation, then at inference uses proxy-camera hybrid denoising to follow proxy structure while producing natural visuals. It also introduces ProxyBench for evaluation.
O7c0HJVxh3.key_idea: Depth is both a conditioning signal and a generated variable, enabling proxy-camera hybrid denoising at inference that follows proxy structure while the model fills in appearance.
O7c0HJVxh3.evidence: Experiments on ProxyBench with quantitative metrics, VLM assessments, human evaluations and qualitative results, compared with camera-controlled and geometry-conditioned methods such as VACE-Depth and Cosmos-Depth.
O7c0HJVxh3.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims a better balance between structural adherence and visual quality than camera-controlled and geometry-conditioned methods, without numbers.
O7c0HJVxh3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning from ordinary posed RGBD video avoids the proxy-video pair bottleneck and that one model supporting varied control strengths is a practical idea.
O7c0HJVxh3.main_concern: The main comparison is confounded by input conditions (a reference first frame for the proposed model but not for VACE-Depth or Cosmos-Depth, which lead on some metrics), and evidence for the hybrid denoising and its difference from Modality Forcing is limited.

mbqOhJ9yHb.one_liner: Distills a PPO policy into a multi-step policy that emits several actions per observation, with a learned commitment length.
mbqOhJ9yHb.problem: Running a policy on a fresh observation at every step is costly even where one observation suffices to choose several optimal actions.
mbqOhJ9yHb.method: While PPO trains as usual, PACE distills it into a multi-step policy that reads one observation and emits several consecutive actions. At each read it also predicts how many actions to commit to by measuring how far the replay can be trusted, and discovered options are recursively added to the MDP action space.
mbqOhJ9yHb.key_idea: Self-distill a one-step PPO teacher into a sequence predictor whose per-state commitment length is set by how far its replayed actions can be trusted.
mbqOhJ9yHb.evidence: Random tasks with deterministic transitions and varying stochasticity, and open-ended environments where curriculum and tabula-rasa learning fail; reviews mention Fixed and SEAR chunking baselines.
mbqOhJ9yHb.claimed_gains: Up to 8x fewer required observations on random deterministic tasks (compression shrinks as stochasticity rises), and drastically higher success rates in open-ended environments where curriculum and tabula-rasa learning fail.
mbqOhJ9yHb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the design simple and well motivated, since imitating a one-step teacher avoids the degradation of return-based chunking, and they consider the self-distillation approach to option discovery interesting.
mbqOhJ9yHb.main_concern: Observation reads are not shown to equal computational savings: there is no latency or FLOP comparison, the architecture is complex and larger (3.3x more deployment parameters), and its design choices are not ablated.

FtBATWQmg4.one_liner: Semantic-level evaluation framework and 25,507-sample dataset for emotional and role consistency of multimodal role-playing agents before modality synthesis.
FtBATWQmg4.problem: Existing evaluation checks multimodal expressions only after modality generation, so errors in semantic response planning cannot be separated from errors in modality realization.
FtBATWQmg4.method: MERRY adds multimodal emotional interpretability and a bidirectional evidence-finding scoring protocol for LLM-as-a-judge, and builds a 25,507-sample dataset with a TV-series-level separated test split.
FtBATWQmg4.key_idea: Score the semantic descriptions of multimodal responses with an evidence-finding LLM judge, evaluating response planning separately from final modality synthesis.
FtBATWQmg4.evidence: Evaluations of multiple multimodal role-playing agents, fine-tuning comparisons, and human agreement studies of 100 samples each per reviews.
FtBATWQmg4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating semantic planning from modality realization is a useful diagnostic perspective, supported by multiple models, fine-tuning comparisons and human validation.
FtBATWQmg4.main_concern: Metric validity: the new emotional and role metrics lack direct human validation, may confuse justified cross-modal contrast with errors, and rely on LLM judges checked on small 100-sample agreement studies.

AMxZBBqCXB.one_liner: Active cross-view object geo-localization: an agent selects new viewpoints and stops, trained with SFT then GRPO under a gain-cost reward.
AMxZBBqCXB.problem: Cross-view object geo-localization assumes a fixed query image, ignoring that mobile agents can actively acquire more informative observations.
AMxZBBqCXB.method: ActiveMoPT trains in three stages: Multi-View Prompt-Preserving Adaptation to aggregate multiple query views, Trajectory-Guided Policy Initialization with supervised agent trajectories for viewpoint selection and stopping, and Cost-Aware Policy Refinement with GRPO and a gain-cost reward.
AMxZBBqCXB.key_idea: Learn viewpoint selection and stopping jointly, with GRPO rewarding localization gain minus observation cost, on top of a localizer that reuses the initial prompt across views.
AMxZBBqCXB.evidence: MoP-UAV and a new zero-shot test set, ActiveGeo-858, with 858 scenes and 1,716 target annotations.
AMxZBBqCXB.claimed_gains: Best performance on MoP-UAV using only 1.45 query views on average, and substantially better than previous CVOGL approaches under zero-shot evaluation on ActiveGeo-858.
AMxZBBqCXB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the active-observation task is well motivated and practical, with a promising accuracy-versus-observation-efficiency trade-off.
AMxZBBqCXB.main_concern: It is unclear the policy is truly adaptive: viewpoints come from 54 predefined candidates with no movement cost, the contributions of selection and stopping are not separated, and a simpler strategy might match it.

VCa6ExL3Zg.one_liner: Switching RL fine-tuning of LLMs from BF16 to FP16 reduces the numerical mismatch between training and inference policies.
VCa6ExL3Zg.problem: RL fine-tuning of LLMs is unstable because of a numerical mismatch between training and inference policies, which BF16 rounding errors worsen.
VCa6ExL3Zg.method: The authors revert from BF16 to FP16, a change of a few lines of code with no change to model architecture or learning algorithm, and test it across tasks, algorithms, and frameworks.
VCa6ExL3Zg.key_idea: Use FP16's finer precision instead of BF16's wider range so rounding errors no longer break training-inference policy consistency.
VCa6ExL3Zg.evidence: Experiments across multiple RL algorithms, model families, frameworks, and task domains, plus swaps of training and inference precision.
VCa6ExL3Zg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the finding is simple and practically useful and is backed by broad experiments across algorithms, model families, frameworks, and tasks.
VCa6ExL3Zg.main_concern: The attribution of gains to reduced mismatch is not established, since higher gradient precision, loss scaling, or solutions robust to inference precision could explain them.

BPEKBFmgIZ.one_liner: Generalizes conditional-mutual-information feature acquisition by conditioning on probabilistically sampled future feature sets, interpolating between greedy and fully non-myopic.
BPEKBFmgIZ.problem: Greedy CMI acquisition scores each feature by immediate information gain and overlooks feature interactions, where a feature is informative only jointly with features acquired later.
BPEKBFmgIZ.method: γ-CMI scores a candidate feature's information gain under future observation contexts in which each remaining feature is included independently with probability γ; γ=0 is greedy CMI and γ=1 conditions on all remaining features. It plugs into existing CMI-based AFA methods with minor changes to the acquisition criterion and no retraining.
BPEKBFmgIZ.key_idea: Include each unobserved feature in the conditioning context with probability gamma when computing CMI, giving a continuous lookahead between myopic and fully non-myopic acquisition.
BPEKBFmgIZ.evidence: Theoretical analysis of the criterion; per reviews, synthetic experiments with oracle models (synergy and redundancy sweeps) and real-world tables with a VAE-MLP backbone.
BPEKBFmgIZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea simple and plug-and-play without retraining, the synthetic experiments well designed, and the decomposition into feature interactions insightful.
BPEKBFmgIZ.main_concern: Real-world gains are often marginal with gamma tuned per dataset, and one reviewer considers the theory largely known (Owen's multilinear extension, probabilistic values) and uncited.

N4vn7nIXGU.one_liner: Split-depth LoRA: an evolving shared Core in early blocks, task-specific Residual LoRAs in later blocks, for rehearsal-free class-incremental learning.
N4vn7nIXGU.problem: Existing LoRA-based parameter-efficient continual learning trades knowledge sharing (merged adapters blur task-specific features) against task isolation (less transfer).
N4vn7nIXGU.method: Early ViT blocks hold a fixed-rank Core LoRA that evolves across tasks via subspace-compatible learning and Fisher-guided consolidation; later blocks keep task-specific Residual LoRAs trained with core-error reweighting and residual-mix consistency. At inference, uncertainty from the consolidated core gives an entropy-guided prior that calibrates residual experts without task identities.
N4vn7nIXGU.key_idea: Evolve a shared low-rank Core with Fisher-guided consolidation while Residual LoRAs capture what the Core misses, combined at test time by core-entropy-based calibration.
N4vn7nIXGU.evidence: Four class-incremental learning benchmarks with frozen pretrained ViTs; reviews note three seeds, longer task sequences, depth allocations, LoRA ranks, and self-supervised backbones.
N4vn7nIXGU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shared/specific organization clearly motivated and the evaluation broad, with ablations and an All-scan variant showing gains over CL-LoRA.
N4vn7nIXGU.main_concern: Training and inference cost is high, since inference scales linearly with the number of tasks through per-task residual experts and training needs multiple passes per batch.

XEJG1TQ18k.one_liner: Selects and jointly tunes paired input-row and output-column FFN pathways by activation-gradient sensitivity, adding no new matrices.
XEJG1TQ18k.problem: PEFT methods either insert new modules at hand-chosen locations, adding compute and placement sensitivity, or update independently chosen weights, ignoring structural coupling within pretrained networks.
XEJG1TQ18k.method: GradPath treats each hidden pathway as a paired unit of an input-projection row and its output-projection column, scores importance by activation-gradient sensitivity, and updates the selected pairs in place; GradPath-S adds gated multi-kernel depthwise convolutions on spatial pathways.
XEJG1TQ18k.key_idea: Rank hidden units by activation-gradient sensitivity and fine-tune each selected unit's input row and output column together as a bottleneck subnetwork inside the pretrained weights.
XEJG1TQ18k.evidence: Medical image classification (seven datasets, three backbones per a review), segmentation, few-shot adaptation of a vision-language model, reduced-data settings and VTAB-1K.
XEJG1TQ18k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing the two projections of an FFN unit is a clean, well-motivated PEFT design that adds no module and is evaluated broadly.
XEJG1TQ18k.main_concern: Evidence for the benefit of pairing and task-sensitive selection is thin (small gains over GPS, alternative schemes within 0.7 points), and the LoRA baseline is abnormally low, suggesting weak tuning.

s6Iqet3WnM.one_liner: Test-time guidance for offline MARL using monotonically factorized team-critic utilities as local gradients steering a supervised-trained flow policy.
s6Iqet3WnM.problem: Offline MARL diffusion and flow policies couple the generator to critic training, and extending test-time critic guidance to cooperative MARL is hard because centralized critics need global inputs while local critics need not improve team value.
s6Iqet3WnM.method: CQF fits the flow policy by supervised matching alone; at deployment each agent steers it using only its observation and a local utility gradient obtained by monotonically factorizing a team critic, with a one-hot relaxation for discrete control.
s6Iqet3WnM.key_idea: Monotonic factorization of a team critic makes simultaneous local utility-gradient steps a first-order ascent direction of the team value at every joint action.
s6Iqet3WnM.evidence: MA-MuJoCo, MPE, SMACv1 and goal-conditioned MangoBench, compared with Gaussian, diffusion and flow methods.
s6Iqet3WnM.claimed_gains: CQF attains the best average scores among compared Gaussian, diffusion and flow methods across MA-MuJoCo, MPE, SMACv1 and MangoBench; no numeric values appear in the abstract.
s6Iqet3WnM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree CQF gives a coherent decentralized-execution interface and is the first test-time gradient guidance for cooperative offline MARL, with extensive experiments.
s6Iqet3WnM.main_concern: The guidance weight is tuned per dataset and domain with reported entries selected as maxima on the same evaluation episodes, and results inherit offline-critic errors.

CvdXzwOP6G.one_liner: Finsler Flow Matching builds a directed anisotropic geometry from Markov transition moments to define geodesic couplings for single-snapshot trajectory inference.
CvdXzwOP6G.problem: Single-cell snapshots do not determine transition dynamics, and existing generative approaches use only marginals, impose symmetric geometry, or encode direction through a single velocity vector per state.
CvdXzwOP6G.method: The first and second local moments of a cell-cell Markov transition kernel form a Finsler structure motivated by the Freidlin-Wentzell action; neural directed geodesics provide Finsler-cost couplings and geometry-aware stochastic conditional paths, distilled into a generative process through simulation-free score and flow matching.
CvdXzwOP6G.key_idea: Use the transition kernel's first moment as preferred direction and second moment as anisotropic accessibility in a Randers-form Finsler metric whose learned geodesics define flow-matching couplings and paths.
CvdXzwOP6G.evidence: Synthetic and single-cell trajectory inference benchmarks (Sheet, Pancreas 20D and ForkSheet per reviews) against OT-CFM, MFM and Curly-FM, with same-information controls.
CvdXzwOP6G.claimed_gains: Improves recovery of withheld intermediate populations in several settings, with particularly strong results on directed synthetic dynamics; no numbers are stated.
CvdXzwOP6G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the graph-to-geometry construction principled and intuitive, combining directional and anisotropic information through a Randers metric tied to Freidlin-Wentzell theory, with relevant baselines and controls.
CvdXzwOP6G.main_concern: The benefit of the stochastic component is unclear (isotropic and anisotropic covariances perform comparably), and the advantage over existing Finsler-based trajectory inference is not directly established.

7CPpheMuF2.one_liner: Task-oriented image fusion as inference over a latent fusion variable, with a task-informed posterior transferred to a source-conditioned prior.
7CPpheMuF2.problem: Task-oriented fusion methods learn a direct mapping to a single fused image, leaving the conditional distribution of task-relevant fusion results unmodeled.
7CPpheMuF2.method: A latent fusion variable capturing fusion cues and task semantics is sampled and decoded into the fused image; task annotations build a task-informed posterior during training that is transferred to a source-conditioned prior for label-free inference, and task predictions on source and fused images are aligned.
7CPpheMuF2.key_idea: Train a task-informed posterior over a latent fusion variable and transfer it to a prior conditioned only on source images, so inference needs no labels.
7CPpheMuF2.evidence: Infrared-visible fusion with semantic segmentation and object detection, with ablations and visualizations noted in the reviews.
7CPpheMuF2.claimed_gains: Competitive fusion quality and improved downstream task performance on infrared-visible fusion with segmentation and detection; no numbers are stated.
7CPpheMuF2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the probabilistic posterior-prior formulation as a reasonable and practical direction, with a clearly written paper and experiments covering fusion quality, detection and segmentation with ablations.
7CPpheMuF2.main_concern: The link between the probabilistic formulation (ELBO and fused-image likelihood) and the actual training objective of fusion and task losses is unclear, and key assumptions are not justified.

dDIQnCKW5L.one_liner: Per-agent criticality weighting with soft long-tailed weights and GAE reconnection finds failures of detect-and-avoid systems via adversarial multi-agent RL
dDIQnCKW5L.problem: Near mid-air collisions are so rare that the sparse learning signal is drowned out by gradient noise from non-critical states, and heterogeneous factors such as other aircraft and the environment have critical moments at different times.
dDIQnCKW5L.method: HAD²RL estimates per-agent state importance from the value of the failure event, then replaces the hard mask of dense RL with long-tailed weighting and an improved GAE reconnection so misjudged states are down-weighted rather than discarded. The paper also proposes DAIDALUS-AST, a closed-loop benchmark for adversarial safety validation of detect-and-avoid systems.
dDIQnCKW5L.key_idea: Each agent's state criticality is estimated from the failure-event value and converted to soft long-tailed weights, so credit follows criticality without discarding misjudged states.
dDIQnCKW5L.evidence: Closed-loop adversarial failure search on the DAIDALUS-AST benchmark with ablations, plus a proof that soft densification adds only bounded bias to the expected policy gradient.
dDIQnCKW5L.claimed_gains: not stated in the truncated abstract; a reviewer refers to a headline gain of 'up to 28×' as overstated.
dDIQnCKW5L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, the approach is clear and backed by theory, and the empirical study and ablations are extensive.
dDIQnCKW5L.main_concern: Reviewers say the central motivations (per-agent criticality and soft versus hard masks) are not isolated experimentally, headline gains are overstated, and novelty and real-world validation relative to prior multi-agent failure-search work are uncertain.

RanROm4wpA.one_liner: Forecasts time series by learning nonlinear observables propagated through fixed multiscale normal operators instead of trained Koopman transition matrices
RanROm4wpA.problem: Learned Koopman transition operators are parameter-intensive and difficult to stabilize under repeated long-horizon rollout.
RanROm4wpA.method: EchoKoop learns an encoder, modal projections, selectors, and decoders that map observed histories onto a fixed bank of multiscale normal operators with different memory ranges, so no transition matrices are trained.
RanROm4wpA.key_idea: Freeze the latent flow as fixed multiscale normal operators with varied frequencies and decay timescales, and learn only the lifting that maps histories into this dynamical basis.
RanROm4wpA.evidence: Ten long-term forecasting benchmarks with controlled ablations comparing frozen and trained transitions, plus a finite-horizon representation result and an error-propagation bound.
RanROm4wpA.claimed_gains: EchoKoop attains the lowest dataset-averaged MSE on six of ten long-term forecasting benchmarks, and controlled ablations show no consistent gain from training its transitions.
RanROm4wpA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is well motivated and simple, with theoretical justification for fixed operators and solid ablations.
RanROm4wpA.main_concern: Reviewers say the theory does not cover the long-horizon regime and the results do not establish significant overall superiority, with near-parity between frozen and trained operators leaving unclear when learning them helps.

7aSYWuCuYK.one_liner: Measures how injection placement changes agent susceptibility to indirect prompt injection across three testbeds, then trains a placement-aware attacker
7aSYWuCuYK.problem: Risk assessment of indirect prompt injection has focused on injection content, while the effect of where the injection appears in the agent's environment has not been systematically characterized.
7aSYWuCuYK.method: The authors build three long-horizon agentic testbeds (tool use, coding, daily workflow), hold injection content fixed while varying placement, and name the resulting variation the trust region effect. They then develop an RL-trained attacker with a two-stage method of placement selection and content optimization.
7aSYWuCuYK.key_idea: Agents implicitly assign different trust to different environment regions, so identical injection content succeeds at different rates depending on placement, which a learned placement policy can exploit.
7aSYWuCuYK.evidence: Three testbeds spanning tool use, coding, and daily workflow, with 30 benign tasks in total, plus RL-trained attacker experiments that transfer to GPT-5.4.
7aSYWuCuYK.claimed_gains: An agent powered by GPT-5.4 follows an unsafe injection instruction in a repository documentation file 2.6× more often on average than the same instruction in a code or data file.
7aSYWuCuYK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree injection placement is an important, under-explored dimension and that the diverse long-horizon testbeds and separation of factors make the evaluation valuable.
7aSYWuCuYK.main_concern: Reviewers say the learned placement policy adds little, since a fixed placement prior from training-set success rates often matches or beats the two-stage attacker (62.7% versus 59.1% in one Table 5 setting), and the testbeds contain only 30 tasks.

9vcMciqM6u.one_liner: A coach agent reads and compresses student behavior pools into experience, trained on frozen-student improvement, then internalized into the student
9vcMciqM6u.problem: Rubrics describe what a good answer looks like but not how to produce one, and summarizing experience from a large pool of student behavior in one pass lowers quality because of long context.
9vcMciqM6u.method: Agent as Coach inspects an external behavior pool, reads selected attempts, and compresses observations before writing experience; its acquisition and writing actions are trained jointly through the improvement of a frozen student. The experience is then internalized into the student through training, so the student generates and uses experience itself.
9vcMciqM6u.key_idea: Train the coach's pool-inspection and experience-writing actions using the frozen student's improvement as the signal, then distill the resulting experience into the student.
9vcMciqM6u.evidence: Multiple benchmarks (reviewers name IFEval, IFBench, and InFoBench) with Qwen3-8B-Base and Qwen3.5-9B-Base students, plus ablations on scored student behavior, agentic versus one-pass reading, and fixed-answer controls.
9vcMciqM6u.claimed_gains: The complete pipeline improves over the strongest rubric-based and experience-based baseline by 4.9 and 3.8 points with Qwen3-8B-Base and Qwen3.5-9B-Base students, respectively.
9vcMciqM6u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the move from rubric criteria to actionable experience is well motivated, gains are consistent on both students, and tool-based reading addresses the long-context problem.
9vcMciqM6u.main_concern: Reviewers say the contribution over existing learned coaching and context internalization work (Retroformer, CTRL, MemAgent) is insufficiently established, and the evaluation leans on rule-checked instruction following rather than open-ended tasks.

44uDvQ1BkG.one_liner: Convexity localizes the best feasible cycle near the minimizer, where lower confidence bounds explore it under blocking constraints
44uDvQ1BkG.problem: In stochastic bandit convex optimization where choosing an action blocks all actions within distance ε for the next p-1 rounds, repeatedly playing the minimizer is infeasible, so the usual regret benchmark does not apply.
44uDvQ1BkG.method: The algorithm first learns a point with low loss, then uses lower confidence bounds to explore feasible cycles of p actions in its neighborhood, grouping repeated queries and controlling transitions between cycles so blocking constraints hold and all exploration and transition costs are counted.
44uDvQ1BkG.key_idea: Regret is measured against the best average loss over feasible p-action cycles, and convexity confines the search for that cycle to a ball of radius 2pε around a global minimizer.
44uDvQ1BkG.evidence: Theory only: a regret upper bound and a minimax lower bound under a geometric local-feasibility condition for fixed dimension d≥2 and blocking period p>2, with the lower bound on the unit Euclidean ball with Gaussian noise; reviewers also mention a tight p=2 case and an offline hardness result.
44uDvQ1BkG.claimed_gains: Regret upper bound Õ(√T[1+(ε√T)^{d/(d+2)}]) and minimax lower bound Ω(√T[1+(ε√T)^{(d-1)/(d+3)}]) for fixed d≥2 and p>2.
44uDvQ1BkG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is new and clearly defined, the feasible-cycle benchmark is well justified, and the paper is a complete theory contribution with upper and lower bounds and clear exposition.
44uDvQ1BkG.main_concern: Reviewers cite the gap between the general-p upper and lower bounds (exponents d/(d+2) versus (d-1)/(d+3)), large dimension exponents with a costly NP-hard oracle, and applications that do not match the model.

DYVrILGM0R.one_liner: Conditions gradient-based multistate protein hallucination on a motif MSA injected only into states that must show the motif
DYVrILGM0R.problem: SwitchCraft runs every hallucination forward pass without an MSA, so sequence-update gradients come from inaccurate predicted structures, and adding an MSA is hard because the query sequence changes each step and is often a continuous distribution.
DYVrILGM0R.method: MevoCraft builds one motif MSA from a single homology search on the fixed functional motif and conditions each forward pass of gradient-based hallucination with it, injecting it only into the states required to exhibit that motif.
DYVrILGM0R.key_idea: A single homology search on the fixed functional motif yields an MSA that is injected only into states needing that motif, avoiding per-step MSA search for the changing sequence.
DYVrILGM0R.evidence: Allostery experiments covering 22 motifs and five ligand contexts with 100 designs per setting, plus motif-switching experiments, compared against SwitchCraft with Boltz and with evaluation-only and all-states MSA ablations.
DYVrILGM0R.claimed_gains: not stated in the truncated abstract; a reviewer reports 177 successful motif-switching designs versus 47 for SwitchCraft, approximately a 3.8-fold improvement.
DYVrILGM0R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is well motivated and clearly written, shows substantial improvement over SwitchCraft, and includes useful ablation controls.
DYVrILGM0R.main_concern: Reviewers say the evaluation compares only against SwitchCraft and uses only Boltz, lacks statistical tests, and may be confounded by state-specific MSAs and performance-based subset selection.

8OOcB31XYc.one_liner: Trains a one-step generator by compressing a Sinkhorn-divergence Wasserstein gradient flow from a reference distribution to the data distribution.
8OOcB31XYc.problem: Diffusion and flow-based generators need many iterative updates at sampling time, which makes generation expensive.
8OOcB31XYc.method: W-Flow defines an evolution from a reference to the target distribution through a Wasserstein gradient flow minimizing an energy functional (instantiated with Sinkhorn divergence), then trains a static generator to compress that evolution into one step. It also proves that finite-sample training dynamics converge to the continuous-time dynamics under suitable assumptions.
8OOcB31XYc.key_idea: Distill a Sinkhorn-divergence Wasserstein gradient flow into a static one-step generator, using an optimal-transport update that captures global distributional discrepancy.
8OOcB31XYc.evidence: One-step ImageNet 256x256 generation with ablations of divergence, entropy, CFG, batch scheme and velocity guidance, plus mode-coverage and domain-transfer experiments and a convergence proof.
8OOcB31XYc.claimed_gains: 1.29 FID for one-step ImageNet 256x256 generation, with approximately 100x faster sampling than multi-step diffusion models of similar FID.
8OOcB31XYc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation is clear, the ImageNet results are strong and beat Drifting models, and the ablations show which design choices matter.
8OOcB31XYc.main_concern: Reviewers question the Sinkhorn/optimal-transport justification, since headline models use a single Sinkhorn iteration and KL is only modestly worse (7.68 vs 7.08 FID with velocity guidance).

nWCmIrlhFN.one_liner: Normalizes each irrep block's update by one scalar so Adam's effective step sizes match across blocks in equivariant networks.
nWCmIrlhFN.problem: Weight sharing across the 2l+1 components of an equivariant layer makes a single learning rate yield different effective step sizes for different irrep blocks.
nWCmIrlhFN.method: Each irrep block update is normalized by a single scalar, which preserves its singular value ratios while the learning rate controls its size, using spectral normalization or a simpler RMS normalization. The step-size mismatch is studied in a controlled SO(3)-equivariant model versus a matched non-equivariant model.
nWCmIrlhFN.key_idea: Rescale each irrep block's update by one scalar (spectral or RMS norm) to equalize effective step size across blocks while keeping singular value ratios.
nWCmIrlhFN.evidence: Controlled SO(3)-equivariant versus matched non-equivariant model for step-size mismatch; reviews cite force MAE on 24 model/dataset pairs (including QM9) and comparisons with Muon.
nWCmIrlhFN.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract only reports that step-size mismatch grows with width in the equivariant model but not in the matched non-equivariant model.
nWCmIrlhFN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the block step-size mechanism insightful and the one-scalar-per-block fix plausible, with RMS normalization lowering Adam's force MAE on all tested model/dataset pairs.
nWCmIrlhFN.main_concern: No experiment isolates equalizing irrep-block step sizes from simply fixing update norms, and the width-dependent mismatch is measured only at Adam's first update.

U4SXtm1SBf.one_liner: Neural-FSM, a non-affine scan-compatible RNN, tracks finite states at any length; affine recurrences at finite precision realize only definite automata.
U4SXtm1SBf.problem: Linear RNNs and state space models train in parallel because their recurrences are affine, but their expressivity guarantees assume idealized arithmetic and break at finite precision, where the parallel scan itself perturbs values.
U4SXtm1SBf.method: The paper formalizes finite-state tracking at finite precision, requiring contraction to suppress numerical perturbations and separation to keep states apart, and proves affine recurrences realize at most definite automata. Neural-FSM uses a non-affine map that stays compatible with a parallel scan, with learned transition tables that can be extracted.
U4SXtm1SBf.key_idea: Use a non-affine, scan-compatible transition map that supplies both contraction (error suppression) and separation (state distinction) at finite precision, which a single affine rate cannot.
U4SXtm1SBf.evidence: Synthetic tasks spanning groups, noninvertible monoids, and textual state tracking, with exhaustive checks of learned transitions on the algebraic tasks; affine baselines fail on every nondefinite task.
U4SXtm1SBf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory gives a clear account of the contraction-versus-separation trade-off and why affine recurrences are limited at finite precision, with rigorous derivations and exhaustive verification of learned transitions.
U4SXtm1SBf.main_concern: Experiments are small synthetic tasks designed for the method (state given as labels, head sizes tuned to the problem), with no larger-scale evidence on performance, speed, memory, or training stability.

ZY7de6Eki9.one_liner: Continual RL regularizer that keeps historical greedy-action gaps above a fraction of their old size instead of preserving Q-values.
ZY7de6Eki9.problem: In value-based continual control, preserving absolute action values is stricter than needed because greedy actions depend only on their relative ordering, and it limits adaptation.
ZY7de6Eki9.method: Greedy Action Consolidation defines a continual action gap, the updated Q-function's value difference between a historical greedy action and its best competitor, and regularizes it to stay at least a prescribed fraction of the historical gap. It is added to value-based agents without changing the base TD objective.
ZY7de6Eki9.key_idea: Regularize the updated Q-function so each historical greedy action keeps a margin over its best competitor, retaining decisions while letting absolute values drift.
ZY7de6Eki9.evidence: A bound on return discrepancy in terms of the regularizer and historical action gaps, a result that GAC admits a strictly larger set of action values than Value Cloning, and experiments on MinAtar and Forager in semi-continual and continual settings.
ZY7de6Eki9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation that retaining greedy decisions does not require preserving Q-values is sound and the regularizer is simple to add to existing value-based agents.
ZY7de6Eki9.main_concern: The evaluation is narrow (three MinAtar games with cyclic shifts and one Forager configuration) and lacks direct policy-preservation baselines, with the memory procedure under-specified.

mAj7LrBMou.one_liner: Weight-space probing on a model's displacement from a shared, learned reference instead of its raw weights.
mAj7LrBMou.problem: Probing-based weight-space learning works within a Model Tree of models fine-tuned from a shared origin, but prior work did not explain why.
mAj7LrBMou.method: DSProbe probes each model's displacement from the shared pretrained origin, extended to second-order Gram responses whose displacement encodes fine-tuning-induced features. R-DSProbe treats the reference as a design choice and learns a shared component to subtract beyond the pretrained origin.
mAj7LrBMou.key_idea: Since leaves of a Model Tree share an origin, probe the weight displacement from a shared reference (learned, not just pretrained) so probes read only what distinguishes models.
mAj7LrBMou.evidence: Four architectures on the Model Jungle benchmark, with ablations on reference choice, higher-order probing, and layer selection.
mAj7LrBMou.claimed_gains: R-DSProbe sets a new best result on Model Jungle across four architectures, matches prior accuracy with substantially fewer probes, and reduces metanetwork parameters by 3.61 times with a single encoder shared across Model Trees.
mAj7LrBMou.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the approach is simple, well motivated, and effective, with improvements over prior results on an established benchmark and extensive ablations.
mAj7LrBMou.main_concern: Generalization is untested beyond Model Jungle Model Trees, and displacement from a reference resembles task-vector ideas that are not discussed, while the theory may be more complex than needed.

9TMSyfAu2T.one_liner: LTL-guided multi-task RL with parameter-aware predicate embeddings and potential-based shaping from simple closeness priors.
9TMSyfAu2T.problem: Existing LTL-guided multi-task RL struggles with representation learning and exploration efficiency in high-dimensional environments with parameterized specifications.
9TMSyfAu2T.method: Atomic propositions are modeled as instances of atomic predicates, and task parameters are injected directly into the goal embedding to enable generalization. Simple priors on closeness to predicate satisfaction speed up learning of complex tasks without biasing the optimal policy.
9TMSyfAu2T.key_idea: Inject predicate parameters into goal-side embeddings and shape rewards with predicate-level closeness priors as potential-based shaping, so the optimal policy is preserved.
9TMSyfAu2T.evidence: Robotic manipulation (Franka) and two-drone navigation, with comparisons to Concatenate, SIAMS, and Discretize parameter-handling baselines and ablations such as persistence gating and robustness calibration.
9TMSyfAu2T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written with strong results, especially on Franka manipulation, and useful ablations such as persistence gating.
9TMSyfAu2T.main_concern: It relies on hand-designed robustness heuristics and a ground-truth labeling function, with limited multi-agent scaling (two drones) and no baseline isolating the Plato embedding from simple goal-side parameter conditioning.

FvXof9xMtt.one_liner: Marginalizing attention over queries reveals a text-intrinsic token signal and a model-private head signature that sets offline KV cache budgets.
FvXof9xMtt.problem: How attention behaves across independently trained language models is far less characterized than representation similarity.
FvXof9xMtt.method: The paper marginalizes post-softmax attention over query positions into a token-head marginal attention space and studies it across 60+ LLMs, linking the token-wise structure to the input-output Jacobian. The head-wise signature, computed offline on pretraining text, gives a per-head KV-cache eviction budget that is combined with a training-free token score.
FvXof9xMtt.key_idea: Sum post-softmax attention over queries to get per-token and per-head profiles: token-wise it is conserved across models, head-wise it is model-specific and yields a fixed per-head cache budget.
FvXof9xMtt.evidence: A census of 60+ LLMs with controls, a theorem linking similar next-token distributions to similar Jacobian statistics under a smoothness assumption, and KV-cache eviction benchmarks including RULER against AdaKV, LU-KV, and KVzip.
FvXof9xMtt.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only says a per-head budget precomputed offline on pretraining text shows competitive performance with methods that recompute the budget on every input.
FvXof9xMtt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the 60+ model census with controls is substantial and clearly presented, and that the head-wise budget improves over AdaKV under the same token scorer.
FvXof9xMtt.main_concern: Novelty is not clearly separated from prior cross-model attention similarity and offline head allocation work (KVzip, LU-KV), and the Jacobian theory is not validated under its assumptions.

Wi7sZS9CBQ.one_liner: Closes a gist-token span at every fixed increment of cumulative attention-based information gain, rather than every fixed token count.
Wi7sZS9CBQ.problem: Latent memory compression for long-horizon agents compresses at a uniform rate, splitting multi-token facts across gist tokens and giving fillers an equal share of the budget.
Wi7sZS9CBQ.method: Casting compression as a rate-distortion problem, they show equal-information-gain spans minimize distortion if span distortion is a convex function of gain. Gain is measured through a retrieval head, where a token is informative if it shifts attention away from its predecessor's focus onto itself, and IncreMem ends a span at each fixed gain increment.
Wi7sZS9CBQ.key_idea: Segment history into gist-token spans of equal retrieval-head attention-shift gain, so each gist token carries equal information instead of equal token count.
Wi7sZS9CBQ.evidence: Three long-context benchmarks (including LongMemEval and BEAM per reviews) and three backbones, against uniform gist compression and KV eviction, with segmentation ablations.
Wi7sZS9CBQ.claimed_gains: Loses virtually no accuracy at half the memory of the uncompressed backbone and outperforms uniform gist compression and KV eviction in nearly every setting; no further figures are visible in the abstract.
Wi7sZS9CBQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled segmentation ablations show gain-aligned boundaries beat equal-length spans, and the information-theoretic framing motivates content-aware memory allocation.
Wi7sZS9CBQ.main_concern: The rate-distortion optimality assumes span distortion depends only on gain, the attention-based gain is a heuristic proxy, and baselines (AdmTree, RAG, Beacon training confounds) are not tightly controlled.

UjLT8kHce8.one_liner: Proves graph-transformer attention decomposes into primal and dual atoms, and derives reconstruction-risk advantages over fixed GCN filters.
UjLT8kHce8.problem: The source of graph transformers' feature-extraction advantage over fixed topology-driven aggregation is unclear.
UjLT8kHce8.method: Shows linearized graph-transformer attention admits an exact finite primal-dual decomposition (key-induced primal atoms analyze the input, query-induced dual atoms synthesize the output), extends it to masked softmax attention, and shows that removing feature dependence yields a fixed linear graph filter with GCN as a special case. It then builds reconstruction networks converging to group-sparse minimizers and derives lower bounds on the reconstruction-risk advantage via a ridge surrogate.
UjLT8kHce8.key_idea: Decompose attention into key-induced primal atoms and query-induced dual atoms, so fixed-filter GCNs are the special case where query-key coordinates lose feature dependence.
UjLT8kHce8.evidence: Theoretical proofs plus controlled synthetic experiments, each mapped to a theoretical component (per reviews).
UjLT8kHce8.claimed_gains: Explicit lower bounds on the reconstruction-risk advantage of adaptive GT-inspired filters over fixed GCN-type filters; no numbers stated.
UjLT8kHce8.reviewer_consensus: Most reviewers value the exact operator decompositions, the containment of fixed filters in the adaptive family, and the close link between theory and controlled experiments.
UjLT8kHce8.main_concern: The risk bounds are oracle-style (spectra chosen from the clean signal) and the synthetic experiments give limited evidence for broader feature-extraction implications; one reviewer found the motivation weak.

ACYrnIY5MU.one_liner: Agentic automata learning tests whether LLM agents can recover a hidden DFA through membership and equivalence queries to an oracle.
ACYrnIY5MU.problem: It is unclear whether tool-calling LLM agents can uncover a hidden environment through interaction, a capability needed in agentic tasks.
ACYrnIY5MU.method: An agent must identify a hidden deterministic finite automaton by sending membership and equivalence queries to an oracle. Task complexity is controlled by DFA size, and interaction efficiency is compared against classic automata-learning algorithms.
ACYrnIY5MU.key_idea: Use active automata learning with procedurally generated DFAs as a controlled agent testbed, with L* and TTT query budgets as efficiency references.
ACYrnIY5MU.evidence: State-of-the-art LLMs with a multi-turn scaffold and a ReAct-style state-tracking scaffold, plus trajectory analyses and a coding-environment test (OpenHands per a review).
ACYrnIY5MU.claimed_gains: No gains stated; LLMs recover simple DFAs but performance drops sharply as DFA size increases, and the ReAct-style scaffold helps but strong models still struggle.
ACYrnIY5MU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the testbed is well posed, scalable and provably solvable, with precise definitions of complexity, success and interaction efficiency.
ACYrnIY5MU.main_concern: The setting is narrow (binary-alphabet deterministic DFAs with ideal oracles), which limits generalization and makes the broad term agentic automata learning too ambitious.

tEGsIB9xna.one_liner: AG-FORGE synthesizes anomalous graphs to train TS-GGAD, a generalist graph anomaly detector combining topology and semantic evidence with curriculum learning.
tEGsIB9xna.problem: Generalist graph anomaly detection lacks training data because real anomalous graphs are scarce and costly to collect and annotate.
tEGsIB9xna.method: AG-FORGE automatically generates anomalous graphs for training. TS-GGAD captures complementary topological and semantic anomaly evidence and is trained with a curriculum strategy for large-scale synthetic data.
tEGsIB9xna.key_idea: Train a generalist graph anomaly detector entirely on generated anomalous graphs, with a model that jointly models topology and semantic anomaly signals under a difficulty-based curriculum.
tEGsIB9xna.evidence: Experiments on 14 real-world datasets with ablations; training on synthetic data is compared with training on real-world data.
tEGsIB9xna.claimed_gains: Synthetic training reaches performance comparable to real-world training, and TS-GGAD trained on AG-FORGE data consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on 14 real-world datasets; no numbers stated.
tEGsIB9xna.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that synthetic training for generalist GAD is a practical idea and that TS-GGAD achieves the highest AUROC across all 14 datasets, with ablations supporting its components.
tEGsIB9xna.main_concern: The synthetic-versus-real comparison is not controlled because training sets differ greatly in size, and the paper does not explain why synthetic training hurts some methods on some datasets.

p6BV8mTYj3.one_liner: Video pretraining with one encoder, global-local view invariance, and SIGReg anti-collapse, using random token dropping to cut compute.
p6BV8mTYj3.problem: Self-supervised video pretraining is computationally expensive, and current methods prevent collapse with EMA target encoders, stop-gradients, and predictors, or with pixel-space reconstruction and a decoder.
p6BV8mTYj3.method: LeVJEPA extends LeJEPA to video: a single encoder is trained with an invariance loss between global and local views of a clip, SIGReg prevents collapse, and no target encoder, predictor, or pixel reconstruction is used. Pretraining cost depends only on the number of observed tokens, so tokens are dropped uniformly at random, and the encoder can also use block-causal attention.
p6BV8mTYj3.key_idea: Replace asymmetric teacher-predictor machinery with a single encoder trained on global-local view invariance plus SIGReg, then drop tokens at random to reduce cost.
p6BV8mTYj3.evidence: Matched-epoch and matched-FLOP comparisons against V-JEPA 2 and other video baselines on ViT-S/B/L with ImageNet-1K, K400, and SSv2 results, plus a consumer-GPU experiment and ablations on token dropping, tokenization, and attention.
p6BV8mTYj3.claimed_gains: At matched epochs LeVJEPA matches or outperforms V-JEPA 2 across ViT-S/B/L with 5.6 to 20.8× less pretraining compute, and at matched FLOPs it exceeds the strongest video baseline by 7.6 points on ImageNet-1K.
p6BV8mTYj3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the single-encoder recipe is simple and removes training overhead, with epoch- and FLOP-matched baseline comparisons and a consumer-GPU experiment giving practical value.
p6BV8mTYj3.main_concern: Reviewers say the objective is inherited from LeJEPA so the video-specific contribution is not isolated, conclusions lean on ImageNet while SSv2 lags (40.4 versus 43.6 for VideoMAEv2), and dense-prediction evidence is only qualitative.

cYit73MIIL.one_liner: Compiles a single agent execution record into a reusable task with an unsolved initial state and an evaluator.
cYit73MIIL.problem: Reusable executable tasks for evaluation and supervision are costly to build from execution records, which give only partial evidence about task inputs and completion conditions mixed with one solver's results.
cYit73MIIL.method: ReTask infers a task specification from the actionable request and initial-state evidence, then builds an unsolved initial state for a new solver and an evaluator for its outcome. Artifacts and outcomes from the recorded run may identify content to withhold or provide validation cases for the evaluator, but never define task requirements or reach the new solver.
cYit73MIIL.key_idea: Freeze one inferred task specification shared by state construction and evaluator, and use recorded outputs only for withholding and validation, never as task requirements.
cYit73MIIL.evidence: Comparative evaluation on 100 paired Workspace-Bench tasks across seven agent configurations, and supervision experiments where new patches are checked against original repository tests (SWE-ReBench per reviewers).
cYit73MIIL.claimed_gains: Native and Compiled aggregate rankings agree on 20 of 21 pairwise orders among seven agent configurations on 100 paired Workspace-Bench tasks (ρ=0.964), and 2,040 new patches pass the original repository tests.
cYit73MIIL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reactivating static execution records as executable tasks is practically useful and that the paper tests both evaluation and supervision uses, including an external check from repository tests.
cYit73MIIL.main_concern: Reviewers say there are no baselines or ablations (for example against Terminal-Universe-style reconstruction or simply prompting a strong model), and evaluator correctness is not validated beyond ranking agreement, with no human audit.

OgcFbxj8Ko.one_liner: Scales transformer neural rendering with hierarchical attention reweighted by represented surface area as a quadrature weight.
OgcFbxj8Ko.problem: Dense attention limits the scalability of transformer neural renderers, and attention depends on triangle-token count, so tessellation changes predictions even when geometry is unchanged.
OgcFbxj8Ko.method: TriRender is a two-stage rendering pipeline that weights triangles and coarse cluster tokens by surface area as a common measure, uses a spatially cohesive 3D hierarchy, and regenerates coarse tokens from constituent triangle features at each layer.
OgcFbxj8Ko.key_idea: Use represented surface area as a quadrature weight in attention so triangles and clusters share a measure across discretizations and hierarchy levels.
OgcFbxj8Ko.evidence: Ablations of the reweighting and generalization to scenes up to 1 million triangles after training on 4k to 10k triangles (per reviews); the abstract is truncated before results.
OgcFbxj8Ko.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree surface-area reweighting is a simple, coherent idea that addresses tessellation dependence and, with hierarchical attention, generalizes to much larger scenes with a large speedup.
OgcFbxj8Ko.main_concern: Reviewers say comparisons are missing or unfair: no quantitative comparison to RenderFormer baselines or simulators, dense-attention timing may not use optimized backends, and fine-tuning on 125k scenes is not matched for baselines.

gMH3HlPBhO.one_liner: Graph layer where each node's SPD matrix is also its local metric and evolves under a matrix-valued Ricci-type flow.
gMH3HlPBhO.problem: Existing graph Ricci flows evolve scalar edge lengths or weights rather than the node representations themselves.
gMH3HlPBhO.method: Each node holds an SPD representation that doubles as its metric. A matrix-valued Ricci-type curvature operator built from AIRM discrepancies between neighboring SPD metrics drives node-wise metric evolution, which is the representation update. The authors prove continuous-time energy dissipation and a link to the principal part of Ricci-DeTurck evolution.
gMH3HlPBhO.key_idea: Make curvature-driven evolution of node-wise SPD metric tensors the representation update, using a curvature operator built from AIRM discrepancies between neighboring nodes.
gMH3HlPBhO.evidence: Node classification, molecular property prediction and financial spillover prediction with ablations on graph propagation and matrix-valued updates, plus theory for continuous-time dissipation.
gMH3HlPBhO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation of SPD node states as local metrics is coherent, and the theory (energy dissipation) and experiments across several applications support metric evolution as an update mechanism.
gMH3HlPBhO.main_concern: The Ricci framing adds little beyond a Dirichlet-energy gradient flow (a smoothing operator), the proofs concern the idealized continuous flow rather than the implemented layer, and gains over strong baselines are small.

oFobMG1OKo.one_liner: Theory of when stochastic Muon preconditions beyond learning-rate rescaling, via structured mini-batch noise in associative memory with heterogeneous task frequencies.
oFobMG1OKo.problem: Muon is widely used for LLM training, but its theoretical benefits under stochastic gradient noise, and when they vanish, are poorly understood.
oFobMG1OKo.method: The paper shows that under isotropic noise Muon is only a learning-rate rescaling, then analyzes structured mini-batch noise in an associative-memory model with heterogeneous task frequencies, deriving an exact two-task balancing threshold, a multi-task extension, and the role of momentum.
oFobMG1OKo.key_idea: Muon's update depends on whether a rare task appears in the batch rather than on its count, softening dependence on task frequency from linear to square-root.
oFobMG1OKo.evidence: Theory plus controlled numerical experiments in synthetic associative-memory settings and a preliminary 0.12B-parameter LLM pretraining comparison with a single run per method.
oFobMG1OKo.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; a review cites final validation losses of 3.0097 for standard Muon and 2.9888 for fast-slow momentum in the 0.12B run.
oFobMG1OKo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is rigorous and well scoped, with an exact two-task threshold that gives an intuitive mechanism for how Muon balances frequent and rare tasks.
oFobMG1OKo.main_concern: Results rely on simplified associative-memory models with orthogonal embeddings, and the practical validation (a single-seed 0.12B run) does not test the theory's predictions.

unBGZ9VhrG.one_liner: Diagnoses why oracle fusion weights are hard to learn; a second verifier judges only candidates some weight can rank first.
unBGZ9VhrG.problem: Retrieval fuses a fast retriever's score with a verifier's score and the best fusion weight varies per query, yet learned weight-prediction policies capture almost none of the oracle headroom.
unBGZ9VhrG.method: Two exact identities explain headroom (the share of queries whose successful-weight interval excludes the constant) and net gain (rescued failures minus harmed successes). The winner-path duel (WPD) then asks a second verifier about only the candidates that some weight can rank first.
unBGZ9VhrG.key_idea: Per-query successful fusion weights form a computable interval for R@1, so policies gain only by rescuing failures without harming successes; knowing which candidate is the target is the bottleneck.
unBGZ9VhrG.evidence: 21 vision-language verifier configurations on CIRR and FashionIQ and five BEIR text datasets, with a label-derived hint control and equal-tuning-budget comparisons.
unBGZ9VhrG.claimed_gains: Choosing the best of 21 weights per CIRR query adds 10.2-12.2 R@1 points over a tuned constant weight versus 0.32 for a ridge policy; a label-derived hint recovers a median 89% of headroom; WPD uses 1.6-2.0 calls per query.
unBGZ9VhrG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the headroom, rescue and harm analysis is insightful and carefully controlled, and the experiments are broad across 21 verifier configurations and image and text retrieval.
unBGZ9VhrG.main_concern: The conclusion that the remaining gap is an information gap is stronger than the evidence, the scope is limited to fixed retrievers, top-20 lists and linear fusion, and the presentation is hard to follow.

fyms5YGRbj.one_liner: Selects informative views before any 3D reconstruction by estimating each candidate's marginal contribution from feed-forward visual and geometric features.
fyms5YGRbj.problem: Active view selection methods need a warm-up reconstruction before valuing views, which adds computation and is unreliable when few initial observations exist.
fyms5YGRbj.method: PreView extracts features with feed-forward visual and geometric priors and models interactions between candidate views and the selected set with a transformer-based selector to estimate marginal contribution, in RGB-aware or pose-only regimes, with optional region-of-interest preference conditioning.
fyms5YGRbj.key_idea: Value a candidate view by the new evidence it adds beyond already selected views, estimated from feed-forward features without building a warm-up 3D scene.
fyms5YGRbj.evidence: Controlled experiments on global versus regional reconstruction quality with 3D Gaussian Splatting, cross-dataset transfer and view-budget analyses against warm-up-based selectors and random selection.
fyms5YGRbj.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a review notes pose-only selection takes about 2 seconds versus about 486 seconds in the RGB-aware regime.
fyms5YGRbj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that avoiding warm-up reconstruction is a useful goal and that supporting RGB-aware and pose-only selection with ROI preference gives practical flexibility and lower selection cost.
fyms5YGRbj.main_concern: Baselines are insufficient: there is no comparison with simple reconstruction-free selectors (farthest-point, pose-diversity, greedy handcrafted utility) or with using all candidate views, so the value of the learned selector is unclear.

Cfk9GCYnn4.one_liner: Flow-map training with a standard diffusion backbone and a lightweight analytic head that handles terminal-time derivatives in closed form.
Cfk9GCYnn4.problem: Flow-map training requires differentiating the whole model with respect to time, which incurs severe overhead.
Cfk9GCYnn4.method: Plain flow maps keep the backbone standard and expose the differentiated time only to a single-layer head with time-adaptive spatial and channel mixing. Secant and velocity parameterizations let terminal-time derivatives and integrals be resolved analytically within the head.
Cfk9GCYnn4.key_idea: Move terminal-time dependence into a lightweight bilinear analytic head so derivatives and integrals are closed-form and no full-backbone JVP or finite differences are needed.
Cfk9GCYnn4.evidence: From-scratch ImageNet and text-to-image training, with motivating studies on terminal-time conditioning and comparisons to flow-map baselines (iMF and alpha-Flow appear in the appendix).
Cfk9GCYnn4.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (it claims strong ImageNet and text-to-image results without numbers); reviews cite 1/2-NFE FID of 2.89/2.40 for Plain-Secant.
Cfk9GCYnn4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is simple and elegant, the motivating studies justify moving terminal-time computation out of the backbone, and the analytic head avoids costly full-backbone differentiation.
Cfk9GCYnn4.main_concern: The main comparison table omits stronger baselines (iMF at 1.72/1.54 and alpha-Flow at 2.81/2.16 FID at 1/2 NFE) that appear only in the appendix, and flow-map composition consistency is not directly evaluated.

QXDBk5f4kY.one_liner: Generates renderable LiDAR Gaussian fields from surround-view images with a diffusion transformer latent and a ray-anchored Gaussian decoder.
QXDBk5f4kY.problem: LiDAR generation methods synthesize range, intensity, and ray-drop maps in image space without an explicit 3D representation, while Gaussian LiDAR reconstruction needs per-scene optimization with real LiDAR measurements.
QXDBk5f4kY.method: A diffusion transformer generates a latent conditioned on multi-view images, and a ray-anchored Gaussian decoder maps it to Gaussian primitives with geometric parameters, intensity attributes, and ray-drop probabilities. A panoramic Gaussian splatting renderer converts these into range, intensity, and ray-drop maps, and the same decoder also converts observed LiDAR feed-forward.
QXDBk5f4kY.key_idea: Decode a camera-conditioned diffusion latent into ray-anchored Gaussian primitives carrying intensity and ray-drop attributes, so generation and LiDAR reconstruction share one renderable 3D representation.
QXDBk5f4kY.evidence: nuScenes LiDAR generation against other generation methods on MMD and JSD, reconstruction baselines, ablations, a trajectory extrapolation test on one scene, and downstream use cases.
QXDBk5f4kY.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says LiFTeR achieves the best MMD and JSD among LiDAR generation methods on nuScenes before the text is cut off.
QXDBk5f4kY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pipeline is well motivated and technically sound, unifies camera-conditioned generation and feed-forward LiDAR reconstruction in one renderable representation, and has thorough ablations and downstream demonstrations.
QXDBk5f4kY.main_concern: The benefit of a reusable 3D field is shown on only one scene with limited motion, and the multi-frame field has no dynamic-object handling or cross-frame latent consistency.

H8S97moUKI.one_liner: Unlearns LLM content with a negative-order Rényi divergence loss on the forget set alone, treating unlearning as inverse continual learning.
H8S97moUKI.problem: Existing unlearning methods typically use off-policy objectives that push the model toward an idealized unlearning target, which leads to utility collapse.
H8S97moUKI.method: MARU uses the negative-order Rényi divergence as a mode-avoiding objective, since minimizing any positive-order Rényi divergence only attracts a model toward a target distribution. It is defined on the forget set alone and needs no retain data.
H8S97moUKI.key_idea: Use a negative-order Rényi divergence on the forget set so the model is repelled from the forget mode, as the inverse of reverse-KL continual learning.
H8S97moUKI.evidence: Experiments on the TOFU benchmark and a second benchmark across multiple model scales against a wide set of baselines, with ablations on the Rényi order.
H8S97moUKI.claimed_gains: MARU leads in forgetting on the hardest forget split (10%) at 1B scale on TOFU while delivering substantially better resistance to membership (the abstract is cut off).
H8S97moUKI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that viewing unlearning as inverse continual learning is a compelling perspective and that the retain-free negative-order Rényi objective is simple, with experiments across model scales, two benchmarks, and many baselines.
H8S97moUKI.main_concern: The implemented loss is a heuristic stand-in for the analyzed divergence with no result linking it to utility preservation, and utility drops notably in some settings (0.708 to 0.533 at 1B with a 10% forget split).

RNtTCzrnYF.one_liner: Synthesizes verified data-analysis tasks from raw data lakes by sampling subgraphs of a physical-semantic dual-view graph and instantiating analytical operators.
RNtTCzrnYF.problem: Real data lakes hold too many files to inspect individually and the files sharing a meaningful join path cannot be identified from local context, which makes grounded, verifiable data-analysis training tasks hard to produce at scale.
RNtTCzrnYF.method: DATA2TASK builds a physical-semantic dual-view graph of the data pool, samples a provenance-preserving subgraph, and instantiates a compatible analytical operator over it so the answer is computable from the sampled files. A staged pipeline turns each motif into a natural-language request with executable ground truth, kept only when independent solvers reproduce the answer.
RNtTCzrnYF.key_idea: Build a dual-view graph that surfaces cross-file relations, then instantiate an analytical operator over a sampled subgraph so each task's answer is grounded by construction.
RNtTCzrnYF.evidence: Fine-tuning Qwen3-8B on 2,000 verified tasks with selected solution trajectories, evaluated on four held-out data-analysis benchmarks including TableBench and DAEval, with a graph ablation and a comparison with DataMind.
RNtTCzrnYF.claimed_gains: With 2,000 verified tasks, fine-tuning Qwen3-8B achieves an average score of 55.17% across four held-out data-analysis benchmarks, outperforming the 29x larger Qwen3-235B and matching the 60x larger Qwen3-Coder-480B on TableBench.
RNtTCzrnYF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that discovering cross-file relations before task writing is practical and controllable, and that fine-tuning on 2,000 trajectories improves all four benchmarks.
RNtTCzrnYF.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed to the task design, since trajectories come from a much stronger teacher, the graph ablation covers only DAEval, and no other synthesis pipeline is compared under the same data, teacher, and budget.

qikkzGqjhO.one_liner: Trains tool-integrated reasoning policies with resource cost as a goal input, not a reward term, using task-aware relabeled cost targets.
qikkzGqjhO.problem: Efficient tool-integrated reasoning methods fold resource cost into the reward, so lower cost can be rewarded at the expense of task success, and refinements still keep both in one learning signal.
qikkzGqjhO.method: Drawing on goal-conditioned RL, task reward alone evaluates outcome while cost enters policy optimization as a goal input. From on-policy performance-cost outcomes it builds a task-aware target reference favoring lower cost, relabels achieved costs around it, and applies a goal-routed update, with sufficient conditions for local cost descent.
qikkzGqjhO.key_idea: Keep cost out of the reward: condition the policy on a cost goal relative to a task-dependent on-policy reference and relabel achieved costs around it.
qikkzGqjhO.evidence: Six mathematical-reasoning and knowledge-intensive benchmarks with Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B, compared with cost-in-reward baselines such as ET-Agent, with component ablations and repeated evaluation.
qikkzGqjhO.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims the strongest overall task performance and tool productivity across six benchmarks.
qikkzGqjhO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating cost goals from task rewards is a useful and distinct mechanism, with a good performance-efficiency trade-off supported by ablations.
qikkzGqjhO.main_concern: The claim that decoupling beats cost-in-reward is not isolated, since no matched baseline puts cost into the reward inside the identical pipeline.

F4nkNMPrps.one_liner: Generates structured editing instructions with explicit reference-to-entity bindings via SFT and GRPO, then trains a multi-reference video editor on them.
F4nkNMPrps.problem: Operation-centric instructions leave preservation requirements and content-source relationships underspecified, and even detailed instructions can tie entities or attributes to the wrong visual sources, giving inconsistent training supervision.
F4nkNMPrps.method: ReBind-Instruct generates reference-consistent instructions in two stages: Structured Instruction Learning by SFT and Reference Attribution Optimization by GRPO with content-level and relation-level rewards that penalize source assignment errors. The annotations supervise ReBind-Edit, which extends a pretrained text-to-video model with joint visual conditioning on the source video and reference images.
F4nkNMPrps.key_idea: Reward an instruction generator with GRPO for both content correctness and correct reference-source attribution, so annotations bind each edited entity to the right reference image.
F4nkNMPrps.evidence: Single-reference and multi-reference editing on IntelligentVBench and UniVBench, controlled ablations that corrupt source assignments, a same-data-and-budget comparison, and a human study with 15 participants on 50 cases.
F4nkNMPrps.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before any results are given.
F4nkNMPrps.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is well established and the paper is clear, with explicit entity-attribute-reference modeling addressing instruction ambiguity and controlled experiments showing better instruction supervision helps editing.
F4nkNMPrps.main_concern: Methodological novelty beyond the standard SFT plus GRPO recipe is not established, and it is unclear why lengthy ReBind instructions are needed over simpler explicit reference bindings.

XGEB8y8XOp.one_liner: Fuses latent semantic queries anchored to Gaussian geometry across agents for collaborative semantic occupancy, with selective packing and query compression.
XGEB8y8XOp.problem: Collaborative perception methods communicate dense bird's-eye-view or voxel features, which either collapse vertical geometry or incur the cost of dense 3D grids under constrained communication budgets.
XGEB8y8XOp.method: GaussianCollab communicates tokenized semantic Gaussians, doing geometry-guided matching and latent-query fusion over matched tokens and decoding and stacking unmatched collaborator evidence. Semantic InConsistency (SIC)-guided selective packing and Partially Embedded Query Compression (PEQC) control the payload.
