XGEB8y8XOp.key_idea: Exchange latent semantic queries anchored to explicit Gaussian geometry, match them geometrically for fusion, and pack tokens chosen by semantic inconsistency to limit payload.
XGEB8y8XOp.evidence: Semantic-OPV2V and Co3SOP collaborative semantic occupancy prediction against a reproduced VOGS-L baseline under matched Gaussian capacity and varying bandwidth, with ablations and pose-noise robustness tests.
XGEB8y8XOp.claimed_gains: Under matched Gaussian capacity, the lowest-communication-volume operating points improve mIoU over the reproduced VOGS-L baseline by 2.95 and 3.47 (the abstract is cut off after this).
XGEB8y8XOp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Gaussians as the communication medium are well motivated and give consistent improvements over existing methods, including under different bandwidth constraints, with SIC-guided selection helping communication efficiency.
XGEB8y8XOp.main_concern: The advantage of latent queries over decoded attributes is not isolated, since decoded-attribute protocols appear to reach similar communication volume and the no-stacking variant gains 1.03 mIoU at 4.58 times the payload.

f9ys7RS1iT.one_liner: Applies Personalized PageRank with sliding-window or exponential time decay to historical graphs as a training-free temporal link prediction baseline.
f9ys7RS1iT.problem: Temporal link prediction methods rely on learned temporal representations, and it is unclear how much they add beyond historical structural proximity.
f9ys7RS1iT.method: Runs Personalized PageRank (PPR) on historical interaction graphs, retaining history by a sliding window or exponential time decay, with only hyperparameter tuning and no learned parameters. It also analyses historical paths from source nodes to previously unseen destinations.
f9ys7RS1iT.key_idea: Score candidate destinations by Personalized PageRank over past interactions weighted by sliding-window retention or exponential time decay.
f9ys7RS1iT.evidence: Evaluated on 14 datasets against recent neural temporal link prediction baselines, with a path analysis of unseen destinations and a negative-sampling robustness check in the appendix.
f9ys7RS1iT.claimed_gains: Time-decay PPR ranks first on nine and second on four of 14 datasets among the compared methods.
f9ys7RS1iT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper asks a meaningful question about how much learned temporal modeling adds beyond historical structure, is easy to read, and backs its message with extensive evaluation on 14 datasets.
f9ys7RS1iT.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (PPR plus standard decay), and results depend on dataset-specific hyperparameter tuning and on how negative candidate sets are built.

wsrCbtVZqc.one_liner: Distills unlabeled agent trajectories into nested shortcut trees that give reusable retry feedback without rewards or correctness labels.
wsrCbtVZqc.problem: Online agent trajectories are abundant but noisy, and extracting reusable evidence normally needs costly manual annotation or verifier signals that do not scale.
wsrCbtVZqc.method: DENSE organizes trajectory evidence into nested shortcut trees by consolidating redundant attempts, identifying resolved subtasks, and keeping useful steps alongside outstanding requirements. The authors also design REFIT, which measures the success-rate change between an initial attempt and a feedback-guided retry.
wsrCbtVZqc.key_idea: Build nested subtask trees from raw trajectories that merge redundant attempts, mark resolved subtasks, and keep useful steps plus remaining requirements as retry feedback.
wsrCbtVZqc.evidence: Evaluated with the REFIT retry protocol on Terminal-Bench 2.1 across four agent models, with an ablation replacing nested analysis by a single holistic analysis.
wsrCbtVZqc.claimed_gains: Highest strict pass rate among feedback methods without external outcome supervision on Terminal-Bench 2.1, improving over initial attempts by 7.12–21.81 percentage points with 19.0–43.6% fewer agent tokens on retries.
wsrCbtVZqc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing unannotated agent trajectories is a practical problem and that the full pipeline gains across several agent models under a reasonably controlled evaluation.
wsrCbtVZqc.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate the nested tree structure from summarization and extra analysis computation, so its added value over flat or sequential organization is unproven.

yItsSosC14.one_liner: Organizes ML trial histories by algorithmic direction so an agentic controller inspects evidence before choosing operations and source implementations.
yItsSosC14.problem: In budget-limited AI-train-AI loops, source selection relies on scalar scores and meta signals, while the supporting trial evidence is only partly used in experiment design.
yItsSosC14.method: The outer loop records successful and failed trials, deterministically groups implementations by algorithmic direction, and links modification intents to outcomes. The inner policy, Operation-aware Evidence Control (OEC), uses compact direction cards and operation-level meta signals to decide which histories and code to inspect, and can revise operations, sources and plans before commitment.
yItsSosC14.key_idea: An inner agentic policy inspects direction cards and trial code on demand to jointly pick operation, source and modification plan, revisable before execution.
yItsSosC14.evidence: Evaluated on MLE-Lite with three backbones and on NatureBench Lite, with a routing ablation and accounting for planning overhead.
yItsSosC14.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coupling evidence inspection with joint selection of operations, sources and modification plans is a useful mechanism, with the highest mean Human Rank on MLE-Lite across three backbones.
yItsSosC14.main_concern: Gains are hard to attribute to evidence inspection because hand-written guardrails and a broader action set in the routing ablation differ from baselines, and the framing overlaps prior work.

uYjLYizjmx.one_liner: Replaces on-device MoE expert computation with a semantic-conditioned lookup table of precomputed outputs plus compression, fused retrieval and prefetching.
uYjLYizjmx.problem: On-device MoE inference stays computation-centric, and token-indexed lookup schemes limit retrieval expressiveness while shifting the bottleneck to storage, fragmented execution and data movement.
uYjLYizjmx.method: RcMoE builds a semantic-conditioned lookup table (SC-LUT) of precomputed expert outputs, then adds SC-LUT compression, a fused retrieval kernel and asynchronous prefetching. Reviews note the conditions are bigram and trigram patterns and that NF4 quantization is used.
uYjLYizjmx.key_idea: Index precomputed expert outputs by local multi-token context (bigram and trigram patterns) rather than single tokens, stored as differences from single-token outputs.
uYjLYizjmx.evidence: Experiments on commodity edge devices compare against D2MoE and MoLE, with ablations over model quality, storage footprint and inference speed.
uYjLYizjmx.claimed_gains: Up to 31.1x the throughput of D2MoE while maintaining competitive accuracy under edge resource constraints.
uYjLYizjmx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the retrieval-centric design is technically coherent, extends token-only lookup with local context, and is supported by a fairly complete system implementation with ablations on quality, storage and speed.
uYjLYizjmx.main_concern: The SC-LUT still needs large external storage (9.93 GB and 6.81 GB for the two models), fixed bigram/trigram contexts may not generalize, and the MoLE comparison is not under matched optimizations.

8Qq6keQnjG.one_liner: Introduces TouchBench for tactile question answering and TouchAgent, a tool-using MLLM agent trained with SFT and reinforcement learning.
8Qq6keQnjG.problem: Tactile intelligence in multimodal LLMs is held back by heterogeneous sensor modalities, diverse domain knowledge and a fragmented task landscape.
8Qq6keQnjG.method: TouchBench has 10K questions and about 383K observation frames across 6 tactile task categories. TouchAgent integrates knowledge retrieval, perception and reasoning through domain-specific tactile models and tools, and is trained on 40K multi-round trajectories (TouchAgent-Instruct) with supervised fine-tuning and RL.
8Qq6keQnjG.key_idea: Train an MLLM controller on multi-round tool-use trajectories with SFT then RL to plan calls to tactile perception models and knowledge retrieval.
8Qq6keQnjG.evidence: Evaluates 24 open-source, proprietary and tactile-language models on TouchBench, plus training-stage and tool-component ablations and a fixed-pipeline comparison added after author response.
8Qq6keQnjG.claimed_gains: The visible abstract gives no TouchAgent performance numbers; a reviewer cites accuracy rising from 66.2% to 76.1% through controller training.
8Qq6keQnjG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree TouchBench is a substantial curation effort covering diverse sensors and tasks, and that the tool-augmented system shows consistent gains with useful ablations.
8Qq6keQnjG.main_concern: Novelty is limited (existing tool-calling, SFT and GRPO), baselines lack the same tactile tools, and benchmark independence from tool-training data and reward bias toward reference tool routes are not fully settled.

K3BkYo314r.one_liner: Trains an LLM orchestrator by midtraining on synthetic exploration trajectories then multi-turn RL to delegate diverse directions to parallel executors.
K3BkYo314r.problem: Chain-of-thought exploration contracts as reasoning proceeds, with less compute spent on new directions, and current LLMs orchestrate exploration poorly through redundant delegation and premature termination.
K3BkYo314r.method: LoRE first midtrains a model on synthetic exploration trajectories to set orchestration priors, then applies multi-turn RL inside an orchestrator-executor harness. The orchestrator decides which directions to explore and delegates them to parallel execution models.
K3BkYo314r.key_idea: Train the orchestrator itself, via synthetic-trajectory midtraining plus multi-turn RL, to decide which directions get test-time compute instead of reasoning inside its own trajectory.
K3BkYo314r.evidence: Analysis of exploration contraction with semantic-level annotations and token-level statistics, plus benchmark comparisons against reasoning harnesses and standard training, and a breadth ablation.
K3BkYo314r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exploration-contraction analysis is well motivated and that LoRE improves performance across several challenging benchmarks.
K3BkYo314r.main_concern: It is unclear whether gains come from greater exploration diversity or from extra test-time compute, and novelty over prior orchestration methods such as APR and ParaManager is not firmly established.

U91NratIpT.one_liner: Foveal-LC learns to combine cheap proxy signals from reference judgments, guiding search and certifying corpus-level decisions with anytime-valid error control.
U91NratIpT.problem: Judging every record in a large corpus with an LLM is costly, while relying only on cheap signals risks drawing the wrong overall conclusion.
U91NratIpT.method: Each acquired reference judgment both contributes to the decision and helps learn how to combine the cheaper signals for future judgments. Reviews describe the construction as variance reduction combined with sequential betting and e-processes for finite-sample decision-error control.
U91NratIpT.key_idea: Learn the proxy combination online from each acquired reference label, using it for variance reduction inside sequential betting (e-process) tests that certify stopping.
U91NratIpT.evidence: Theory (error control, learning-overhead and label-cost bounds) plus experiments with held-out evaluation; reviewers note the empirical validation is on tabular data, not LLM workflows.
U91NratIpT.claimed_gains: On held-out data, learning separate weights for the signals saves 3.0% and 4.6% of judgments compared with learning one weight for their average.
U91NratIpT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well defined and the theory is solid, giving finite-sample decision-error control that holds regardless of proxy quality.
U91NratIpT.main_concern: Evidence is limited: validation is on tabular data rather than LLM workflows, gains are modest, and the strongest cost guarantees do not cover the best-performing DEFAULT policy.

UjJscQaOAj.one_liner: SyncNet separates module content from a learned Kuramoto phase state, letting phase alignment gate communication between modules.
UjJscQaOAj.problem: Modular networks do not guarantee that reusable roles develop, and unrestricted communication between modules can undermine whatever specialisation emerges.
UjJscQaOAj.method: SyncNet keeps module content separate from a dynamical phase state. Learnt Kuramoto dynamics evolve the phases, and phase alignment determines communication through a shared channel.
UjJscQaOAj.key_idea: Learned Kuramoto dynamics evolve per-module phases, and phase alignment sets which modules communicate through a shared channel.
UjJscQaOAj.evidence: Evaluated on Sort-of-CLEVR (relational reasoning) and SQOOP (systematic generalisation at varying pair variety), with addressing ablations and test-time phase overrides.
UjJscQaOAj.claimed_gains: Best held-out accuracy of the compared models at the three lowest SQOOP pair varieties, by 5.1 percentage points at the hardest, and competitive on Sort-of-CLEVR though below the strongest attention baselines.
UjJscQaOAj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and tests its own hypothesis through systematic ablations, concluding that stable modular decomposition matters more than synchrony itself.
UjJscQaOAj.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to two small synthetic benchmarks with no scalability evidence, model and training details are too thin to replicate, and Sort-of-CLEVR results trail FiLM, Transformer and Shared Workspace baselines.

LVhtPhBHbt.one_liner: Training-free hybrid linear attention caches Gated DeltaNet chunk summaries and retrieves them by camera geometry for long-horizon video world models.
LVhtPhBHbt.problem: Gated DeltaNet forgets distant but relevant scenes because later state updates attenuate them, hurting scene consistency over long video rollouts.
LVhtPhBHbt.method: HLA-WM exploits the affine structure of GDN to cache compact chunk-wise transition summaries, retrieves scene-relevant historical chunks using camera geometry, and recomposes them into query-specific recurrent states. It requires no additional training.
LVhtPhBHbt.key_idea: Because the GDN update is affine in the state, cache per-chunk transition summaries and recompose camera-geometry-selected chunks into a query-specific recurrent state.
LVhtPhBHbt.evidence: Evaluated on the 60-second SANA-WM-Bench and on MBench-A (four subsets, all evaluated inference modes), including after downstream refinement, with an ablation separating GDN recomposition from KV selection.
LVhtPhBHbt.claimed_gains: On the 60-second SANA-WM-Bench, improves all six aggregate revisit-consistency and camera-control metrics of the base generator, including a 0.74 dB PSNR gain and a 28.5% reduction in rotation error.
LVhtPhBHbt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and training-free, clearly diagnoses long-range forgetting in GDN, and reuses available camera poses at little throughput cost.
LVhtPhBHbt.main_concern: Quantitative gains are small at very low fidelity, much of the camera improvement comes from the KV path rather than GDN recomposition, and comparisons with memory methods such as WorldMem and Context-as-Memory are missing.

TC0a1LlZXH.one_liner: Extends detect-and-switch to bandits under global differential privacy: private successive elimination, stochasticity tests, and a private adversarial fallback.
TC0a1LlZXH.problem: Private best-of-both-worlds bandit algorithms exist separately for stochastic and adversarial settings, but none achieves both at once under global differential privacy.
TC0a1LlZXH.method: PrivDaS combines private successive elimination with tests for consistency with stochastic losses, keeps sampling and monitoring eliminated arms, and switches to a private adversarial algorithm when a test fails. The construction controls privacy cost across elimination, monitoring and switching.
TC0a1LlZXH.key_idea: Private successive elimination runs alongside private consistency tests on eliminated arms, and a failed test triggers a switch to a private adversarial algorithm.
TC0a1LlZXH.evidence: Regret analysis under pure global epsilon-DP for stochastic and oblivious-adversarial environments, plus experiments on four synthetic settings with epsilon fixed at 1/512.
TC0a1LlZXH.claimed_gains: Expected regret O((log^2 T) sqrt(KT/epsilon) + 1/epsilon) against oblivious adversaries and O(sum over i with Delta_i>0 of (log T)(1+log(1/Delta_i)) / min{Delta_i, epsilon}) in stochastic environments.
TC0a1LlZXH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a solid theoretical contribution that moves best-of-both-worlds private bandits from local to global DP with regret guarantees in both environments.
TC0a1LlZXH.main_concern: Experiments are limited to four synthetic settings at one strong-privacy budget (epsilon = 1/512), and the technical novelty over combining existing private mechanisms is not clearly separated.

hwlfWFU20v.one_liner: Combines MARS-style variance-reduced gradient correction with Muon's matrix preconditioning, with an exact method and a cheaper approximation.
hwlfWFU20v.problem: Muon lacks variance reduction, which benchmarks show can substantially speed up LLM pretraining, and its established convergence rate is only O~(T^-1/4).
hwlfWFU20v.method: MARS-M adds MARS-style same-sample gradient-difference correction to Muon. For the exact form it proves an O~(T^-1/3) rate under stated assumptions, and an approximation separately controls momentum memory and gradient-difference contributions with Nesterov look-ahead.
hwlfWFU20v.key_idea: Add a MARS-style gradient-difference correction, scaled by a coefficient gamma, to Muon's momentum buffer before matrix orthogonalization.
hwlfWFU20v.evidence: Convergence theorem for the exact method, plus language-modeling experiments (GPT-2 models from 125M to 1.5B, two datasets, 3-seed repeats) and computer vision experiments against Moonlight.
hwlfWFU20v.claimed_gains: An O~(T^-1/3) convergence rate for the exact formulation versus the previously established O~(T^-1/4) for Muon, and more effective optimization than Moonlight with no numbers given in the abstract.
hwlfWFU20v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the language-model gains over a tuned Moonlight baseline are small but consistent across model sizes and datasets at negligible cost, and the approximate variant is clearly derived.
hwlfWFU20v.main_concern: Gains may not come from variance reduction, since approximate MARS-M reduces to Moonlight at a particular gamma, and the headline theory covers only the exact method rather than the evaluated approximation.

Y8wsZl1c4s.one_liner: SCAD splits agents into planning and bounded subtask execution, using local-context distillation and cross-rollout prefix-tree credit to train long-horizon agents.
Y8wsZl1c4s.problem: Sparse terminal rewards obscure intermediate contributions in long-horizon agent training, and on-policy distillation loses informative teacher guidance as student histories grow.
Y8wsZl1c4s.method: SCAD organizes interactions into planning and bounded subtask execution, distills execution in local contexts, and refines planning credit through cross-rollout subtask prefix trees. Planning receives full terminal credit, while execution receives positive terminal credit plus teacher guidance.
Y8wsZl1c4s.key_idea: Score worker tokens with the teacher inside bounded local subtask contexts and assign planner credit from cross-rollout subtask prefix trees, with role-specific reward signals.
Y8wsZl1c4s.evidence: 19 text and multimodal benchmarks against RL, on-policy distillation and hybrid baselines, with component ablations, a stronger-teacher setting, and transfer to ALFWorld, WebShop and AppWorld.
Y8wsZl1c4s.claimed_gains: Improves macro-average accuracy over the strongest training baseline by 4.48 percentage points on text tasks and 4.19 points on multimodal tasks.
Y8wsZl1c4s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad (19 environments) and the local-context distillation finding is well supported, with three challenges mapped clearly to three design components.
Y8wsZl1c4s.main_concern: Most of the gain comes from local distillation, while prefix-tree credit and role allocation add 1.1–2.1 points within seed noise, and novelty over existing Plan-and-Execute, OPD and credit-assignment work is limited.

t6Bf16ReBA.one_liner: Values concept groups by how much of the model's local gradient they span, then allocates credit via Shapley values.
t6Bf16ReBA.problem: Scoring concepts one at a time overcounts when concepts overlap, because each is credited with the shared sensitivity and the scores sum to no meaningful total.
t6Bf16ReBA.method: SPACE values a concept group by the part of the model's local gradient its concept vectors can express, giving a closed-form coverage score, a non-negative Shapley allocation that sums exactly to coverage, and greedy subset selection with a worst-case guarantee. It needs one gradient and one factorisation, with no masked inputs.
t6Bf16ReBA.key_idea: Define the game value of a concept set as the norm of the local gradient's projection onto the span of its concept vectors, then take Shapley values.
t6Bf16ReBA.evidence: ImageNet experiments with a ResNet50 and fifteen texture and colour concepts, extended to refitted concepts, all 1,000 classes and a vision transformer, plus a synthetic benchmark.
t6Bf16ReBA.claimed_gains: The three concepts with the largest shares keep 76% of what all fifteen reach, against 67% for the top three one-at-a-time scores, and selection comes within one point of the best possible three.
t6Bf16ReBA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation is mathematically coherent and intuitive, handles overlapping concept directions, and is compared usefully against independent ranking and optimal selection.
t6Bf16ReBA.main_concern: Exact Shapley computation scales as O(2^K K^3), so it is practical only for small concept vocabularies, and concept-vector quality and explanation quality are thinly validated.

Jg4AtJ6TNy.one_liner: Trains a jailbreak investigator against a curriculum of target-model variants whose refusals are progressively restored, ending at the original target.
Jg4AtJ6TNy.problem: Training an RL investigator directly against a safety-trained target gives sparse reward because most prompts are refused.
Jg4AtJ6TNy.method: CoM trains the investigator against a sequence of modified target versions from which the behavior is progressively harder to elicit, starting with one that rarely refuses. Training advances once the investigator succeeds on the current version; reviews describe the curriculum as linear interpolation of an anti-refusal LoRA weight.
Jg4AtJ6TNy.key_idea: Interpolate an anti-refusal LoRA's strength on the target model and advance to a harder, less weakened target once the investigator elicits the behavior.
Jg4AtJ6TNy.evidence: Single- and multi-behavior elicitation tasks on CBRN materials, explosives and illicit drugs with two target models, compared with PRBO and a black-box baseline, plus hyperparameter ablations.
Jg4AtJ6TNy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is clear and well motivated, with an anti-refusal LoRA curriculum that addresses sparse reward and ablations of each hyperparameter.
Jg4AtJ6TNy.main_concern: CoM is outperformed by PRBO in multi-behavior experiments and roughly matches a black-box baseline on GPT-OSS-120B, with a narrow evaluation (one investigator, two targets, high seed variance) and limited novelty over easy-to-hard curricula.

jQDbBMncVh.one_liner: Gates imagined multi-agent experience by world-model fidelity, sending reliable rollouts to agent training and unreliable ones to world-model repair.
jQDbBMncVh.problem: In imagination-based multi-agent RL, a high-learning-signal trajectory may reflect a real policy weakness or merely world-model error, so a curriculum that ignores fidelity can reinforce model errors.
jQDbBMncVh.method: PROWL-2 keeps two curricula, one for task agents and one for finding and repairing world-model failures. It scores imagined experience on learning potential and fidelity against the real environment, promotes reliable informative rollouts to the agent curriculum, sends unreliable ones to repair, and uses a developer policy to search for further model failures.
jQDbBMncVh.key_idea: Gate imagined rollouts by realized world-model error against the real environment before they enter the agent curriculum, routing failures to a separate world-model repair curriculum.
jQDbBMncVh.evidence: Cooperative tasks in SMACv2 and the Multi-Agent Quadruped Environment (MQE) against strong baselines including the MARIE backbone, with ablations of the gate, curricula and developer policy.
jQDbBMncVh.claimed_gains: The visible abstract says PROWL-2 consistently outperforms strong baselines without giving numbers; a reviewer cites improvements of 20–40% on challenging MQE tasks.
jQDbBMncVh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fidelity gate is a simple, well-motivated fix to a real confound between learning potential and world-model error, supported by extensive experiments on SMACv2 and MQE.
jQDbBMncVh.main_concern: The developer policy's necessity and cost are not isolated, since the lightweight fidelity gate accounts for almost all of the gain while the developer doubles GPU-hours and adds uncharged real-environment interactions.

fpo2KEAUhH.one_liner: Clusters vocabulary-level patterns in logit-lens and J-lens readouts to recover unsupervised concepts that express an LLM's judgement of factual claims.
fpo2KEAUhH.problem: Supervised probes for an LLM's internal judgement need labelled data and training for each setting, and internal judgements can diverge from verbalised responses.
fpo2KEAUhH.method: An unsupervised method clusters vocabulary-level patterns in lens readouts into token-group concepts for true, false or uncertain judgements, and derives a training-free signal from them. A topic-modelling analysis tracks how truth, falsity and misconception patterns develop across layers and instruction tuning.
fpo2KEAUhH.key_idea: Cluster lens-readout token patterns into concept directions, then swap those directions to flip verdicts and read them out as a training-free belief signal.
fpo2KEAUhH.evidence: Experiments across several model families, prompt styles and datasets, with intervention controls (random directions, polarity swaps, answer-word removal), ablations, and a base versus instruct analysis.
fpo2KEAUhH.claimed_gains: The training-free signal approaches supervised linear probes and stays comparatively stable under a user's conflicting belief; no numbers are stated.
fpo2KEAUhH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is intuitive and that the intervention experiments, with random-direction and polarity-swap controls, give credible causal evidence across prompts, layers and model families.
fpo2KEAUhH.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (it builds on J-lens, PCA and HDBSCAN), the unsupervised signal still trails supervised probes, and interventions do not show whether they change belief or only response tendency.

Yk4LNGEnIo.one_liner: Maintains a budget-constrained GPU cache of LM-head rows across dialogue turns, selecting rows by token prevalence, query relevance and residency.
Yk4LNGEnIo.problem: In multi-turn small-model inference the vocabulary-dependent LM-head is a memory and data-movement bottleneck, and existing vocabulary-reduction methods treat queries independently, missing cross-turn reuse.
Yk4LNGEnIo.method: SLMCoach selectively retains LM-head rows with high reuse potential and incrementally updates a budget-constrained cache across consecutive queries. The selection policy scores token prevalence, current-query relevance and GPU residency.
Yk4LNGEnIo.key_idea: Keep LM-head rows likely to be reused across dialogue turns in an incrementally updated GPU cache, ranked by token prevalence, current-query relevance and residency bonus.
Yk4LNGEnIo.evidence: Evaluated on a multi-turn dialogue benchmark (MultiWOZ 2.2 per reviewers) with a compact model on desktop GPU hardware, against full-head inference and query-isolated loading.
Yk4LNGEnIo.claimed_gains: Reduces the LM-head footprint by 99.2% and peak GPU memory by 51.5% relative to full-head inference while preserving response quality, and reduces LM-head data movement by 7.5× versus query-isolated loading at matched response fidelity.
Yk4LNGEnIo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree cross-turn LM-head reuse is a practical, underexplored overhead source and that the cache policy coherently balances dialogue relevance, recent token usage and residency to cut memory and transfers.
Yk4LNGEnIo.main_concern: Evaluation is narrow (one dialogue dataset, a compact model, desktop GPU), quality is measured as agreement with full-head greedy outputs, and the policy is undefined when mandatory rows exceed the memory budget.

htxUziKk4C.one_liner: Parallel Top-1 routers with skip options set token expert counts; an MPC controller tunes skip loss to reach target sparsity.
htxUziKk4C.problem: A single router per layer with a predetermined number of experts per token gives an inflexible activation rate and limits adaptable network sparsity.
htxUziKk4C.method: OCAT (One Choice at A Time) uses parallel Top-1 routers per layer, each with a skip mechanism that allows bypassing when predictive precision holds, so both which experts and how many are decided per token. A Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework adjusts the skip-loss weight to steer realized skip probability toward a target setpoint.
htxUziKk4C.key_idea: Parallel Top-1 routers each can skip, so the number of active experts emerges per token, while MPC adjusts skip-loss weight to hold a target skip rate.
htxUziKk4C.evidence: Models of 2B, 7B and 10B total parameters trained on 600B tokens, compared with Top-K router baselines at comparable activation levels, with test-time activation sweeps and a comparison to public models.
htxUziKk4C.claimed_gains: OCAT models achieve an average 2% improvement over Top-K router baselines at comparable activation levels across different model scales.
htxUziKk4C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the parallel Top-1 routing is simple, allows flexible per-token expert counts, improves over fixed Top-K across scales, and lets one checkpoint serve different compute budgets at test time.
htxUziKk4C.main_concern: The many added components (skip expert, MPC, soft cap, modified z-loss) are not ablated, MPC is not compared with simpler controllers, and comparisons with dynamic-sparsity methods such as MoE++ and ReMoE are missing or not compute-matched.

RyIGne4oFm.one_liner: FURETON benchmarks protein function retrieval under joint sequence and structure similarity controls; contrastive projection heads adapt frozen protein language models.
RyIGne4oFm.problem: Proteins with similar functions can have dissimilar sequences and structures, yet existing methods are insufficiently evaluated at recovering such relationships under joint sequence and structure controls.
RyIGne4oFm.method: The benchmark uses 91,788 reviewed Swiss-Prot proteins with AlphaFold structures and GO annotations, controls sequence and structure similarity between query-target pairs, and defines relevance through informative shared GO ancestors. The authors also train projection heads with a contrastive objective on frozen pretrained protein language models.
RyIGne4oFm.key_idea: Define relevance by informative shared GO ancestors on query-target pairs with controlled sequence and structure similarity, and adapt frozen protein LMs with contrastive projection heads.
RyIGne4oFm.evidence: Zero-shot evaluation of sequence and structure search, protein language models, structure-aware models, protein-text contrastive models, protein-to-text generative models and signature-derived descriptions, plus contrastive adaptation across Molecular Function, Biological Process and Cellular Component.
RyIGne4oFm.claimed_gains: Contrastive adaptation improves retrieval across Molecular Function, Biological Process, Cellular Component and overall; no numbers are given in the visible abstract.
RyIGne4oFm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets a biologically meaningful problem with a clear construction protocol, joint sequence and structure controls, and a broad comparison of methods.
RyIGne4oFm.main_concern: Relevance relies only on GO annotations (possible false negatives), and text-generating models trained on Swiss-Prot descriptions may be recalling known annotations rather than inferring function, which the paper does not check.

gejL7zYGCR.one_liner: Adds a worst-case empirical Fisher trace penalty over a parameter neighborhood during task learning, shaping solutions for later EWC consolidation.
gejL7zYGCR.problem: EWC's local Fisher importance at the retained solution does not characterize sensitivity after a finite parameter displacement.
gejL7zYGCR.method: FS-EWC minimizes the worst-case empirical FIM trace within a prescribed neighborhood during task learning, favoring solutions less sensitive to bounded future displacement. At task completion, the retained reference is selected for subsequent Fisher estimation and consolidation.
gejL7zYGCR.key_idea: Minimize the worst-case empirical Fisher trace in a neighborhood of the current parameters during training so the retained solution is insensitive to future drift.
gejL7zYGCR.evidence: Experiments on four standard vision benchmarks, five fine-grained datasets and two Llama scales (full-parameter and LoRA), with controlled studies of stability-plasticity and parameter drift, and a theoretical bound on sensitivity.
gejL7zYGCR.claimed_gains: Improves over EWC across multiple benchmarks with a more favorable stability–plasticity balance and greater tolerance to parameter drift; no numbers are stated.
gejL7zYGCR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reframing of EWC's local-importance limitation is well motivated and that evaluation across vision and language, full-parameter and LoRA, supports the value of solution shaping.
gejL7zYGCR.main_concern: The objective closely resembles flatness regularizers such as C-Flat, its added benefit is not isolated under matched budgets, and the training time and memory cost of the extra gradient evaluations are not reported.

cByGCdk4rD.one_liner: Replaces UMAP's stochastic negative sampling with a synchronous field-based repulsion computed from three scalar moments via interpolation-based FFT.
cByGCdk4rD.problem: Stochastic negative sampling makes UMAP embeddings unstable across reruns because the repulsive forces depend on the ordering of sampling events.
cByGCdk4rD.method: ibUMAP evaluates attraction and repulsion from a shared embedding snapshot and applies them synchronously. The degree-weighted repulsive field, motivated by the conditional expectation of negative sampling, is represented by three scalar moments evaluated with an interpolation-based FFT, avoiding all-pairs computation.
cByGCdk4rD.key_idea: Compute degree-weighted repulsion as a field from three scalar moments of the embedding snapshot, evaluated by interpolation-based FFT, instead of sampling negatives.
cByGCdk4rD.evidence: Controlled experiments on synchrony, kernel capping and FFT evaluation, plus end-to-end CPU and GPU benchmarks against umap-learn and cuML on million-scale datasets with fidelity metrics.
cByGCdk4rD.claimed_gains: Median speedups of 3.29× unseeded and 5.79× seeded over umap-learn on CPU, and 1.44× over cuML on million-scale datasets under unseeded GPU execution.
cByGCdk4rD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method gives substantial CPU speedups and better reproducibility, with controlled experiments that explain the fidelity trade-offs.
cByGCdk4rD.main_concern: Embedding fidelity is generally lower than standard UMAP on neighborhood preservation and global distance correlation, and the downstream impact of that loss is not established.

HKuoFpDLvP.one_liner: Splits a hidden diffusion-model backdoor across Signature and Payload LoRAs that activates only when the matched pair is co-loaded.
HKuoFpDLvP.problem: Safety checks that inspect LoRA adapters one at a time miss attacks where benign-looking adapters redirect image generation only when combined with a matched partner.
HKuoFpDLvP.method: The Signature adapter writes a pair-specific code into intermediate carrier representations, while the Payload adapter uses code-selective responses and opposing signal/reference branches that approximately cancel alone or with a mismatched Signature. Matched code–reader alignment breaks the cancellation inside GEGLU blocks, and both adapters are exported as ordinary static LoRA files.
HKuoFpDLvP.key_idea: Payload's opposing signal/reference branches cancel unless a matched Signature's code aligns with its reader, so the trigger is the partner adapter's identity.
HKuoFpDLvP.evidence: Text-to-image experiments on SD v1.5 and SDXL covering pair selectivity, standalone fidelity and robustness to deployment variations.
HKuoFpDLvP.claimed_gains: Matched-pair attack success rates of 97.9% on SD v1.5 and 98.7% on SDXL, compared with 2.8–4.6% when implanted adapters are loaded individually.
HKuoFpDLvP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the attack is a distinctive, plausible threat that shows evaluating adapters one at a time is insufficient, backed by a broad empirical evaluation.
HKuoFpDLvP.main_concern: The method is hard to verify (no code or checkpoints, unclear details), and practical reach is uncertain because the attacker must control both adapters and the benign utilities shown are simple.

xztyadrEYG.one_liner: Scales the DMD critic with the teacher and conditions it on the student's generation step to improve few-step diffusion distillation.
xztyadrEYG.problem: In Distribution Matching Distillation, a small critic paired with a larger teacher can degrade student quality and cause training collapse, and a step-agnostic critic must model a mixture of student outputs.
xztyadrEYG.method: Joint scaling sizes the critic alongside the teacher, and the step-aware critic (STAC) conditions on the student's generation step to estimate step-specific scores. STAC adds no student inference cost.
xztyadrEYG.key_idea: Size the online critic with the teacher and condition it on the student's current generation step so it estimates step-specific scores rather than a mixture.
xztyadrEYG.evidence: Controlled experiments across seven SiT model sizes on ImageNet, plus class-conditional ImageNet generation, text-to-image with SDXL and FLUX.2, and text-to-video with Wan2.1, with ablations on learning rate, critic update frequency and initialization.
xztyadrEYG.claimed_gains: Joint scaling and STAC consistently improve few-step distillation across ImageNet, SDXL, FLUX.2 and Wan2.1; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
xztyadrEYG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the critic-scaling study is systematic and informative, showing teacher-only scaling can backfire, and that STAC is a simple conditioning change supported by targeted ablations across image and video generation.
xztyadrEYG.main_concern: STAC's relation to the closest prior work (TDM's budget-conditioned critic, Phased DMD) is not clearly separated or used as a baseline, and some ablations are incomplete or not fully controlled.

F0NzC1CdRm.one_liner: Intent Ambiguity Score measures whether a decomposed query sequence could come from a benign query and filters attack datasets.
F0NzC1CdRm.problem: Existing decomposition-attack datasets contain many sub-query sequences that could plausibly come from benign queries, so they are not genuine attack instances.
F0NzC1CdRm.method: IAS predicts a benign query whose decomposition is semantically equivalent to the malicious sub-query sequence, generates that query's own decomposition, and cross-evaluates whether each sequence is a natural decomposition of the other's original query. A dataset-generation pipeline then filters candidates with IAS.
F0NzC1CdRm.key_idea: Score ambiguity bidirectionally: infer a benign query for the sub-queries, decompose it, and check whether each sequence naturally decomposes the other's original query.
F0NzC1CdRm.evidence: Formal justification of IAS, comparison with human and LLM annotations, a TF-IDF lexical-bias analysis of the existing DecomposedHarm dataset, and attack success rates on five LLMs under two evaluation settings.
F0NzC1CdRm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies real quality flaws in existing decomposition-attack datasets, such as intent ambiguity and lexical shortcuts, and backs them with in-paper measurements and an IAS-filtered pipeline.
F0NzC1CdRm.main_concern: Strong lexical bias remains in the new dataset (TF-IDF ROC-AUC 0.9963), and the attack-success metric (non-refusal) and IAS validation are too weak to support the reliability claims.

0MZtRDw81t.one_liner: Runs independent visual-exploration rollouts over entity hypotheses; a verifier compares entities and evidence across trajectories to select an answer.
0MZtRDw81t.problem: In knowledge-based VQA, an agent can retrieve genuine facts about a visually similar but wrong entity, producing a coherent yet incorrect trajectory (a grounding trap).
0MZtRDw81t.method: DiVE combines fine-grained evidence access with direct interaction tools. At inference, independent rollouts explore alternative entity hypotheses, and an off-the-shelf verifier compares recorded candidate entities and supporting evidence across trajectories (cross-trajectory verification, CTV) to select an existing answer.
0MZtRDw81t.key_idea: Group rollouts by terminal entity into an evidence forest and have a verifier compare candidate entities and their evidence across trajectories to choose an existing answer.
0MZtRDw81t.evidence: Experiments on E-VQA and InfoSeek against RAG, agentic-search and test-time-scaling baselines, using shared eight-rollout pools across four backbones with paired significance tests.
0MZtRDw81t.claimed_gains: Reports the best performance on E-VQA and InfoSeek versus RAG, agentic-search and test-time-scaling baselines, and higher accuracy with fewer verifier-stage tokens on shared rollout pools; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
0MZtRDw81t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is disciplined, with all selectors sharing the same frozen eight-rollout pools and significance tests, and that cross-trajectory verification improves candidate selection.
0MZtRDw81t.main_concern: The headline is compute-confounded (eight rollouts versus single-trajectory baselines), and the prevalence of grounding traps and their role in the gains rest on a single unvalidated exploratory audit.

MylO9Iqi7J.one_liner: Supervises Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian prediction with a Grassmannian geodesic loss on the occupied orbital subspace, invariant to orbital gauge rotations.
MylO9Iqi7J.problem: Element-wise Hamiltonian regression does not enforce accuracy of the occupied orbital subspace, and directly supervising orbital coefficients suffers from gauge redundancy and unstable eigenvector gradients near degeneracies.
MylO9Iqi7J.method: GrassDist aligns predicted and reference occupied subspaces with a Grassmannian geodesic loss that is invariant to gauge transformations among occupied orbitals by construction, and adds two gradient-stabilization components.
MylO9Iqi7J.key_idea: Penalize the geodesic distance between predicted and reference occupied subspaces on the Grassmann manifold, making the loss invariant to rotations among occupied orbitals.
MylO9Iqi7J.evidence: Experiments on QH9 splits and other datasets with multiple backbones, including a chordal-loss comparison and an outlier case study.
MylO9Iqi7J.claimed_gains: The visible abstract gives no numbers; a reviewer cites mean energy error on QH9 stable-iid falling from 4.87 to 0.04 kcal/mol and median error from 0.28 to 0.03.
MylO9Iqi7J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree occupied-subspace supervision is physically meaningful, simple to add to existing Hamiltonian prediction models, and gives large empirical gains on density-derived quantities.
MylO9Iqi7J.main_concern: The benefit of the Grassmannian geodesic form over simpler gauge-invariant subspace losses (chordal, Procrustes) is not isolated, and novelty relative to prior Grassmann-based density-matrix work is unclear.

LpsJRBpY3E.one_liner: UniSwap swaps appearance and voice in talking videos within one streaming audio-visual diffusion transformer trained via a swap-and-reconstruct pipeline.
LpsJRBpY3E.problem: Talking-video character replacement uses separately optimized models for appearance and voice, making audio-visual consistency hard to enforce, and aligned cross-identity training pairs are scarce.
LpsJRBpY3E.method: A single audio-visual diffusion transformer transfers reference appearance and vocal timbre while preserving source content. A swap-and-reconstruct pipeline synthesizes identity-mismatched sources, and a bidirectional backbone is adapted through In-context Pretraining, Conditional Streaming Adaptation (block-causal KV cache) and Efficient Self-forcing DMD, cutting sampling from 30 to 3 denoising steps per block.
LpsJRBpY3E.key_idea: Synthesize identity-mismatched source videos with learned replacement models, train the model to reconstruct the real clips under reference guidance, then distill to few-step block-causal streaming.
LpsJRBpY3E.evidence: 100 held-out clips against cascaded baselines on Sync-C, Sync-D and identity similarity, a four-clip blinded user study, cache and positional-encoding ablations, and a long-video benchmark of 30 one-minute sequences.
LpsJRBpY3E.claimed_gains: Reduces sampling from 30 to 3 denoising steps per block; the visible abstract gives no quality numbers, and reviewers cite 23.5 FPS on three H100 GPUs and best Sync-C and Sync-D on 100 held-out clips.
LpsJRBpY3E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree joint appearance-and-voice replacement is a useful task and that UniSwap shows a synchronization benefit over the evaluated cascades, supported by ablations of the streaming design.
LpsJRBpY3E.main_concern: Real-time and hour-scale claims exceed the evidence (23.5 FPS throughput on three H100 GPUs, no end-to-end latency, only one-minute clips), and demos show lip-sync misalignment and hand artifacts.

7DH2mj6meg.one_liner: Turns a pretrained video diffusion model into a latent action learner by extracting compact action latents from its spatiotemporal features.
7DH2mj6meg.problem: Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions and conflate the action with irrelevant visual variation, which limits transfer across embodiments.
7DH2mj6meg.method: DreamX extracts compact latent actions from a pretrained video diffusion model's spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by 300× and using the generative prior to separate action-relevant dynamics from appearance. The latent space serves as a shared action interface supporting any-to-any video transfer, zero-shot cross-embodiment action transfer and a compact latent policy.
7DH2mj6meg.key_idea: Read action latents out of a pretrained video diffusion model's features, using its generative prior to disentangle motion from appearance.
7DH2mj6meg.evidence: Evaluation on LARY-Bench, any-to-any video transfer, zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer, real-robot human-to-robot demonstrations, a latent-policy test on one drawer-closing task, and an ablation removing auxiliary action supervision.
7DH2mj6meg.claimed_gains: Compresses each latent video frame by 300× and reports top representation quality on LARY-Bench, with a compact latent policy improving task performance; other numbers are not stated.
7DH2mj6meg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the representation and transfer results on LARYBench are strong and that using a pretrained video diffusion model for action-relevant features, including human-to-robot transfer without paired data, is a promising direction.
7DH2mj6meg.main_concern: Comparisons are not apples-to-apples (language conditioning, auxiliary action supervision, larger pretrained backbone) and ablations do not isolate the mechanism, while physical validation and viewpoint robustness are limited.

CriSopAQzW.one_liner: EarthAlign pairs ERA5 weather data with multi-style captions, and MeteoLIP aligns meteorology tokens with language in a dual encoder.
CriSopAQzW.problem: General-purpose alignment between Earth system data and language is underexplored because diverse language supervision grounded in meteorological conditions is scarce.
CriSopAQzW.method: EarthAlign combines 10 expert-curated natural event and disaster sources with climatology-derived normal-weather samples (2000–2024), each with four caption styles aligned to 63-variable ERA5 data. MeteoLIP is a dual encoder whose MetTok uses a geolocation- and time-conditioned query to aggregate variable-specific patch embeddings into a compact sequence of meteorology tokens.
CriSopAQzW.key_idea: MetTok aggregates variable-specific ERA5 patch embeddings with a geolocation- and time-conditioned query into meteorology tokens that a dual encoder aligns with captions.
CriSopAQzW.evidence: Three downstream tasks (cross-modal retrieval, weather-condition classification, physical variable estimation), a WeatherQA transfer experiment, a stratified human audit of captions, and ablations on conditioning and caption styles.
CriSopAQzW.claimed_gains: The visible abstract is cut off before any numbers; a reviewer cites retrieval R@1 of 58.79/60.10 for the full model versus 31.64/31.10 for four-style CLIP.
CriSopAQzW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree EarthAlign is a large, carefully documented resource for meteorology-language research that combines event records, normal-weather samples and multiple caption styles.
CriSopAQzW.main_concern: Retrieval gains are confounded by metadata shortcuts, since a model seeing only geolocation and time reaches 50.4/58.5 R@1 versus 58.8/60.1 for the full model, and MetTok's own benefit is not isolated.

y5runSPdHm.one_liner: CryoASTRA keeps a semantic voxel representation through cryo-EM atomic modeling, using sparse BallTree attention where atoms query nearby voxels.
y5runSPdHm.problem: Learned cryo-EM atomic model builders use local map crops, patch tokens or density samples at predicted atoms, losing voxel-wise semantics before coordinate generation.
y5runSPdHm.method: CryoASTRA computes on the 1 Å grid only within the macromolecular region, with a two-scale representation of EM points aligned to the input sequences and a semantic voxel representation from a voxel encoder. Heterogeneous BallTree Attention lets atoms query nearby voxels at linear cost for a fixed leaf size, and a GPU sparse pipeline runs whole-map inference without sliding windows.
y5runSPdHm.key_idea: Atoms cross-attend to nearby semantic voxels through BallTree-organized sparse attention with linear cost, so voxel features persist through coordinate generation.
y5runSPdHm.evidence: 103 sequence-novel maps from 2026 (1.5–3.9 Å) compared with other builders including CryoAtom2, with a common 50-target subset and an EM-point localization probe.
y5runSPdHm.claimed_gains: Places on average 92.5% of protein atoms within 3 Å of deposited positions and has the highest TM-score among the evaluated builders on proteins and nucleic acids.
y5runSPdHm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retaining voxel-level features is well motivated, the sparse pipeline addresses a GPU memory bottleneck, and the prospective 103-map evaluation is careful about coverage and sequence leakage.
y5runSPdHm.main_concern: No controlled ablations isolate the semantic voxel representation, EM points or BallTree attention from the pretrained backbone, MSA conditioning and atomic diffusion.

4M8ekhjSIM.one_liner: Starts few-step diffusion sampling from mean-shifted Gaussian noise that approximates the high-noise intermediate distribution, with no training.
4M8ekhjSIM.problem: Few-step diffusion sampling suffers large discretization errors from big step sizes, and existing intermediate-start methods need extra trained models or real samples at inference.
4M8ekhjSIM.method: MSIS approximates the high-noise intermediate distribution with mean-shifted Gaussian noise, where the shift follows from the forward noising formula and the dataset and is computed once offline. It is reusable across samplers, timestep schedules and models sharing the input space, and the authors show the mean shift is the dominant data-dependent deviation near the Gaussian endpoint.
4M8ekhjSIM.key_idea: Replace the pure-noise start with Gaussian noise shifted by a precomputed dataset mean at the chosen intermediate noise level, and begin reverse sampling there.
4M8ekhjSIM.evidence: Experiments across datasets, samplers, timestep schedules and architectures, including conditional ImageNet 256×256 with DDIM step budgets and Stable Diffusion 2.1 on MS-COCO, plus a cumulant-based theoretical analysis.
4M8ekhjSIM.claimed_gains: On conditional ImageNet 256×256, MSIS needs 2.22 minutes of one-time preprocessing on a single RTX 3090 and reduces FID by 35.18%–55.33% across the evaluated DDIM step budgets.
4M8ekhjSIM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free, adds negligible inference overhead, and gives substantial FID improvements across datasets, samplers and architectures in the few-step regime.
4M8ekhjSIM.main_concern: Performance is sensitive to the starting timestep and the calibration procedure is under-specified, while the theory is asymptotic and does not bound the finite-step initialization error or account for the dropped covariance.

fpqZI99Hbf.one_liner: Contrastive learning with auxiliary variables identifies latent states and instantaneous plus lagged causal structure in nonstationary time series.
fpqZI99Hbf.problem: Methods that jointly handle instantaneous causal relations, lagged relations and nonstationarity in latent-state time series remain limited.
fpqZI99Hbf.method: The authors prove sufficient conditions to identify latent states up to permutation and component-wise invertible transformation, and their instantaneous and lagged causal structures up to the same permutation, using an observed auxiliary variable linked to transition-noise changes. iCReN implements this with contrastive learning (TCL and GCL variants) for discrete or continuous auxiliary variables.
fpqZI99Hbf.key_idea: An auxiliary variable (time or condition label) that shifts transition-noise distributions makes latent states and both causal graphs identifiable, learned via contrastive losses plus structural regularization.
fpqZI99Hbf.evidence: Synthetic experiments on recovery of latent states and of instantaneous and lagged structures, plus downstream forecasting on real-world data.
fpqZI99Hbf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly modeling instantaneous relations, lagged relations and nonstationarity is a well-motivated problem and that the framework offers flexible discrete and continuous auxiliary-variable implementations.
fpqZI99Hbf.main_concern: Identifiability rests on strong, hard-to-verify assumptions and observed auxiliary variables with a gap between theory and implementation, and novelty over IDOL, IIA and Jacobian-based methods is limited.

97XCQK26JE.one_liner: Optimizes a five-parameter physics-based thermal plume, coupling refraction and radiance through one temperature field, with CMA-ES to attack infrared VLMs.
97XCQK26JE.problem: The robustness of infrared vision-language models to non-contact thermal variations is underexplored.
97XCQK26JE.method: Thermal Plume Attack models a rising thermal plume whose shared temperature field couples refractive displacement with radiance variation, and optimizes its configuration with CMA-ES in a score-only black-box setting.
97XCQK26JE.key_idea: Search a low-dimensional plume model whose single temperature field drives both refractive displacement and radiance change, using CMA-ES against model scores.
97XCQK26JE.evidence: Person and vehicle crops from FLIR and LLVIP against LanguageBind Thermal and IRGPT, plus four CLIP backbones adapted to infrared data and matched controls.
97XCQK26JE.claimed_gains: Shows effective top-1 flips for LanguageBind Thermal and IRGPT; no success rates are stated in the abstract.
97XCQK26JE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the low-dimensional, physically interpretable perturbation is a logical way to probe infrared VLMs, with a broad evaluation that reports query budgets and limitations carefully.
97XCQK26JE.main_concern: No ablations isolate refraction, radiance or the shared temperature field, and physical realism is unverified because there is no real thermal-source validation and the attack uses ground-truth boxes and continuous scores.

qucLiqr42z.one_liner: Grounds Solver targets in frozen-detector evidence and rewards the Proposer only for measured Solver progress on separate probe images.
qucLiqr42z.problem: In self-evolving multimodal models, Solver majority answers can reinforce shared errors and Proposer rewards can favor invalid questions, so the self-rewarding signal cannot be trusted.
qucLiqr42z.method: A frozen detector grounds candidate questions in visual evidence and yields supported answer sets in place of Solver consensus. The Solver learns from the full supported set, and the Proposer earns credit only when matched trial updates yield greater Solver progress on separate probe images, with no task-specific labels, teacher model or answer judge.
qucLiqr42z.key_idea: Replace Solver-consensus labels with detector-supported answer sets, and reward the Proposer by the Solver's measured gain on held-out probes from matched trial updates.
qucLiqr42z.evidence: Failure-mode diagnosis across seven checkpoints on POPE and HallusionBench, then training on 851 spatial-relation questions over 256 COCO images with detector supervision, with set-versus-single-answer and frozen-versus-learned-Proposer ablations and MMMU transfer.
qucLiqr42z.claimed_gains: Unanimous errors account for 14.5–76.7% of wrong majority answers across seven checkpoints on POPE and HallusionBench; the visible abstract gives no gain numbers for the method itself.
qucLiqr42z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis of self-evolution failure modes is rigorous, showing that consensus rewards cannot separate unanimous errors from unanimous successes, and that independent grounding gives more reliable supervision.
qucLiqr42z.main_concern: Most of the gain comes from detector-grounded supervision in a narrow spatial setting (91.2% of questions have a single supported answer), while the learned Proposer adds only a small increment.

CzXEImoNtO.one_liner: Detects time series anomalies from deviations along prototype-guided DDIM inversion trajectories, with no reverse denoising or test-time reconstruction.
CzXEImoNtO.problem: Diffusion-based anomaly detectors rely on iterative reverse denoising, which couples detection to generative fidelity, can reconstruct anomalies, and adds inference overhead.
CzXEImoNtO.method: PiAD runs deterministic DDIM inversion and scores windows against normal latent dynamics learned by a noise predictor. Because normal behavior is multimodal, it combines prototype-conditioned latent diffusion with prototype-specific Gaussian trajectory priors and aggregates the most discriminative deviations across inversion states with training-calibrated Top-k.
CzXEImoNtO.key_idea: Score each window by its deviation from prototype-specific Gaussian priors along its deterministic data-to-noise inversion path, aggregated by training-calibrated Top-k.
CzXEImoNtO.evidence: Experiments on five real-world datasets reporting VUS and affiliation metrics, multiple runs and efficiency measurements against diffusion-based baselines.
CzXEImoNtO.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms existing diffusion-based approaches on five real-world datasets; no numbers are stated in the visible abstract.
CzXEImoNtO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mode-conditioned, reconstruction-free scoring is well motivated for multimodal normal behavior, and that the evaluation reports VUS and affiliation metrics, multiple runs and efficiency.
CzXEImoNtO.main_concern: Reconstruction-free inversion scoring is already covered by InvAD and DiffPath, a clean-latent-only prototype control is missing, and results depend on thresholding for Affiliation-F1.

TXu9q35Dmi.one_liner: Rubric-scores memory-search steps offline, distills reflective experience, and retrieves it at inference to guide planning without parameter updates.
TXu9q35Dmi.problem: In deep memory search, final outcomes alone do not show which search behaviors to keep or correct, since successful searches include unnecessary steps and failed ones contain useful steps.
TXu9q35Dmi.method: Offline, a Rubric-guided Evaluator scores planning and reflection steps on search-specific rubrics, giving scores, reasons and suggestions, and a self-Reflection Learner turns selected high- and low-scoring steps and their feedback into reusable fine-grained reflective experience. At inference the agent retrieves relevant experience to guide planning and reflection without updating model parameters.
TXu9q35Dmi.key_idea: Score individual planning and reflection steps with multi-dimensional rubrics, then convert high- and low-scoring steps into retrievable experience entries injected at inference time.
TXu9q35Dmi.evidence: Experiments on LoCoMo, HotpotQA and NarrativeQA with Qwen2.5 and Llama backbones, component ablations, and a Self-Evo setting in which the backbone evaluates itself.
TXu9q35Dmi.claimed_gains: With Qwen2.5-3B, R^2-Mem achieves a 22.6% relative F1 gain while reducing online token usage by 12.9% and search iterations by 20.2%.
TXu9q35Dmi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and that step-level, rubric-guided diagnosis improves answer quality while reducing online tokens and search iterations across backbone sizes.
TXu9q35Dmi.main_concern: Generality is not established: experience is built per benchmark with no cross-dataset transfer, there is no comparison against a stronger model such as GPT-4o solving the same tasks, and the backbones are dated.

mIN6wvMF1Z.one_liner: Coarse-to-fine diffusion forecaster recentering sampled block averages on a point-forecast anchor, with zero-mean fine detail preserving each coarse scenario.
mIN6wvMF1Z.problem: Forcing every sampled trajectory to match one point forecast for a block removes spread in that block's average, so multi-resolution probabilistic forecasts lose aggregate uncertainty.
mIN6wvMF1Z.method: A first diffusion model samples coarse residuals per trajectory; for each block the mean residual across trajectories is subtracted and the centered residuals are added to the anchor. A second diffusion model generates fine detail conditioned on each coarse scenario, and the detail is projected to zero mean within each block so block averages are retained up to numerical precision.
mIN6wvMF1Z.key_idea: Center sampled coarse residuals across the ensemble around the anchor, then condition fine diffusion on each coarse scenario and project its detail to zero block mean.
mIN6wvMF1Z.evidence: Six datasets across four forecasting horizons with three training seeds, plus ablations and fixed-coarse-scenario and matched-mean comparisons on ETTh1 and Weather.
mIN6wvMF1Z.claimed_gains: Achieves the lowest mean fine-resolution CRPS in 15 of 24 dataset–horizon settings, but performs substantially worse on Electricity and Traffic, where the generated coarse distributions are highly overdispersed.
mIN6wvMF1Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation is clear and the structural guarantees are transparent, separating ensemble-mean preservation from fixing individual aggregate outcomes, with informative controlled comparisons.
mIN6wvMF1Z.main_concern: The method degrades severely on Electricity and Traffic from overdispersed coarse samples, and its benefit over simple mean correction is small, leaving the necessity of the full pipeline unestablished.

UkYifKhPOx.one_liner: AgentCIScope converts privacy cases into executable multi-application agent tasks with disclosure constraints from policies, persona agreement and a sensitive-attribute taxonomy.
UkYifKhPOx.problem: Existing agent privacy evaluations cover only model-level leakage or a limited set of application environments with manually built disclosure constraints, so contextual integrity of agent information flows is under-measured.
UkYifKhPOx.method: A unified pipeline turns synthetic and real-world privacy cases into executable agent tasks in realistic application environments such as email and calendar. Disclosure constraints are grounded in the intersection of governing privacy policies, persona-based agreement and a predefined sensitive-attribute taxonomy.
UkYifKhPOx.key_idea: Define a task's disclosure constraints as the intersection of policy, persona agreement and sensitive-attribute criteria, then run agents on executable multi-step tasks and measure contextual-integrity violations.
UkYifKhPOx.evidence: Evaluation of 12 types of agents across backbone models, agent frameworks, source and destination applications and task types, on 936 tasks sharing 212 contracts, with human validation of contracts and the judge.
UkYifKhPOx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is broad and well described, covering diverse executable multi-application tasks across several models and frameworks, and that it shows task completion can coexist with substantial disclosure failures.
UkYifKhPOx.main_concern: Tasks are selected for inducing leakage in a surrogate agent and use disclosure-inducing instructions whose fairness is unverified, so reported rates may reflect instruction-following and a deliberately selected failure set.

hu2Jd3c2gX.one_liner: MuseFACET benchmarks MLLMs on identifying and interpreting 5,000 museum objects from 9 museums, scoring trustworthiness and controllability.
hu2Jd3c2gX.problem: Existing museum and artwork text-generation efforts are limited in scale and diversity and rely on reference-based similarity metrics that miss trustworthiness and knowledge-grounded, context-aware generation.
hu2Jd3c2gX.method: The benchmark has two hierarchical tasks: Identification of object attributes from images, and Interpretation that generates coherent, context-aware descriptions. Evaluation uses identification accuracy plus five interpretation criteria: Faithfulness, Completeness, Conciseness, Depth and Acuity.
hu2Jd3c2gX.key_idea: Separate identification accuracy from interpretation quality scored on five criteria, and compare image-only against metadata-supplied inputs across cultural regions.
hu2Jd3c2gX.evidence: Evaluation of 14 proprietary and open-source MLLMs in image-only and metadata-supplied settings, with human validation under an iterative protocol and a breakdown by cultural region.
hu2Jd3c2gX.claimed_gains: The highest accuracy on the Identification task among the 14 evaluated MLLMs reaches only 31.2%, and providing metadata substantially improves Interpretation.
hu2Jd3c2gX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the resource is thorough and soundly built, with multi-museum schema alignment, metadata normalization, manual quality control and human evaluation that goes beyond reference similarity.
hu2Jd3c2gX.main_concern: Identification accuracy is not separated from visual answerability, since abstaining (not sure) and wrong answers both score zero, so low scores mix model failure with insufficient image evidence.

EZIT4KKU9j.one_liner: MultiBit aligns Hamming candidate rankings across nested code lengths with a scale-decomposable fractional diffusion teacher built from label co-occurrence.
EZIT4KKU9j.problem: Cross-modal hashing methods do not ensure that fine-grained multi-label relations survive as consistent candidate rankings in finite, multi-length Hamming spaces (the relevance resolution bottleneck).
EZIT4KKU9j.method: A fractional-diffusion relation teacher built from dataset-level label co-occurrence and label specificity models local to long-range dependencies over continuous diffusion scales and gives query-conditioned relevance targets. Discretized diffusion scales and their weights map to scale-aware bit subblocks, code lengths are nested prefixes, and Hamming candidate rankings are aligned with the teacher.
EZIT4KKU9j.key_idea: Assign diffusion scales to bit subblocks of nested-prefix codes and align each code length's Hamming ranking with a fractional-diffusion relevance teacher.
EZIT4KKU9j.evidence: Experiments on four benchmarks measuring retrieval mAP plus collision, reversal and cross-code-length ranking consistency.
EZIT4KKU9j.claimed_gains: Consistent improvements in retrieval accuracy on four benchmarks; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
EZIT4KKU9j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the relevance resolution bottleneck is a meaningful problem and that experiments on multiple benchmarks show competitive retrieval, better ranking consistency across code lengths, and reduced deployment cost.
EZIT4KKU9j.main_concern: For 16-, 32- and 64-bit codes only the first scale subblock is used, so multi-scale fusion appears only at 128 bits, mAP gains over strong baselines are sometimes small, and the candidate pools for the ranking metrics are not comparable.

ueXanPoRpQ.one_liner: Nested channel masking orders features so a leading prefix guides velocity correction while the full representation predicts the clean image.
ueXanPoRpQ.problem: In pixel diffusion, x-prediction learns stronger representations and gives lower FID with enough steps but underperforms in few-step sampling, because converting x to velocity amplifies errors along high-energy directions.
ueXanPoRpQ.method: OiT (Ordered-representation image Transformer) uses nested channel masking so dominant image information is progressively accessible from the leading feature channels. A compact prefix guides a full-dimensional velocity correction while the full representation handles clean-image prediction; bottlenecked Representation Alignment (bREPA) and a Hann Decoder are added.
ueXanPoRpQ.key_idea: Nested channel masking concentrates dominant image information in leading feature channels, whose compact prefix drives a velocity correction on top of x-prediction.
ueXanPoRpQ.evidence: ImageNet 256×256 pixel-space generation with OiT-B and OiT-XL, a few-step sampling evaluation, and ablations on nested masking, prefix width, bREPA and the Hann Decoder.
ueXanPoRpQ.claimed_gains: On ImageNet 256×256, OiT-B and OiT-XL achieve FID-50K scores of 2.52 and 1.55, respectively.
ueXanPoRpQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the x-pred versus v-pred trade-off is clearly motivated and that OiT gives strong ImageNet results that scale from B to XL, with useful ablations and promising few-step sampling.
ueXanPoRpQ.main_concern: The core correction mechanism adds little on its own (FID 5.84 to 5.68 in Table 3), most gains come from the decoder and bREPA, and results lack seeds and compute-matched comparisons.

JErEPDsUBc.one_liner: Residual addresses keep compressed LLM memories locatable; retrieval searches a compressed graph and reads original records only when needed.
JErEPDsUBc.problem: Lightweight memory compression keeps content semantics but discards details such as names, locations and temporal cues needed to locate memories for future queries, while graph memories need costly LLM relation construction up front.
JErEPDsUBc.method: DuCoMem compresses both memory content and graph structure while preserving on-demand access to original records. Residual addresses store key details discarded by the compressor; for the graph, a low-cost candidate graph is simplified by removing redundant nodes and edges and an LLM checks relations only on the smaller graph. Retrieval starts from a few representative nodes, reads nearby original records, and searches further only when evidence is insufficient.
JErEPDsUBc.key_idea: Pair each compressed memory with residual addresses of discarded details, and retrieve coarse-to-fine over an LLM-checked compressed graph with local recovery of original records.
JErEPDsUBc.evidence: Experiments on two datasets including LoCoMo, with seven answering models of different sizes compared against methods such as SimpleMem, plus retrieval diagnostics and component ablations.
JErEPDsUBc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between preserving content and preserving retrievability is useful, that residual addressing is a concrete fix, and that DuCoMem improves accuracy and token cost over compared memory methods across answering models.
JErEPDsUBc.main_concern: The graph's added value over ReadAgent and GraphReader is unclear, ablations do not isolate residual addressing, and the extra construction and retrieval steps may add overhead against simpler memory structures.

FudBt5JaF6.one_liner: L2T discretizes tool-produced visual states into visual tokens and trains routing and difficulty-aware rewards to choose reasoning form and depth.
FudBt5JaF6.problem: Fast-slow reasoning methods regulate only textual reasoning length and treat visual computation from external tools or visual tokens as auxiliary, which prevents jointly optimizing perception and reasoning.
FudBt5JaF6.method: L2T discretizes tool-produced visual states into visual tokens so perception and text reasoning share one autoregressive space. It then adds a modality-aware routing reward to select reasoning modes and a difficulty-aware fast-slow strategy to adapt reasoning depth to task complexity.
FudBt5JaF6.key_idea: Quantize tool outputs into visual tokens generated in-sequence, then use a modality-aware routing reward and a difficulty-aware fast-slow strategy to choose reasoning form and depth.
FudBt5JaF6.evidence: Experiments on general perception and reasoning-intensive tasks with Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 7B, compared with explicit tool-calling approaches, with ablations from a shared SFT starting point.
FudBt5JaF6.claimed_gains: Compared with explicit tool-calling approaches, L2T maintains competitive performance while achieving 1.7–3.6× higher throughput.
FudBt5JaF6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is practical, cutting external tool-call and long-reasoning cost while roughly keeping accuracy, and that it unifies visual and textual reasoning in one token sequence.
FudBt5JaF6.main_concern: The core claim that generated visual tokens can replace real visual operations is not directly validated, the tool-calling comparison does not control for data and optimization, and only Qwen2.5-VL 3B and 7B are tested.

au25Jrxrf0.one_liner: PGR splits conditional molecular graph diffusion sampling into size planning, endpoint-property guidance and chemistry-constrained edge repair on a frozen backbone.
au25Jrxrf0.problem: Conditional molecular graph generators leave molecular size, property control along the reverse trajectory and chemical correction to one denoising process, although each needs different information at different stages.
au25Jrxrf0.method: Plan selects a condition-dependent, training-supported molecular size before denoising. Guide learns the endpoint property implied by sampled categorical states from actual reverse trajectories and, at each reverse step, differentiates the target discrepancy on soft node and edge distributions to steer generation. Repair uses the backbone edge posterior to revise late bond choices that violate valence, aromaticity or connectivity constraints.
au25Jrxrf0.key_idea: Pick size before denoising, steer each reverse step by gradients of a learned endpoint-property predictor on soft node/edge distributions, then repair invalid bonds.
au25Jrxrf0.evidence: Joint O2/N2/CO2 generation and the BACE, BBBP and HIV tasks, with ablations of the three components.
au25Jrxrf0.claimed_gains: On joint O2/N2/CO2 generation, PGR attains 0.9991 raw validity and 0.497 average property error; on BACE, BBBP and HIV it reaches property accuracies of 0.9716, 0.9665 and 0.9912 with raw validities of 0.9248, 0.9549 and 0.7745.
au25Jrxrf0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Plan, Guide and Repair decomposition is clear and maps to distinct needs in conditional generation, with comprehensive experiments showing effective condition control.
au25Jrxrf0.main_concern: Guide relies on surrogate-predicted property labels whose errors may transfer, evidence that Guide plus Repair are necessary is thin, simple molecular-string baselines are missing, and the method motivation is under-explained.

tvgKaRKDmg.one_liner: Federated agent memory shares locally verified, MDL-pruned executable rules that check candidate actions and give a frozen LLM corrective feedback.
tvgKaRKDmg.problem: Episodic replay and retrieval-augmented memory raise inference cost and expose detailed interaction records when shared across users.
tvgKaRKDmg.method: Clients synthesize rules (compact, stateless programs) from local failures, verify their behavior and apply Minimum Description Length (MDL) pruning before upload. The server deduplicates retained rules and broadcasts a global library that clients re-validate against later local evidence, while raw records stay local and the acting LLM stays frozen.
tvgKaRKDmg.key_idea: Share compact stateless programs that test candidate actions, so each rule can be validated against a client's own logged outcomes without an LLM call.
tvgKaRKDmg.evidence: Nine independent end-to-end runs on Crafter and ALFWorld against a matched federated textual-rule control, plus ablations on behavioral verification.
tvgKaRKDmg.claimed_gains: Reaches a Crafter Score of 13.5±2.4 and ALFWorld success of 64.8±0.8%, versus 11.4±2.0 and 62.4±0.9% for the matched federated textual-rule control; the final Crafter library occupies 0.031 MB per client and end-to-end token use is 61.9k per task.
tvgKaRKDmg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sharing small executable rules with a frozen acting LLM is practical for API-only models and that behavioral verification before sharing makes a clear empirical difference.
tvgKaRKDmg.main_concern: The comparison does not show that the executable format itself drives the gain (verification and execution are tested jointly), the same 134 ALFWorld tasks recur across rounds, and embedding-based rule merging may discard complementary conditions.

nEDVIjb07v.one_liner: Jointly ranks every MLP neuron and attention head via soft pruning across sparsity targets, making pretrained transformers elastic without retraining.
nEDVIjb07v.problem: Model families offer only a few fixed sizes, forcing users to commit to one under hardware and latency constraints, which is suboptimal under varying query loads.
nEDVIjb07v.method: A retraining-free method optimizes a differentiable relaxation of the functional unit-ranking problem: instead of one importance weight per block or head, every MLP neuron and attention head is ranked jointly on a common scale by minimizing the model's loss under soft pruning across many sparsity targets at once. The resulting ranking lets one model adapt on the fly across computational budgets.
