nEDVIjb07v.key_idea: Optimize per-neuron and per-head importance scores on one shared scale by minimizing loss under soft pruning across many sparsity targets at once.
nEDVIjb07v.evidence: 27 vision and text transformer encoders from 22M to 8B parameters across classification, retrieval and segmentation, compared with one-shot baselines, with latency and throughput measured on AugReg ViT-B/16.
nEDVIjb07v.claimed_gains: Smooth degradation up to 60% sparsity across 27 encoders; pruning DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 to 50% sparsity removes 427M parameters while reducing ImageNet-1k linear-probing accuracy by only 0.8%, and a pruned AugReg ViT-B/16 at 60% sparsity reaches up to 1.80× higher throughput and 1.26× lower single-query latency.
nEDVIjb07v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical, with one frozen model prunable to any budget at inference time, broad evaluation across 27 encoders, and smoother degradation than baselines at high sparsity.
nEDVIjb07v.main_concern: Methodological novelty over SnapViT and standard soft-mask pruning is limited, and speedups are shown for only one model and depend on compilation and hardware-friendly tiling constraints.

AliBDQPkO6.one_liner: EvoWeb benchmarks coding agents on 320 cumulative requests over 32 web apps, testing each version in a live browser.
AliBDQPkO6.problem: Web-generation benchmarks evaluate development toward fixed specifications, while real development proceeds through successive requests that extend an existing implementation.
AliBDQPkO6.method: Requests are grounded in real product features and structured by functional dependency graphs. Agents iteratively modify a persistent codebase while a multimodal web agent tests each intermediate application for new functionality, cross-request integration and previously requested functionality, and trajectory performance is integrated across user-tolerance thresholds instead of a fixed stopping criterion.
AliBDQPkO6.key_idea: Chain feature requests in dependency graphs over a persistent codebase and score each stage with functional, integration and backward tests aggregated across user-tolerance thresholds.
AliBDQPkO6.evidence: Experiments on open- and closed-source frontier models, with analyses of dependency depth and runtime errors over successive requests, plus human and cross-vendor judge validation.
AliBDQPkO6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark extends web generation to realistic cumulative development, and that dependency graphs with separate functional, integration and backward tests give an actionable evaluation validated by human and cross-vendor judges.
AliBDQPkO6.main_concern: Evaluator uncertainty (the human audit shows integration-score bias and low agreement on ambiguous cases) is not propagated into trajectory scores, and the dependency findings are observational and partly confounded.

WANnDuFpxf.one_liner: Orders layerwise QAT by each layer's estimated recovery from other layers' quantization errors, then trains scales with a fused kernel.
WANnDuFpxf.problem: Layerwise QAT uses a fixed input-to-output order that assigns adaptation by depth, which can leave layers with limited adaptation ability to handle errors after more capable layers are frozen.
WANnDuFpxf.method: Oats (Order-aware Adaptation Score) estimates a layer's potential recovery from other layers' quantization errors. Stout's first stage computes Oats through shared measurements and trains layers with the model's output loss in ascending score order; the second stage trains scales with fixed quantized weights using ScaleKernel, a fused backward kernel that avoids dense weight-gradient intermediates in global memory.
WANnDuFpxf.key_idea: Train layers in ascending order of a score that estimates recoverable loss from cross-layer gradient response, saving high-recovery layers for last.
WANnDuFpxf.evidence: Experiments on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 2-bit, with ordering ablations (ascending versus descending, depth-matched), comparisons against quantization baselines, and a local analysis of recovery.
WANnDuFpxf.claimed_gains: On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 2bit, Stout improves LiveCodeBench pass@1 and the BFCL aggregate score by 0.87% and 2.68% over the development-selected ordering baseline.
WANnDuFpxf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree layer ordering is an under-explored, practically relevant factor in layerwise QAT, supported by clean ablations and an efficient scoring procedure, and that the paper is well written.
WANnDuFpxf.main_concern: The theory rests on restrictive local-quadratic assumptions and does not guarantee that sorting by the score improves overall QAT, while the ordering ablations are single-run with differences near seed noise.

8SZkaiC1UC.one_liner: NebulaSD pools draft and target workers independently and dynamically rebuilds stage-specific batches from shared request pools for speculative decoding.
8SZkaiC1UC.problem: Drafting and verification favor different batch configurations, so fixed draft-target coupling is inefficient under concurrent workloads, and existing disaggregated designs keep request or batch affinities that block global capacity sharing.
8SZkaiC1UC.method: NebulaSD organizes draft and target workers into independently schedulable resource pools and reconstructs stage-specific batches from shared request pools. It makes request state available at newly selected workers without migration stalls through worker-triggered batch reconstruction and asynchronous KV-state preparation overlapped with model execution.
8SZkaiC1UC.key_idea: Let any worker pull requests from shared pools to rebuild stage-specific batches, while overlapping asynchronous KV-state preparation with execution to avoid migration stalls.
8SZkaiC1UC.evidence: System and scaling evaluations on a four-GPU deployment (largest experiment 8B per reviewers, with most results from simulation), plus sensitivity studies on KV growth, concurrency, proposal depth and draft-model size.
8SZkaiC1UC.claimed_gains: Dynamic pooling improves request-round processing rate by 50.4% over a physically disaggregated baseline and 72.6% over co-located execution on a four-GPU deployment.
8SZkaiC1UC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a practical inefficiency caused by different draft and verify batching needs, with concrete mechanisms for KV management and overlapped state preparation.
8SZkaiC1UC.main_concern: Evaluation scale is small (up to 8B on four GPUs, mostly simulation without communication costs), only rounds per second is reported, and novelty over existing disaggregated systems such as StarSD is not convincingly established.

s7mKg3JuI7.one_liner: SURE-Tagger builds semi-structured speech representations with explicit attribute values and abstention by integrating specialist observations through LLM reasoning.
s7mKg3JuI7.problem: Speech captioning models give inconsistent attribute coverage and ambiguous omissions, which hinders systematic analysis across recordings.
s7mKg3JuI7.method: SURE-Tagger builds semi-structured representations with explicit attribute values, supplementary descriptions and abstention under insufficient evidence, integrating specialist observations through language-model reasoning so conditions can be queried across datasets. Tag-Bench combines real recordings with agentically synthesized speech scenes and verified annotations, and the representations are used to build evaluation subsets and select fine-tuning data.
s7mKg3JuI7.key_idea: Fuse specialist speech-model observations with an LLM into a fixed schema where each attribute holds a value, a description or an explicit abstention.
s7mKg3JuI7.evidence: Tag-Bench with real and controlled synthetic speech across 29 dimensions, cross-dataset ASR error analysis, and one-hour fine-tuning data selection for Qwen3-ASR-1.7B from a separate candidate pool.
s7mKg3JuI7.claimed_gains: Highest scores on 25 of 29 evaluated dimensions for real speech and 24 of 29 for synthetic speech, and a 14.3% relative reduction in overall ASR error rate of Qwen3-ASR-1.7B under a one-hour fine-tuning budget.
s7mKg3JuI7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the semi-structured schema with explicit abstention addresses a real gap in speech captioning, and that the work tests downstream use through cross-dataset error profiles and data selection.
s7mKg3JuI7.main_concern: The gain is not isolated from the stronger specialist inputs versus the integration step, descriptive axes are scored by an LLM from the family that generated them, and methodological novelty beyond structured annotation is unclear.

tlcjadlctZ.one_liner: Builds synchronized reframings from real monocular videos via crop-and-resize camera intrinsics to supplement synthetic multi-camera supervision for video retaking.
tlcjadlctZ.problem: Video retaking models trained on synthetic multi-camera data struggle to preserve real subject appearance and motion (rapid movement, large displacements) because real synchronized multi-view recordings are unavailable.
tlcjadlctZ.method: CoFrame constructs synchronized reframings from real monocular videos and expresses the crop-and-resize as explicit camera-intrinsics conditions for conditional re-rendering. It also explores relative camera conditioning and paired flow matching to encode source-target camera relationships and jointly supervise synchronized target predictions.
tlcjadlctZ.key_idea: Treat crop-and-resize of a real video as a change in camera intrinsics, giving synchronized source-target pairs with explicit camera conditions that complement synthetic extrinsic-viewpoint supervision.
tlcjadlctZ.evidence: The abstract text is truncated; reviews describe quantitative and qualitative comparisons against baselines on DAVIS, scored with estimator-based metrics (ViPE, CoTracker, GIM) and a proposed Motion Magnitude Error.
tlcjadlctZ.reviewer_consensus: All three reviewers credit the cheap, practical use of real-video reframing as complementary supervision, and report clear gains over baselines in comparisons and visualizations.
tlcjadlctZ.main_concern: Real-video reframing yields only crop-style viewpoint changes and DAVIS has no ground truth, so the evidence rests on estimator-based metrics, including a Motion Magnitude Error that reviewers say needs stronger validation.

ZDN60qfSXS.one_liner: Estimates achievable visual-token-pruning performance by greedily selecting one shared token subset against auxiliary QA sets generated by a frontier VLM.
ZDN60qfSXS.problem: It is unclear whether current visual token pruning performance reflects an inherent limit or the weakness of existing token-selection algorithms.
ZDN60qfSXS.method: Pruning is cast as picking one shared visual-token subset per image under a fixed budget, optimizing a teacher-forced answer-probability objective on a finite auxiliary QA set with the evaluated VLM frozen. The authors build nested subsets greedily with QA mini-batch greedy (QA-MBG), which estimates token marginal gains from randomly sampled QA components at each step.
ZDN60qfSXS.key_idea: QA-MBG grows nested token subsets greedily, estimating each token's marginal gain from a random mini-batch of auxiliary QA pairs under a teacher-forced answer-probability objective.
ZDN60qfSXS.evidence: Reviews describe two VLM architectures (Qwen3-VL-4B, Gemma 4 E4B), nine benchmarks, multiple token budgets, and controls on QA overlap, generation protocols, and search strategies.
ZDN60qfSXS.claimed_gains: QA-MBG is both cheaper and more effective than full greedy, at one frontier-VLM call and approximately 0.5 (Qwen3-VL-4B) to 1.1 (Gemma 4 E4B) H100 GPU-hours (abstract is truncated before the accuracy numbers).
ZDN60qfSXS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnostic question is useful and that the searched subsets beat existing pruning methods at fixed budgets, showing that part of the pruning loss is recoverable selector error.
ZDN60qfSXS.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited because QA-MBG resembles existing mini-batch subset optimization, and generalization beyond the auxiliary-QA protocol to unseen question distributions is only weakly controlled.

m2lJd5vpWF.one_liner: Co-evolves a language-agent world model and policy, balancing real-observation supervision with policy-derived behavioral supervision to reduce behavioral mismatch.
m2lJd5vpWF.problem: Semantically similar simulated observations can still induce different policy actions (behavioral mismatch), and the mismatch grows as the policy keeps learning while the world model stays fixed.
m2lJd5vpWF.method: CoWISE lets the world model and policy co-evolve by leveraging each other's predictions, and adaptively balances real-world observational supervision against behavioral supervision derived from the current policy. Reviews describe a shared-parameter policy and world model trained with behavioral fidelity under GRPO.
m2lJd5vpWF.key_idea: Refresh behavioral supervision with the current policy during training and adaptively weight it against real-observation supervision, so the world model keeps tracking the evolving policy.
m2lJd5vpWF.evidence: Experiments across 8 benchmarks, with reviews citing policy-only, behavioral-fidelity, and test-time-simulation comparisons plus ablations (Table 2) on frozen supervisor, simulated training feedback, and fixed objective weights.
m2lJd5vpWF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a static world model drifting from an evolving policy is a real problem and that updating behavioral supervision with the current policy is a sensible fix evaluated on diverse benchmarks.
m2lJd5vpWF.main_concern: Ablations show the co-evolution components change policy-only performance by only about 0.1-0.3 points, with benefits concentrated in test-time simulation, and novelty over prior shared-parameter and behavioral-fidelity work is questioned.

gI40n3fdJ6.one_liner: Infers latent actions jointly from all cameras with a shared encoder and decoder; the VLA predicts them from one camera.
gI40n3fdJ6.problem: Existing latent action models infer the latent action from a single camera, so it can lose part of the physical change and carry camera-specific content instead.
gI40n3fdJ6.method: A shared transition encoder summarizes every available camera's frame pair, learned queries read all summaries before quantization, and one shared decoder must predict every camera's next features from the single latent action and that camera's first frame. The VLA then predicts the latent action from the primary camera alone, so no extra camera is needed at deployment.
gI40n3fdJ6.key_idea: Fuse all cameras' transition summaries into one quantized latent action before decoding, and force a shared decoder to reconstruct every camera's next features from it.
gI40n3fdJ6.evidence: Latent-action decoding error and readout stability under image perturbations versus primary-camera-only LAMs, plus policy success on the four LIBERO suites, LIBERO-10 camera-pose perturbations, LIBERO-Pro, and ALOHA experiments.
gI40n3fdJ6.claimed_gains: Lower action-decoding error and a readout more stable under image perturbations than primary-camera-only LAMs; highest average success among compared policies on the four LIBERO suites, LIBERO-10 camera-pose perturbations, and LIBERO-Pro, and highest observed success in six of seven ALOHA (the abstract is truncated at this point).
gI40n3fdJ6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using synchronized multi-view data only at training time, while deploying with one camera, is a practical, well-motivated design that beats the compared latent-action methods.
gI40n3fdJ6.main_concern: The primary-only ablation changes several factors at once (inputs, fusion module, reconstruction targets, loss weighting), so the benefit of joint multi-view fusion is not isolated, and novelty over MVP-LAM is incremental.

70mhG1dA8H.one_liner: Black-box contamination audit measuring how added context shifts generations at a few informative token positions.
70mhG1dA8H.problem: Existing contamination detectors need gray-box access, and black-box alternatives rely on full-sequence sampling or rigid heuristics that cost many inference calls.
70mhG1dA8H.method: A generation-based framework infers context-induced information gain from targeted token discrepancies under a query budget, using a policy that targets informative positions (selected via lexical overlap per reviews) instead of uniform sampling.
70mhG1dA8H.key_idea: The membership signal is concentrated in a few tokens, so query only those positions and compare predictions with and without added context.
70mhG1dA8H.evidence: Experiments across several model families with tests of fine-tuning, sampling temperature, and context selection, a formal argument for why sparsity helps, and an application to closed frontier models through commercial APIs.
70mhG1dA8H.claimed_gains: Reports higher black-box separation accuracy than baselines while needing about 3x fewer queries than uniform position sampling.
70mhG1dA8H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method works without token probabilities and that selecting token positions cuts query cost, with experiments across several model families.
70mhG1dA8H.main_concern: The main results may reflect distribution shift between compared datasets (for example StackExchange versus GSM8K) rather than training exposure, and a no-extra-context next-token accuracy baseline is missing.

fxaVy2jzvx.one_liner: Learns variable importance from a low-rank-plus-diagonal Mahalanobis kernel to select correlated variable groups in high-dimensional Bayesian optimization.
fxaVy2jzvx.problem: Axis-aligned importance scores used for variable selection in high-dimensional BO ignore how variables act together, so they fail when the objective is governed by correlated groups.
fxaVy2jzvx.method: CAVS fits a Mahalanobis kernel with a low-rank-plus-diagonal structure and derives variable importance from it, capturing correlations while avoiding the quadratic cost of a full metric. The paper proves a sublinear cumulative regret bound under an oracle-kernel assumption.
fxaVy2jzvx.key_idea: Score variable importance from a low-rank-plus-diagonal Mahalanobis kernel metric, which captures correlated directions with linear rather than quadratic parameter cost.
fxaVy2jzvx.evidence: Sublinear regret proof under an oracle-kernel assumption, rotated (non-axis-aligned) objective tests, and eight real-world benchmarks from 16D to 888D where CAVS gets the best average rank among the baselines.
fxaVy2jzvx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the low-rank-plus-diagonal kernel is a sound, practical way to model correlations cheaply, supported by broad experiments on real-world tasks up to 888D and kernel comparisons.
fxaVy2jzvx.main_concern: The correlation-aware claim is not isolated: the regret theorem assumes a fixed metric while the algorithm refits it every iteration, rotation tests rotate only the active block, and gains may come from added capacity.

hRyyO1Qi7q.one_liner: Benchmark of 100 reproducible coding tasks mined from four of the largest open-source repositories, testing codebase navigation by agents.
hRyyO1Qi7q.problem: Current repository-level coding benchmarks mostly draw from small codebases, unlike real development in much larger repositories where agents must navigate code under a limited context window.
hRyyO1Qi7q.method: Mines 100 reproducible tasks from four of the largest open-source repositories on GitHub, with mean per-instance source size roughly an order of magnitude larger than reference benchmarks, packaged as Harbor tasks. Five frontier models are evaluated under OpenHands and OpenCode, followed by trajectory analysis.
hRyyO1Qi7q.key_idea: Select tasks from very large repositories (14.8M to 148.2M tokens per a reviewer) so success depends on search and context management, then compare agent search behavior with other benchmarks.
hRyyO1Qi7q.evidence: Five frontier models run under OpenHands and OpenCode, with trajectory analysis of codebase searches and directories visited compared against other benchmarks.
hRyyO1Qi7q.claimed_gains: Best pass@1 is 47.6% under OpenHands and 48.6% under OpenCode.
hRyyO1Qi7q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it fills an important gap by testing localization, search and context management in large repositories, with tasks from real pull requests in reproducible containers.
hRyyO1Qi7q.main_concern: Validity is questioned: repository size alone may not indicate complexity, more searches do not show better capability coverage, and synthetic problem statements and test oracles lack independent audit, with only four repositories.

cfImU3X4f7.one_liner: Linear-time constrained decoding for LL(1) grammars using HMM surrogates that marginalize over a fixed look-ahead window.
cfImU3X4f7.problem: Steering a language model to satisfy a context-free grammar needs the probability that a continuation stays grammatical, and even with a tractable HMM surrogate, constrained generation for unambiguous grammars is cubic in sequence length.
cfImU3X4f7.method: Extends HMM-surrogate constrained generation from regular languages to LL(1) grammars, and develops CTRL-CFG, a linear-time approximation that marginalizes only over a fixed look-ahead window. A reviewer notes a #P-hardness result for unambiguous grammars that motivates the LL(1) restriction.
cfImU3X4f7.key_idea: Approximate the grammatical-continuation probability with an HMM surrogate marginalized over only the next k tokens of an LL(1) grammar.
cfImU3X4f7.evidence: Experiments on program synthesis and molecule generation; reviewers add regex and Spider text-to-SQL results compared against locally constrained decoding and unconstrained baselines.
cfImU3X4f7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is clear and substantive, with a principled LL(1) tractability condition and a cached decoding algorithm with explicit complexity, and that the fixed look-ahead idea is realistic.
cfImU3X4f7.main_concern: Gains are modest relative to cost: on Spider accuracy rises 1.34 points while latency goes from 26.11 to 40.59 ms/token and memory from 16.38 to 33.75 GB, and the approximation error is not isolated.

JdSRS0BDoS.one_liner: EEG-conditioned flow matching with a learned source samples parcellated BOLD activity, preserving cross-region covariance for fMRI connectivity recovery.
JdSRS0BDoS.problem: Per-region regressors and joint MSE decoders from EEG collapse toward the conditional mean and discard residual cross-region covariance, harming functional connectivity estimates.
JdSRS0BDoS.method: BOLDFlow models the conditional distribution of parcellated BOLD activity given EEG with conditional flow matching using a learned EEG-conditioned source. Sampled trajectories retain residual cross-region covariance, and repeated draws give ensemble spread as uncertainty.
JdSRS0BDoS.key_idea: Sampling from a conditional flow keeps residual cross-region covariance that mean-regression decoders discard, and repeated samples supply uncertainty without a separate head.
JdSRS0BDoS.evidence: Subject-disjoint evaluation on two simultaneous in-scanner EEG-fMRI datasets (NeuroBOLT and OpenNeuroSleep) spanning rest and sleep, with scaling to 512-component parcellations and recalibration of ensemble spread.
JdSRS0BDoS.claimed_gains: Measured-FC recovery improves from 0.428 to 0.584 (NeuroBOLT) and 0.340 to 0.528 (OpenNeuroSleep), and temporal correlation from 0.272 to 0.326 and 0.151 to 0.212, with scaling to output parcellations of 512 components.
JdSRS0BDoS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the covariance-preservation motivation is sound, FC recovery improves substantially over baselines on two datasets, and the experiments are extensive with subject-disjoint cross-validation and controls.
JdSRS0BDoS.main_concern: Practical value is limited: predicted BOLD time-series correlations remain low (0.326 and 0.212), outputs are atlas-level rather than spatially resolved fMRI, and few baselines are compared.

k6SyJnjjwv.one_liner: One flow-matching backbone with log-signature history conditioning supports both one-pass point prediction and iterative sampling across deterministic and stochastic PDEs.
k6SyJnjjwv.problem: Shared pretraining across deterministic and stochastic PDEs must handle both unique continuations and conditional distributions of futures under unobserved stochastic forcing.
k6SyJnjjwv.method: UniDynamic jointly learns point prediction and conditional generation in a flow-matching framework with a shared backbone conditioned on multiscale windowed log-signature history representations. The authors also build a paired benchmark with repeated-future DNS ensembles for conditional moments, marginals, and spatial fluctuations.
k6SyJnjjwv.key_idea: Multiscale windowed log-signature histories condition a shared backbone that runs in a one-pass prediction mode for deterministic PDEs and an iterative sampling mode for stochastic ones.
k6SyJnjjwv.evidence: A controlled Kolmogorov-flow experiment, 11 deterministic PDE subsets, three stochastic PDEs with repeated-future DNS ensembles, few-shot transfer to unseen equations, and ablations adding deterministic training data.
k6SyJnjjwv.claimed_gains: Competitive accuracy across 11 deterministic PDE subsets and the lowest lead-20 marginal energy distance among the compared methods on the three stochastic PDEs.
k6SyJnjjwv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation protocol is a strength, especially the repeated-future DNS benchmark and the broad set of datasets and baselines, and that unifying deterministic and stochastic forecasting is an interesting question.
k6SyJnjjwv.main_concern: The method section is unclear with undefined notation (log-signature encoding), the training recipe is under-tested (a one-seed encoder ablation, no isolation of gate, prediction, and flow losses), and the SPDE framing relative to forced neural-operator setups is unclear.

PawuLS3p2L.one_liner: Benchmark of 544 knowledge-graph-generated, verified questions with controllable candidate-set and constraint structure for long-horizon search agents.
PawuLS3p2L.problem: Building hard deep-search benchmarks depends on labor-intensive expert authoring to ensure factual validity and difficulty.
PawuLS3p2L.method: An automated pipeline samples tree- and graph-structured subgraphs from a Wikipedia-derived KG with 7.62 million entities, converts them to natural-language questions, and applies automated validation, difficulty filtering, and human review. KG structure controls candidate-set size and constraints and enables answer-uniqueness checks.
PawuLS3p2L.key_idea: Sample KG subgraphs whose candidate-set size and constraint structure set question difficulty, and check answer uniqueness across the whole graph.
PawuLS3p2L.evidence: 544 questions across seven domains evaluated under a standardized setup with several models and context-management strategies.
PawuLS3p2L.claimed_gains: Even the best-performing model reaches only 52.02% accuracy, successful DeepSeek-V4-Flash trajectories use 1.7x as many tool calls as on BrowseComp, and context-management strategies give at most a 6.8 percentage point gain.
PawuLS3p2L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the KG-based pipeline is well designed and cuts expert authoring cost, with clear presentation and solid verification (constraint checks, alternative-answer searches, human review).
PawuLS3p2L.main_concern: Scalability and the controllable-difficulty claim are weakly demonstrated (only 544 questions from 2,000 initial pairs, descriptive evidence), and mainstream agent harnesses are not evaluated.

b87zh47rMi.one_liner: SURD-Bench evaluates unified multimodal models on urban spatiotemporal cognition across Sensing, Understanding, Reasoning and Decision stages with eight tasks.
b87zh47rMi.problem: Existing benchmarks target general visual understanding or specific remote sensing tasks and cannot evaluate the unified understanding and generation abilities of unified multimodal models on urban remote sensing.
b87zh47rMi.method: Eight tasks are organized around four cognitive stages, built from in-house and public datasets through an AI-assisted curation workflow with human verification, with a unified evaluation framework for diverse text and image outputs.
b87zh47rMi.key_idea: Structure evaluation as a four-stage progressive cognitive chain requiring both open-ended text reasoning and conditioned visual generation (inpainting, mask generation, future-scene generation).
b87zh47rMi.evidence: Evaluation of 18 representative commercial and open-source multimodal models on the benchmark.
b87zh47rMi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the four-stage benchmark is comprehensive and valuable, covering both understanding and generation, with 18 models evaluated.
b87zh47rMi.main_concern: Evaluation validity is questioned: generation tasks use generic image metrics without a copy baseline, text tasks rely on an LLM judge (GPT-5-mini also writes the references), and overlap with existing benchmarks is not clearly justified.

3useo7znsf.one_liner: Training-free LLM-to-SNN conversion with a two-stage hybrid spike encoder and spiking square-root, exponent, and division units for nonlinearities.
3useo7znsf.problem: ANN-to-SNN conversion trades off representation fidelity, spike activity, and time steps, and nonlinear operations such as Softmax, RMSNorm, and SiLU are hard to realize with signed binary spikes.
3useo7znsf.method: A Two-Stage Hybrid Encoding Neuron keeps one membrane state across stages, using population-activity-constrained BinarySpike encoding for large-magnitude components and SingleSpike encoding for residuals. Dedicated spiking units for square root, exponentiation, and division compose spike-driven Softmax, RMSNorm, and SiLU, reusing pretrained ANN parameters.
3useo7znsf.key_idea: Encode large-magnitude activation parts with BinarySpike and the residual with SingleSpike in one neuron, and build nonlinear operators from spiking sqrt, exp, and division units.
3useo7znsf.evidence: Experiments on BERT and four LLMs measuring zero-shot accuracy and perplexity at T=44, with BERT comparisons to LAS and other conversion methods, ablations, and local error analysis.
3useo7znsf.claimed_gains: At T=44 the converted LLMs incur only 0.12-0.64 percentage-point drops in average (metric truncated in the visible abstract); a review notes the abstract also quotes a synaptic-computation ratio of about a third of the ANN.
3useo7znsf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper tackles both encoding and nonlinear operators and keeps near-ANN accuracy and perplexity across architectures and scales, with ablations supporting the hybrid encoding design.
3useo7znsf.main_concern: The LLM experiments mostly compare against the source ANN with no direct comparison to other LLM-to-SNN conversion methods, and the energy numbers are theoretical and cover only synaptic computation.

oIFSl9dna3.one_liner: Forecasts post-checkpoint learning curves by transporting mean and covariance while updating the feature frame with optimizer-induced motion.
oIFSl9dna3.problem: Existing learning-curve extrapolation ignores checkpoint model and optimizer state, and neural-tangent-kernel forecasts use coordinates fixed at the checkpoint that become inaccurate as features evolve.
oIFSl9dna3.method: A moving-frame predictor transports the checkpoint-conditioned mean and covariance and updates the frame with optimizer-induced feature motion, with theory splitting forecast error into irreducible minibatch stochasticity and avoidable feature-drift error.
oIFSl9dna3.key_idea: Propagate checkpoint-conditioned mean and covariance in a frame that moves with optimizer-induced feature evolution, instead of freezing features as an NTK approximation does.
oIFSl9dna3.evidence: Theory on irreducible state MSE that is locally linear in the horizon and avoidable drift error; experiments on MLPs and Transformer language models (including Pythia-1B) against several forecasting baselines.
oIFSl9dna3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the moving-frame formulation and the split of forecast error into irreducible stochasticity and avoidable feature drift insightful, with theory and experiments supporting it.
oIFSl9dna3.main_concern: Theory relies on restrictive local assumptions and surrogate processes, and experiments cover only small MLPs and shallow Transformers with limited evidence on larger models and longer horizons.

1KpIx2ATfN.one_liner: Recurrent reasoning models trained with winner-takes-all over parallel sampled trajectories, backpropagating only through the candidate closest to the solution.
1KpIx2ATfN.problem: Stochastic recurrent reasoning models gain from exploring multiple trajectories at inference, but nothing in training encourages exploration directly.
1KpIx2ATfN.method: xRRM refines multiple sampled neural states in parallel, evaluates the loss for all trajectories at each deep supervision step, and computes gradients only from the trajectory whose output is closest to the correct solution.
1KpIx2ATfN.key_idea: Winner-takes-all supervision across parallel sampled trajectories with learned perturbations, so losing trajectories receive no gradient and are free to explore.
1KpIx2ATfN.evidence: Combinatorial reasoning tasks including Sudoku-Extreme under approximately matched training FLOPs and five-run evaluations, compared with TRM, EqR, and URM per reviews.
1KpIx2ATfN.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; reviews cite 90.2% on Sudoku-Extreme with a single test-time candidate versus 67.8% for EqR.
1KpIx2ATfN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and shows a large Sudoku-Extreme gain under matched training compute with five-seed evaluation.
1KpIx2ATfN.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate winner-takes-all from learned noise, extra trajectories, or batch-size changes, and novelty relative to EqR, PTRM, and Forward XM is unclear.

a2yHtMwGxS.one_liner: Memory compression for world action models that segments history by robot-state cues into variable-length chunks sharing fixed learnable slots.
a2yHtMwGxS.problem: Long-horizon manipulation needs historical evidence at low memory cost, but keyframe selection can discard brief important interactions and fixed per-frame compression gives redundant observations the same capacity.
a2yHtMwGxS.method: Online robot-state cues organize history into variable-length segments. Once a boundary is causally confirmed, a shared set of learnable slots jointly reads the segment and prior context within the WAM's video Transformer layers, producing layer-wise key-value memories for action prediction, optimized by joint video and action prediction.
a2yHtMwGxS.key_idea: Allocate memory per robot-state-defined segment instead of per frame, compressing each segment into fixed learnable slots that write layer-wise KV memory.
a2yHtMwGxS.evidence: Nine history-dependent RMBench tasks and three real-world memory-required tasks on one Wan2.2-based WAM backbone, with ablations and a KV-cache size comparison against per-frame allocation.
a2yHtMwGxS.claimed_gains: Average success rates of 84.1% on nine history-dependent RMBench tasks and 71.7% on three real-world memory-required tasks, with a smaller historical KV cache than per-frame allocation.
a2yHtMwGxS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grouping redundant observations into adaptive segments is an intuitive, well-motivated way to keep evidence at lower memory cost, with a careful causal design.
a2yHtMwGxS.main_concern: The average gain over the per-frame MemoryWAM baseline is small (84.1% vs 83.0%), and segmentation relies on hand-crafted robot-state rules.

qe3k6r9hkc.one_liner: Decoupled supervisor that decides when to intervene in doctor-LLM consultations and what to advise, trained by selective on-policy distillation.
qe3k6r9hkc.problem: Doctor LLMs and clinicians show process drawbacks such as repetitive questioning, misdirected inquiry, omitted key evidence and premature closure, and fine-tuning the doctor LLM couples supervision to one model.
qe3k6r9hkc.method: MedPreceptor is a decoupled supervisor that selectively intervenes in multi-turn consultations while the Doctor LLM stays unchanged. It uses prefix-aligned supervision from a two-stage annotation pipeline that avoids future-information leakage, and DG-OPD, which routes teacher signals by intervention decision using trajectories from three Doctor LLMs and real doctor-patient dialogues.
qe3k6r9hkc.key_idea: Train a separate supervisor with on-policy distillation where teacher signals are routed by whether its intervention decision was correct, leaving the doctor model frozen.
qe3k6r9hkc.evidence: Several doctor models (including Baichuan-M2, Doctor-R1, GPT-5.6-Sol, DeepSeek and GLM), the CACI annotated-consultation benchmark and downstream MAQuE evaluation, compared against standard OPD and no-supervisor baselines.
qe3k6r9hkc.claimed_gains: not stated (the provided abstract is truncated; a reviewer cites an abstract claim of gains up to 10.27 points).
qe3k6r9hkc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the compact supervisor is practically useful, guiding arbitrary doctor models without fine-tuning them and giving relatively consistent gains across models.
qe3k6r9hkc.main_concern: Simple baselines (always-intervene, generic advice, other supervisors) are missing, and advice quality is judged by an LLM without clinical expert validation.

32Z0Mjr9HS.one_liner: TROVE learns a policy that predicts a coarse interval, then re-observes dense frames inside it to refine temporal grounding.
32Z0Mjr9HS.problem: Uniform frame sampling spreads extra observations across relevant and irrelevant video regions, while temporal grounding needs both global context and fine-grained local evidence at boundaries.
32Z0Mjr9HS.method: A shared policy predicts a coarse interval from sparse global frames, then refines it using dense local frames selected by that interval plus sparse global support. Training uses Grounding Initialization then Joint Re-Observation Learning with a Geometry-to-Metric Reward Curriculum and Contrastive Re-Observation Calibration.
32Z0Mjr9HS.key_idea: Train the first-stage interval prediction using both its localization reward and the reward gap between targeted and uniform second observations (contrastive re-observation calibration).
32Z0Mjr9HS.evidence: TimeLens-Bench (Charades, ActivityNet, and QVHighlights subsets), three model scales, and training, observation, and boundary ablations.
32Z0Mjr9HS.claimed_gains: With a 4B backbone, TROVE improves mIoU over the native model by 11.7, 8.5, and 4.5 points on the Charades, ActivityNet, and QVHighlights subsets, respectively.
32Z0Mjr9HS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coarse-to-fine re-observation framework is intuitive and well motivated, and that experiments across datasets and model sizes show consistent gains.
32Z0Mjr9HS.main_concern: The two-pass design adds training and inference cost that is not reported (frame counts only, no latency), and the novelty over coarse-to-fine sampling with GRPO and reward shaping is limited.

RlW0Jx9mSG.one_liner: Shows a transformation-recovery attack on SLIM's TEE-GPU LLM inference and defends with GateFlow's secure attention authorization.
RlW0Jx9mSG.problem: SLIM's transformed-domain propagation exposes reusable linear relationships during authorization, so multi-query inference makes its secret transformations identifiable.
RlW0Jx9mSG.method: The attack exploits these linear relationships to recover equivalent secret transformations without access to the original secrets. GateFlow redesigns the initial decoder execution to prevent recoverable intermediate representations during authorization, while later decoder blocks keep transformed-domain propagation without extra TEE involvement.
RlW0Jx9mSG.key_idea: Solve for equivalent secret transformations as a linear inverse problem from multiple queries; defend by hiding attention in the TEE during the first decoder block's authorization.
RlW0Jx9mSG.evidence: Experiments show accurate transformation recovery against SLIM from relatively few prompts and GateFlow's mitigation with practical inference overhead, with model recovery also tested under the existing GAME attack.
RlW0Jx9mSG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the transformation-recovery attack is clearly formulated and experimentally supported, exposing a concrete weakness in propagation-based protection, and that the paper is clearly written.
RlW0Jx9mSG.main_concern: GateFlow is not evaluated directly against the new recovery attack, SLIM already scores near random under the existing GAME attack, and generalization beyond SLIM and protection against functional extraction are unclear.

599JXe7y7w.one_liner: Learns multiple latent reasoning paths via routed projection experts and a diversity loss, then optimizes the policy with GRPO.
599JXe7y7w.problem: Existing latent CoT methods rely on a single latent condition or simple resampling and perturbation, which explores the solution space poorly and fails to capture functionally distinct reasoning directions.
599JXe7y7w.method: Stage one uses path-specific routers over a shared set of projection experts to build multiple input-dependent latent conditions, trained with answer-only supervision and a contrastive diversity objective against collapse. Stage two freezes the latent-path constructor, activates paths round-robin to give diverse conditions for GRPO, and adds a correctness-gated length reward.
599JXe7y7w.key_idea: Compose shared projection experts through per-path routers to produce distinct latent conditions, then cycle them round-robin during GRPO with a correctness-gated length reward.
599JXe7y7w.evidence: Five-benchmark average accuracy including GSM8K, ASDiv-Aug, and CSQA, compared with SoftCoT, Self-SoftCoT, and explicit CoT baselines at one and four candidates per reviews.
599JXe7y7w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-path latent framework is intuitive and well motivated, with strong improvements over multiple baselines and informative ablations.
599JXe7y7w.main_concern: It is not shown that the latent paths are functionally distinct rather than just geometrically separated, and comparisons do not isolate the paths' contribution from decoder GRPO training.

7zXjPo0YZ4.one_liner: Trains one RTL model to generate designs, build EDA checks, and revise with tool feedback, using staged SFT and PAPO.
7zXjPo0YZ4.problem: Existing RTL-specialized models often lack learned interaction with EDA tools or rely on separate generation and repair components.
7zXjPo0YZ4.method: A multi-task post-training framework with automatically constructed multi-task demonstrations and staged supervision from chain-of-thought to tool-integrated reasoning. Pattern-Aware Policy Optimization (PAPO) augments GRPO with correctness-gated rewards that favor concise successful checking while rewarding effective revision, and uses task grouping to preserve coverage across objectives.
7zXjPo0YZ4.key_idea: Reward correct RTL only when it follows a concise successful self-check or an effective revision, and group tasks during GRPO, so one model learns to use EDA tools.
7zXjPo0YZ4.evidence: CVDP, VerilogEval v2, and RTLLM v2 against RTL-specialized baselines and the teacher DeepSeek-V3.2, with ablations of SFT order, pattern-aware rewards, and task grouping.
7zXjPo0YZ4.claimed_gains: RTL-Interact-32B reaches 48.7% weighted Pass@1 and 68.9% Pass@5 on CVDP, surpassing its teacher DeepSeek-V3.2; the 8B model reaches 44.9% weighted Pass@1; PAPO reduces average tool calls by 63.8% while improving Pass@1.
7zXjPo0YZ4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that one model handling generation, checking, and revision removes separate repair components and gives consistent gains on CVDP, VerilogEval v2, and RTLLM v2 with fewer tool calls.
7zXjPo0YZ4.main_concern: PAPO's design is not isolated: the only reward ablation removes all terms at once, with no simple cost-aware reward control, and no error bars, multiple seeds, or end-to-end cost are reported.

2trVUOmfZz.one_liner: DIAL combines many LLM-judge comparisons with few human comparisons to remove position bias and calibrate rankings toward human preferences.
2trVUOmfZz.problem: LLM judges are sensitive to response order and, even after position effects are removed, can diverge systematically from human preferences.
2trVUOmfZz.method: DIAL jointly models judge-specific position effects, shared low-rank structure in position-debiased LLM preferences, and adaptive calibration of that structure toward the human preference target using limited human comparisons. The theory covers identification, adaptive estimation, and fixed-weight uncertainty quantification.
2trVUOmfZz.key_idea: Learn shared low-rank structure in position-debiased LLM pairwise preferences, then adaptively weight it against limited human comparisons to estimate human-aligned scores.
2trVUOmfZz.evidence: Controlled simulations and three human-preference benchmarks, with a collected set of over 410K judgments from 21 LLM judges in both display orders, plus theory on identification, estimation and uncertainty quantification.
2trVUOmfZz.claimed_gains: DIAL remains robust to unbalanced response order, achieves strong human-aligned rankings with limited labels, and adapts toward human evidence when LLM information is imperfect; the only numbers are over 410K judgments from 21 LLM judges.
2trVUOmfZz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory (identification and guarantees) is solid and the empirical evaluation is substantial and promising.
2trVUOmfZz.main_concern: The low-rank modeling choice is not justified or compared against alternatives such as prediction-powered inference (e.g., a Bradley-Terry PPI++ estimator), and simple baselines like AtC remain competitive.

nTh608IsKA.one_liner: Gated key adaptation aligns visual and textual attention-key distributions while regularizing within-modality geometry.
nTh608IsKA.problem: Multimodal language models can over-rely on text and underuse visual evidence when inputs conflict or contain distractions.
nTh608IsKA.method: MaLoRA combines modality-aware gated key adaptation with multi-kernel maximum mean discrepancy alignment. Gram-reference regularization preserves within-modality key geometry during alignment.
nTh608IsKA.key_idea: Align visual and textual self-attention keys with modality-aware gates and MMD while constraining changes to within-modality Gram structure.
nTh608IsKA.evidence: Evaluations span multiple MLLM backbones, image–text conflict and irrelevant-context tests, and POPE, AMBER, and HallusionBench, including parameter-matched LoRA comparisons.
nTh608IsKA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the attention-key intervention and broad experiments showing gains, especially on hallucination-sensitive tasks.
nTh608IsKA.main_concern: The evidence does not establish that key-space separation causes text-centric bias or that distribution alignment explains the improvements.

83Vy4UlbNb.one_liner: Measured pretrained spectra predict layer-specific LoRA update thresholds for the emergence of intruder singular directions.
83Vy4UlbNb.problem: LoRA updates can introduce nearly orthogonal leading singular directions associated with forgetting, without established layer-specific appearance thresholds.
83Vy4UlbNb.method: The paper derives critical update strengths through a rectangular spiked-deformation transform and an exact secular-equation characterization. It also turns thresholds into per-layer update caps.
83Vy4UlbNb.key_idea: Combine the pretrained spectral transform with LoRA update strength to estimate the threshold where new leading singular directions emerge.
83Vy4UlbNb.evidence: The study scans 9,840 layers across 18 adapters and seven base models, with out-of-sample checks on 53 further and six third-party adapters.
83Vy4UlbNb.claimed_gains: Threshold predictions fall within a factor of two on 82% of layers, combined edge evaluations reach 98%, and deployment classification achieves mean AUC 0.88–0.97.
83Vy4UlbNb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value theoretically motivated layer-specific thresholds and extensive validation across adapters and architectures.
83Vy4UlbNb.main_concern: The proposed spectral predictor and update caps show only marginal advantages over simpler spectral rules or uniform LoRA scaling.

ZBrQnODenS.one_liner: Frequency and attention calibration identify class-critical neurons that anchor feed-forward consolidation in pruned vision transformers.
ZBrQnODenS.problem: Activation-magnitude pruning can mistake strongly responding background tokens for evidence of class-critical neurons.
ZBrQnODenS.method: AC-Prune calibrates token activations using frequency stability and attention weights to select anchor neurons. These anchors guide FFN consolidation while multi-head attention weights receive low-rank regularization.
ZBrQnODenS.key_idea: Calibrate token activation contributions with frequency stability and attention weights before choosing anchors for FFN neuron consolidation.
ZBrQnODenS.evidence: Experiments cover five base vision transformers, three visual tasks, and four datasets, with component ablations and pruning comparisons.
ZBrQnODenS.claimed_gains: AC-Prune-derived vision transformers retain approximately 20%–40% of the base models' parameters while outperforming them in the reported class-specific evaluation.
ZBrQnODenS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize empirical support for calibrated importance scoring and gains under aggressive pruning.
ZBrQnODenS.main_concern: The comparisons and ablations do not cleanly isolate the calibrated scoring criterion from the existing consolidation and factorization pipeline.

KeTRXGXsTD.one_liner: Masking every occurrence of an information anchor lets diffusion models score reasoning support through reconstruction probabilities.
KeTRXGXsTD.problem: Generative verifiers can hallucinate and spend computation on reasoning segments that do not need checking.
KeTRXGXsTD.method: De-Anchoring identifies chains of repeated key information, masks all occurrences together, and scores their reconstruction probabilities from the remaining context. It uses these scores for candidate selection, error diagnosis, and reinforcement-learning rewards.
KeTRXGXsTD.key_idea: Simultaneously mask all copies of an information anchor and measure whether the remaining bidirectional context reconstructs it.
KeTRXGXsTD.evidence: Evaluations cover two models and tasks involving mathematics, multiple-choice reasoning, code generation, and planning, including Best-of-N selection and auxiliary RL rewards.
KeTRXGXsTD.claimed_gains: De-Anchoring achieves comparable performance with only 12.5% of the generative verification cost.
KeTRXGXsTD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple anchor-masking mechanism and evidence of verification gains across models and tasks.
KeTRXGXsTD.main_concern: Handcrafted, task-specific anchor extraction leaves generalization to open-ended or interactive agent trajectories unclear.

2Zw9n2mBDy.one_liner: Projecting gradients onto a feature-derived principal subspace suppresses directions assumed to be domain-specific.
2Zw9n2mBDy.problem: Feature-distribution regularization can leave parameter updates entangled with domain-specific directions.
2Zw9n2mBDy.method: The method estimates a shared principal subspace from aggregated uncentered second-order feature statistics. During backpropagation, it projects raw gradients along their input-feature dimension onto this subspace.
2Zw9n2mBDy.key_idea: Use principal directions of aggregated feature second moments to constrain gradient updates along the input-feature dimension.
2Zw9n2mBDy.evidence: The paper provides theoretical analyses and evaluations on PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, and TerraIncognita, including domain-label-free PACS experiments.
2Zw9n2mBDy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the method is clearly explained and supported by competitive domain-generalization experiments.
2Zw9n2mBDy.main_concern: High-energy feature directions need not encode shared task information, so the assumed separation from domain-specific directions remains unvalidated.

NxgL0hMAUH.one_liner: Sampling action-availability and rule posteriors guides planning with uncertain laws compiled from programmatic world models.
NxgL0hMAUH.problem: Partial world-model laws leave uncertainty about whether actions can execute and which competing action-effect rules are correct.
NxgL0hMAUH.method: ProPS compiles partial laws into planning rules specifying whole action effects, maintains separate availability and rule posteriors, and plans under samples from both. It updates the posteriors after observing outcomes.
NxgL0hMAUH.key_idea: Compile partial laws into complete action-effect rules, then sample separate availability and rule posteriors before planning.
NxgL0hMAUH.evidence: An exact variant has a Bayes-adaptive dynamic-programming optimality result for small complete-program libraries, and Crafter-OO comparisons use the same laws across controllers.
NxgL0hMAUH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of planning with uncertain symbolic world models and find the empirical results promising.
NxgL0hMAUH.main_concern: The setup, formal definitions, and component roles are difficult to follow and lack sufficient implementation detail.

eZZ1Hqm7Mi.one_liner: Hierarchical temporal and spatial rotary encodings address fixed-capacity world-model memory with content-conditioned spatial offsets.
eZZ1Hqm7Mi.problem: Long-horizon world models need compact spatial memory that remains useful despite accumulated localization drift.
eZZ1Hqm7Mi.method: HiSTFormer assigns local temporal RoPE and multi-periodic spatial RoPE to different layers, with content-conditioned address offsets. Fixed-capacity memory bounds KV storage and attention cost per step.
eZZ1Hqm7Mi.key_idea: Separate temporal and spatial attention across layers while adapting spatial addresses to content.
eZZ1Hqm7Mi.evidence: MemoryMaze and HM3D experiments evaluate long-horizon visual prediction, deeper Transformer stacks, and architectural ablations.
eZZ1Hqm7Mi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the hierarchical memory architecture and ablations supporting long-horizon prediction improvements.
eZZ1Hqm7Mi.main_concern: Unclear exposition of the architecture and component roles makes the necessity of the proposed spatial encoding difficult to assess.

DnAsidFUmk.one_liner: Two-point zeroth-order updates adapt only retained floating-point tensors while keeping quantized weights and metadata fixed.
DnAsidFUmk.problem: Memory-efficient adaptation of quantized language models requires choosing updateable parameters whose finite-query loss signals remain detectable.
DnAsidFUmk.method: QPZO collects retained floating-point checkpoint tensors into a quantization-preserved subspace and applies two-point zeroth-order updates there. Signal-to-Error Ratio analysis relates finite forward-loss differences to expected update alignment.
DnAsidFUmk.key_idea: Restrict forward-only optimization to existing floating-point tensors in a fixed quantized checkpoint.
DnAsidFUmk.evidence: Theory analyzes projected-gradient signal and SER thresholds; experiments cover Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-9B, GPTQ, AWQ, classification, and SQuAD.
DnAsidFUmk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent adaptation gains across models and quantizers without maintaining a fully dequantized trainable copy.
DnAsidFUmk.main_concern: Missing comparisons with first-order adaptation methods under matched memory constraints leave the practical efficiency trade-off unclear.

bl6czbuFst.one_liner: Expert-corrected explanation pairs supervise colonoscopy video QA through fine-tuning and selective preference optimization.
bl6czbuFst.problem: Correct colonoscopy answers can still rely on visual claims that contradict curated reference explanations.
bl6czbuFst.method: ColonExplainVQA retains original and minimally corrected explanations for video-question pairs. Qwen-Colon-8B applies supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization to Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, selecting modules through Colon Function Layer analysis.
bl6czbuFst.key_idea: Use minimally corrected explanations as paired supervision and apply preference optimization to selected model modules.
bl6czbuFst.evidence: A manually reviewed test set drawn from 7,962 video-question pairs across nine tasks and three public datasets compares nineteen baselines.
bl6czbuFst.claimed_gains: Qwen-Colon-8B reaches 79.15% answer accuracy and a 0.95% reference-contradiction rate among correct answers, compared with the reported 10.60% across evaluated general-purpose open-source models.
bl6czbuFst.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value preserving original and corrected explanations and the dataset's expert review procedures.
bl6czbuFst.main_concern: Reference contradiction does not measure all unsupported visual claims, so a low contradiction rate cannot establish full visual grounding.

nhPVET9bhV.one_liner: Text-only reasoning training followed by reduced-data audiovisual reinforcement learning separates reasoning improvement from perception recovery.
nhPVET9bhV.problem: Joint audiovisual reasoning training is costly, while correct single-hop perception does not ensure successful multi-hop reasoning.
nhPVET9bhV.method: The text-centric pipeline performs text-only supervised fine-tuning and RL for reasoning, then applies reduced-data native audiovisual RL to restore perception. Diagnostic studies examine perception-reasoning failures and local optimization relationships.
nhPVET9bhV.key_idea: Optimize reasoning with text first, then recover perception through a smaller native audiovisual RL stage.
nhPVET9bhV.evidence: Diagnostics and training experiments span data sources, model scales, and families, with nine reasoning scores reported for Qwen2.5-Omni-7B.
nhPVET9bhV.claimed_gains: The best text-only route raises the reasoning-score geometric mean by 25.83% with 56.6% fewer GPU-hours, text-synthesized data yields 21.01%, and refinement uses about 90% fewer input tokens while retaining 93.5% of the best text-only reasoning gain.
nhPVET9bhV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled perception-reasoning diagnosis and the systematic empirical study it motivates.
nhPVET9bhV.main_concern: The experiments do not cleanly establish that the staged training fixes the diagnosed reasoning bottleneck rather than benefiting from additional training or data.

SRD2vnmGQa.one_liner: Recomposable RGBA scene layers test how visual fragmentation changes VLM answer accuracy and evidence grounding.
SRD2vnmGQa.problem: Complete-image VQA benchmarks do not reveal how models use the same evidence when fragmented across inputs or turns.
SRD2vnmGQa.method: Layered-VQA decomposes each scene into ordered RGBA layers and annotates supporting, minimal-sufficient, and distractor evidence. Controlled presentation variants compare fragmented, complete, and recomposed scenes with question fragmentation.
SRD2vnmGQa.key_idea: Hold scene content and questions fixed while varying evidence-layer composition and presentation.
SRD2vnmGQa.evidence: The benchmark uses 93 scenes and 300 questions, eleven open-weight VLMs and two proprietary models, with 266,400 conversations and 2.61M cross-judgments.
SRD2vnmGQa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled presentation comparisons useful for studying fragmented visual evidence.
SRD2vnmGQa.main_concern: Layer fragmentation also changes visual token budgets, image format, and context, so the experiments do not isolate scene composition as the cause.

ZfY34Tc1wp.one_liner: Drift-adaptive KL regularization adjusts FTRL updates to delayed bandit feedback for stochastic and adversarial regret guarantees.
ZfY34Tc1wp.problem: Delayed bandit feedback complicates obtaining favorable stochastic and adversarial regret with the same FTRL algorithm.
ZfY34Tc1wp.method: The algorithm combines Tsallis entropy and KL divergence in a time-varying hybrid regularizer, adapting the KL learning rate to iterate drift. An additional skipping technique removes the need to know the maximum delay.
ZfY34Tc1wp.key_idea: Track feedback-induced iterate drift to adapt the strength of KL regularization.
ZfY34Tc1wp.evidence: Regret analysis covers stochastic and adversarial delayed bandits, with numerical experiments and a separate skipping analysis.
ZfY34Tc1wp.claimed_gains: The stated regret is $O\left(\sum_{i\neq i^\star}\frac{\log T}{\Delta(i)}+d_{\max}\sqrt K\right)$ stochastically and $O\left(\sqrt{KT}+\sqrt{D\log K}+d_{\max}\sqrt K\right)$ adversarially, with skipping giving $O(\sqrt{KT}+\sqrt{D\log K})$ adversarial regret.
ZfY34Tc1wp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate drift-adaptive KL regularization and removing a previous delay-dependent stochastic regret term within FTRL.
ZfY34Tc1wp.main_concern: The additional maximum-delay times square-root-of-actions remainder can weaken the bound and limits its advantage over prior methods.

2BiARKAD3q.one_liner: Persistent evidence memory and selective injection support recovery from information loss in language-model multi-agent systems.
2BiARKAD3q.problem: Existing multi-agent memory designs lack guidance on what to preserve and when to intervene after errors propagate.
2BiARKAD3q.method: The paper couples communication and environment feedback in an error-propagation law and analyzes recovery under information loss. RECOVER uses in-task persistent memory with precondition-based evidence and selective injection to support recovery.
2BiARKAD3q.key_idea: Preserve recovery-relevant evidence outside transient communication and selectively reinsert it when needed.
2BiARKAD3q.evidence: Theory, controlled error injection, and experiments across five benchmarks and three multi-agent frameworks evaluate recovery and token-storage costs.
2BiARKAD3q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing error reduction from information recovery and report consistent practical benefits from persistent memory.
2BiARKAD3q.main_concern: The theory motivates memory but does not establish that RECOVER's particular representation and insertion rules suffice for general task recovery.

L5PytBwMCx.one_liner: High-resolution references and frequency-aware diffusion jointly upscale generated images and refine generation artifacts.
L5PytBwMCx.problem: Reference-guided generation discards high-resolution details, while existing refinement and super-resolution methods address different parts of the resulting degradation.
L5PytBwMCx.method: RefGC-SR² reuses the original high-resolution reference during post-processing. A diptych-conditioned generator supplies aligned training triplets, and a frequency-aware diffusion transformer uses frequency-specialized experts and an adaptive loss.
L5PytBwMCx.key_idea: Train reference-conditioned refinement and upscaling on aligned generated-image triplets using frequency-aware expert processing.
L5PytBwMCx.evidence: Comparisons with super-resolution and refinement baselines, including fine-tuned ImageCritic and AdaRefSR, include changed image sources, input generators, and component ablations.
L5PytBwMCx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the triplet-construction pipeline for creating generation artifacts while preserving alignment with clean targets.
L5PytBwMCx.main_concern: Ablations do not directly establish the intended frequency specialization or separate it from increased model capacity.

pHhBlg59AU.one_liner: Gradient-norm trends and class-marginal entropy gate restoration to reliable checkpoints during continual segmentation adaptation.
pHhBlg59AU.problem: Long-horizon open-vocabulary segmentation adaptation can collapse, while stable methods or episodic resets sacrifice accumulated gains.
pHhBlg59AU.method: CAGA monitors gradient-norm trends and class-marginal entropy as label-free collapse signals. It selectively restores model parameters toward a previously reliable state while retaining useful adaptation.
pHhBlg59AU.key_idea: Use optimization and prediction-distribution signals to gate anchoring to a reliable adapted state.
pHhBlg59AU.evidence: A stress test evaluates eleven baselines across eight benchmarks over 150 adaptation rounds, with restoration and signal ablations.
pHhBlg59AU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad long-horizon study for exposing collapses that short evaluations miss.
pHhBlg59AU.main_concern: The comparisons do not establish the advantage of the proposed gates and anchors over simpler periodic or source-parameter restoration.

9DloiVhj1m.one_liner: Leave-one-out query projection disentangles shared demand from query-specific eviction risk for training-free KV-cache compression.
9DloiVhj1m.problem: Recent observation queries in KV-cache eviction share strong directional alignment that repeatedly reinforces the same historical tokens and obscures rarer query-specific retention evidence.
9DloiVhj1m.method: DisenKV uses training-free leave-one-out projection to remove each observation query's component along a shared direction estimated from neighboring queries. It aggregates raw query demand and query-specific residual eviction risk separately before applying a one-sided correction.
9DloiVhj1m.key_idea: Project out shared query directions via leave-one-out estimation and separately aggregate raw demand and query-specific residual risk for KV-cache eviction.
9DloiVhj1m.evidence: Experiments evaluate four model families from 3.8B to 24B across 16 LongBench tasks and RULER under matched non-layer-aware and layer-wise cache allocation budgets.
9DloiVhj1m.claimed_gains: At 20% KV retention across 16 LongBench tasks and four model families, DisenKV closes 32.5% of the remaining average gap to Full Cache over the strongest reproduced non-layer-aware baseline, while Layer-DisenKV closes about 44% under a shared layer-wise budget.
9DloiVhj1m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DisenKV is a practical, training-free plug-in evaluated across four model families and multiple long-context benchmarks with well-controlled norm and leave-one-out ablations.
9DloiVhj1m.main_concern: Reviewers argue that geometric query alignment is not causally shown to represent undesirable semantic redundancy, while absolute score gains are modest (~1–1.4 points) and tested mainly at 20% retention.

Q9pki3nH6t.one_liner: Terminal recurrent loops supervise intermediate loops on student-generated rollouts, with dynamic teacher refreshes during shared-parameter updates.
Q9pki3nH6t.problem: Post-training looped language models faces sparse rewards or dependence on external teachers and privileged contexts.
Q9pki3nH6t.method: LoopOPD distills a frozen terminal-loop policy into an intermediate-loop student using student-generated rollouts. D-LoopOPD refreshes the terminal-loop teacher as shared model parameters change.
Q9pki3nH6t.key_idea: Use additional recurrent computation as an internal teacher for earlier-loop predictions on the student's own rollouts.
Q9pki3nH6t.evidence: Ouro-Thinking experiments include three AIME benchmarks and two model scales, while theory gives sufficient conditions for simultaneous local improvement at two loop depths.
Q9pki3nH6t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find recurrence-based internal supervision well motivated and recognize mathematical-reasoning gains at intermediate and terminal loops.
Q9pki3nH6t.main_concern: Unequal rollout lengths and training settings confound comparisons and prevent clean attribution of gains to dynamic cross-loop distillation.

Ngz5mJAltH.one_liner: Matched base-versus-adapter image differences characterize LoRAs and train weight embeddings for text- and image-based retrieval.
Ngz5mJAltH.problem: Large text-to-image LoRA libraries are difficult to characterize, evaluate, and search through thumbnails and documentation alone.
Ngz5mJAltH.method: LoRA Scope measures CLIP-space differences between matched base and adapted generations, using VLM-guided prompts and a score of change stability, precision, and strength. LoCAL aligns weight representations with prompt and image embeddings for retrieval without query-time generation.
Ngz5mJAltH.key_idea: Represent each adapter by its induced CLIP-space changes and align its weights with diagnostic prompt and image embeddings.
Ngz5mJAltH.evidence: Experiments on a large real-world LoRA corpus evaluate characterization, agreement with human judgments, and retrieval, with comparisons against Stylus variants.
Ngz5mJAltH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see practical value in understanding and retrieving community LoRA adapters through their realized behavior.
Ngz5mJAltH.main_concern: The retrieval evaluation omits CARLOS, the closest-setting comparison identified by a reviewer.

eFi8mdUJNV.one_liner: Randomized skill injection within GRPO groups estimates individual contributions and guides evolving skill-library management.
eFi8mdUJNV.problem: Co-retrieved skills and task difficulty confound individual skill contributions, obstructing reliable lifecycle decisions as agent policies evolve.
eFi8mdUJNV.method: TrackRL independently randomizes skill injection within same-task GRPO rollout groups and aggregates within-group contrasts with reliability weights. These estimates track external skill utility and inferred model mastery to guide library lifecycle decisions.
eFi8mdUJNV.key_idea: Randomize each skill's presence across same-task rollouts and aggregate contribution estimates to track skill utility during policy training.
eFi8mdUJNV.evidence: Reviewers describe evaluations on multiple benchmarks that distinguish skill-assisted performance from skill-free capability.
eFi8mdUJNV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value randomized skill-level evaluation and evidence-guided management of skills whose usefulness changes during training.
eFi8mdUJNV.main_concern: Success without a target skill can reflect compensation by other skills, so the mastery estimate does not establish capability internalization.

LPxZxKhhSk.one_liner: A risk-constrained controller chooses between frozen VLM predictions and sparse-label interventions according to available semantic evidence.
LPxZxKhhSk.problem: Correct but semantically sparse target labels can degrade test-time predictions when they do not justify broad adaptation.
LPxZxKhhSk.method: STTI builds a preserved prediction hypothesis from complementary frozen VLM views and an intervention hypothesis from actively queried target labels. A regime-blind controller applies risk constraints when choosing between them.
LPxZxKhhSk.key_idea: Compare frozen and label-informed hypotheses, intervening only when observable semantic evidence supports sufficient benefit relative to risk.
LPxZxKhhSk.evidence: Evaluation spans 11 benchmarks with varied semantic complexity and annotation budgets, including matched-query comparisons and multiple VLM configurations.
LPxZxKhhSk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the distinction between label correctness and semantic coverage and find selective intervention supported by experiments.
LPxZxKhhSk.main_concern: The evaluation does not sufficiently isolate gains from selective intervention versus the stronger frozen dual-VLM preservation baseline.

uoY7qJgd6f.one_liner: A learned retrieval token gates driving knowledge access after gain-based supervision and cost-aware reinforcement learning.
uoY7qJgd6f.problem: Indiscriminate retrieval in driving VLMs adds latency and can introduce misleading knowledge into reasoning.
uoY7qJgd6f.method: ARDrive trains a [RAG] retrieval gate with pseudo-labels obtained by comparing retrieval and no-retrieval answers using an LLM semantic scorer. Reinforcement learning then optimizes the trade-off between reasoning accuracy and retrieval cost.
uoY7qJgd6f.key_idea: Train a retrieval-control token from measured answer gains, then refine its decisions with an accuracy-versus-cost reward.
uoY7qJgd6f.evidence: Experiments include BDD-X and DriveLM, adaptive retrieval baselines, human assessments, and closed-loop driving evaluation.
uoY7qJgd6f.claimed_gains: The abstract reports 14% lower reasoning latency and 34% lower RAG activation while improving driving reasoning.
uoY7qJgd6f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find adaptive retrieval relevant to driving and recognize reported reductions in retrieval use and latency alongside several task gains.
uoY7qJgd6f.main_concern: Different retrieval budgets across baselines prevent isolating retrieval decision quality from retrieval frequency and stronger response generation.

KMkcLWTOJH.one_liner: Policy-relative tests admit reusable action sequences only when they preserve task success and save policy decisions.
KMkcLWTOJH.problem: Frequently repeated and executable skills can still harm the particular policy that deploys them as single actions.
KMkcLWTOJH.method: PRA converts candidate skills into operator sequences executed by a deterministic binder. Held-out games test effect fidelity and decision savings under a task-success non-inferiority constraint for a frozen policy.
KMkcLWTOJH.key_idea: Certify each candidate against the deploying policy using effect fidelity and paired tests of decision savings subject to non-inferior task success.
KMkcLWTOJH.evidence: ALFWorld experiments compare recurrence-, executability-, and policy-relative selection and examine how admitted skills change with policy capacity.
KMkcLWTOJH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distinction between reliable skill execution and deployment value useful and supported by the ALFWorld results.
KMkcLWTOJH.main_concern: Individual skill certificates do not establish that the combined deployed catalogue preserves success when skills interact or overlap.

MA2RJA1yuw.one_liner: Physics-guided frequency decomposition feeds parallel structure and detail branches for self-supervised ultrasound despeckling.
MA2RJA1yuw.problem: Ultrasound denoising lacks clean targets, while single-stream self-supervision struggles to separate speckle from anatomical detail.
MA2RJA1yuw.method: PSDN uses adaptive frequency decomposition informed by acoustic priors to separate noisy images into subbands. Parallel low- and high-frequency streams reconstruct macro-structure and fine detail without clean reference images.
MA2RJA1yuw.key_idea: Decompose noisy ultrasound into prior-modulated frequency subbands and reconstruct structure and detail through separate branches.
MA2RJA1yuw.evidence: Experiments on three datasets include ENL and CNR measurements, physician scoring, and ablations of frequency decomposition and dual-stream reconstruction.
MA2RJA1yuw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical value of denoising without clean ultrasound targets and the experimental support for the proposed design.
MA2RJA1yuw.main_concern: Insufficiently specified, unmatched baseline capacity and training budgets prevent attributing gains to the physics-guided dual-stream design.

I4lstuqzEx.one_liner: Persistent simulated organizations generate contextual professional tasks, review feedback, and trajectories for agent evaluation and training.
I4lstuqzEx.problem: Professional agent work depends on accumulated artifacts, decisions, and feedback that isolated task generation does not capture.
I4lstuqzEx.method: OfficeTown initializes organizations from natural-language descriptions, with members coordinating assignments and reviewing assistant deliverables under role-based permissions. Persistent artifacts and unresolved matters shape later work, which becomes executable evaluation and learning resources.
I4lstuqzEx.key_idea: Generate new assignments from continuing organizational state, preserving artifacts, decisions, permissions, and review feedback across tasks.
I4lstuqzEx.evidence: OfficeTown Bench contains 406 tasks and 4,836 criteria from 23 organizations across eight domains, with frontier-model evaluations and Qwen3.5-9B training transfer tests including GDPval.
I4lstuqzEx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the professional-work benchmark and training resources, including evidence of transfer to external benchmarks.
I4lstuqzEx.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate persistent organizational simulation from simpler task generation with matched data and training budgets.

vzn9mvMuJq.one_liner: Intent-OPSD distills active-task supervision from a frozen teacher into students processing dialogues with rejected or superseded requirements.
vzn9mvMuJq.problem: Language models can treat mentioned changes as active requirements even after users reject or replace them.
vzn9mvMuJq.method: Intent-Eval controls proposals and user decisions across multi-turn tasks. Intent-OPSD initializes teacher and student from one model, using a frozen teacher's decision-matched complete task to supervise the student on the full dialogue.
vzn9mvMuJq.key_idea: Train on full dialogues using teacher supervision generated from the complete task that matches the user's final decision.
vzn9mvMuJq.evidence: Intent-Eval spans tool actions, code, databases, and mathematics, with neutral, retained, revised, and matched single-turn controls.
vzn9mvMuJq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the focused intent-tracking question and controlled comparisons of acceptance, rejection, and neutral dialogue.
vzn9mvMuJq.main_concern: The rejection-specific effect and its improvement are insufficiently separated from general multi-turn degradation, particularly without stronger repeated-trial evidence.

qpycp8oJns.one_liner: LatentWeave jointly trains a compressor and low-rank residual adapter to make history-memory representations usable by frozen language models.
qpycp8oJns.problem: Preserving information through soft-token compression does not ensure a frozen target model can use the compressed representations effectively.
qpycp8oJns.method: LatentWeave applies nonlinear, content-dependent residual corrections to the entire history-memory prefix, including uncompressed segments. Target-derived KV and attention supervision initialize the adapter before joint compressor-adapter refinement through the frozen target.
qpycp8oJns.key_idea: Jointly adapt compressed and uncompressed history embeddings with a shared low-rank residual correction trained through the frozen target model.
qpycp8oJns.evidence: A predictive-log-loss decomposition and LongMemEval experiments assess Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3.5-4B, and Qwen3.8-27B, including fixed-compressor ablations.
qpycp8oJns.claimed_gains: On LongMemEval, accuracy exceeds the uncompressed Qwen3-8B target across nominal assistant compression factors from 8× to 256× while end-to-end inference latency falls by 39.3--49.5%.
qpycp8oJns.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating compression-induced information loss from predictive mismatch in how frozen models use memory.
qpycp8oJns.main_concern: The comparison with unadapted raw context does not isolate compression benefits from the additional answer supervision and representation adaptation.

S8WMD4JP5Q.one_liner: SMoRe retrieves and geometrically verifies past observations to revise long-horizon estimates from frozen geometry models.
S8WMD4JP5Q.problem: Windowed geometry predictions accumulate alignment errors, while streaming models cannot revise earlier estimates when new evidence contradicts them.
S8WMD4JP5Q.method: SMoRe adds external memory that associates spatial location with observations. It retrieves history, verifies agreement with new geometric evidence, and revises stored poses and scene structure without changing backbone weights.
S8WMD4JP5Q.key_idea: Associate spatial context with observations in revisable memory, then use verified historical matches to correct past geometry estimates.
