S8WMD4JP5Q.evidence: Eight frozen geometry models are evaluated on seven datasets for pose, depth, and reconstruction, with long-sequence, resource, and retrieval/revision ablations.
S8WMD4JP5Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize broad practical compatibility and consistent long-horizon geometry improvements without fine-tuning.
S8WMD4JP5Q.main_concern: Most gains may come from conventional loop closure, and full-task matched comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the scaffold memory's additional contribution.

YP3CqEeU4S.one_liner: OneField aligns NeRF and Gaussian-splat representations through contrastive embeddings and shared field reconstruction for cross-format downstream transfer.
YP3CqEeU4S.problem: Format-specific radiance-field encoders cannot share downstream models between NeRF weights and Gaussian primitives.
YP3CqEeU4S.method: OneField maps both representations into a shared embedding space using contrastive alignment. A shared decoder enforces field reconstruction, allowing heads trained on one format to operate on the other and retrieve from mixed-format galleries.
YP3CqEeU4S.key_idea: Align paired NeRF and 3DGS embeddings contrastively while enforcing reconstruction through a shared field decoder.
YP3CqEeU4S.evidence: Experiments assess bidirectional classification, part segmentation, language tasks, mixed-gallery retrieval, and embedding-loss ablations on paired NeRF–3DGS data.
YP3CqEeU4S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize strong cross-format transfer across downstream tasks and useful mixed-format retrieval.
YP3CqEeU4S.main_concern: Invariance and robustness to representation-preserving transformations remain unclear, leaving uncertainty about whether embeddings capture fields or particular parameterizations.

p720ZNjvAx.one_liner: HorizonBridge applies horizon-conditioned residual translations to a shared time-series representation with adaptive patching and cyclical embeddings.
p720ZNjvAx.problem: Separate horizon-specific forecasting models increase training and maintenance costs while limiting flexibility across forecasting demands.
p720ZNjvAx.method: A shared base encoder preserves common temporal structure, and a horizon-conditioned translator generates residual representation adjustments. Adaptive patching follows local information density while cyclical embeddings encode periodicity.
p720ZNjvAx.key_idea: Adapt shared encoder features to each forecast horizon through conditioned residual adjustments, supported by information-density patching and periodic embeddings.
p720ZNjvAx.evidence: Theory examines horizon-dependent representations, and benchmarks including Weather, Electricity, and Traffic evaluate predefined horizons with component and efficiency analyses.
p720ZNjvAx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reusing an encoder across forecasting horizons and recognize the practical deployment motivation.
p720ZNjvAx.main_concern: The evaluation does not test unseen horizons or adequately justify the choice of source horizon, limiting evidence for general cross-horizon adaptation.

VOuROdbyLv.one_liner: CompAct composes single-object interaction predictions using body-part contact fields and classifier-free guidance to synthesize multi-object human interactions.
VOuROdbyLv.problem: Collecting training data for every combination of interacting objects does not scale.
VOuROdbyLv.method: A flow-matching model jointly generates body and object poses with contact/proximity InterFields. At inference, per-part fields weight proxy single-object interactions around a classifier-free body prior, while decoupled timesteps support editing.
VOuROdbyLv.key_idea: Blend single-object interaction branches using body-part InterField weights around an unconditional body prior supplied by classifier-free guidance.
VOuROdbyLv.evidence: GRAB and BEHAVE evaluate single-object synthesis, while HIMO tests fixed-object and joint multi-object generation with ablations.
VOuROdbyLv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value composing multi-object interactions from single-object training data through explicit body-part contact structure.
VOuROdbyLv.main_concern: Multi-object results are mixed and deteriorate against mTRiDi when object poses are jointly generated, weakening broad superiority claims.

wxCVY9gx2F.one_liner: LiveAnimate combines causal diffusion distillation with static and pose-retrieved KV sinks for bounded-memory streaming human animation.
wxCVY9gx2F.problem: Diffusion-based pose-driven animation is too slow for live interaction and struggles to preserve appearance over long streams.
wxCVY9gx2F.method: Teacher-forcing adaptation converts a pretrained bidirectional DiT into a block-causal generator, followed by block-wise self-forcing distillation. PR-Sink attention combines a fixed first block, a pose-retrieved historical block, and a rolling window to retain appearance context.
wxCVY9gx2F.key_idea: Keep a static appearance anchor and retrieve a historical block by pose similarity alongside a bounded rolling KV window.
wxCVY9gx2F.evidence: Reviews describe three-minute animation evaluations, cache-component ablations, video demonstrations, and end-to-end deployment analysis on a 14B DiT system.
wxCVY9gx2F.claimed_gains: The abstract reports reducing the sampling budget to three steps while keeping memory and per-block latency constant with stream duration.
wxCVY9gx2F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize sustained appearance quality during long streaming generation and the usefulness of pose-based historical retrieval.
wxCVY9gx2F.main_concern: Video demonstrations retain motion and visual artifacts that limit evidence of consistently natural animation.

vCK9KqAnV2.one_liner: Multi-projection packing balances Gaussian watermark carriers, while complementary-pair modulation coordinates embedding updates to limit rendering interference.
vCK9KqAnV2.problem: The supplied abstract targets spatially concentrated watermark carriers, whereas the title and reviews address ambiguous targets in surrogate-based watermark attacks.
vCK9KqAnV2.method: The abstract's MPP-GS assigns Gaussians multiple candidate UV-grid destinations and coordinates parent–auxiliary pair updates for watermark embedding. This differs from the AACT attack discussed in the supplied reviews.
vCK9KqAnV2.key_idea: Assign multiple candidate UV destinations to each Gaussian, then distribute and jointly modulate parent–auxiliary pairs over the balanced carrier.
vCK9KqAnV2.evidence: The abstract evaluates MPP-GS on Blender, LLFF, and Mip-NeRF 360, while the mismatched reviews discuss AACT attacks using a fixed HiDDeN surrogate.
vCK9KqAnV2.claimed_gains: The supplied abstract reports carrier overflow falling from 17.75% to 0.08%, with 35.15 dB PSNR and 95.95% bit accuracy at 64 bits.
vCK9KqAnV2.reviewer_consensus: The supplied reviewers, discussing AACT rather than MPP-GS, recognize surrogate target ambiguity as a meaningful watermark-security problem.
vCK9KqAnV2.main_concern: For AACT, reviewers agree that a single surrogate and output-polarity-flip experiments insufficiently establish generality across decoder mismatch.

e8IpDdDQKN.one_liner: Candidate-level comparisons test whether historical similarity predicts forecasting utility across retrieval and augmentation interfaces.
e8IpDdDQKN.problem: Similarity-based retrieval assumes that historical segments resembling a query improve its forecast.
e8IpDdDQKN.method: The study holds forecasting backbones fixed and measures how often historical candidates help, whether similarity retrieves them, and whether usefulness transfers between augmentation interfaces.
e8IpDdDQKN.key_idea: Compare each historical candidate's forecasting utility against its similarity score and its utility under other augmentation interfaces.
e8IpDdDQKN.evidence: Experiments cover 24 settings with frozen forecasting backbones, including Exchange and ETT datasets.
e8IpDdDQKN.claimed_gains: The abstract reports 38.32--56.23% useful candidates and best-candidate gains of 24.56--71.01%, while similarity retrieval loses to random sampling in 83.33% of comparisons and cross-interface transfer yields negative gains in 55.56% of cases.
e8IpDdDQKN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the direct examination of whether similarity predicts useful retrieval in time-series forecasting.
e8IpDdDQKN.main_concern: Limited dataset diversity and experimental configurations constrain the generality of the conclusions.

HpnuHDtvwJ.one_liner: Population-wide task records and modification histories guide revisions to individual agents' harnesses.
HpnuHDtvwJ.problem: Parent-centered agent evolution leaves useful capabilities and diagnostic evidence from other population members underused.
HpnuHDtvwJ.method: Population-Centered Evolution distills population task records and modification histories into a population block describing recurring failures, complementary successes, and previous modification effects. This block guides revisions to a selected parent's harness.
HpnuHDtvwJ.key_idea: Distill outcomes and modification histories across the agent population into evidence that guides a selected parent's harness changes.
HpnuHDtvwJ.evidence: Matched-model comparisons against GEA use SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot, with held-out task evaluations and a parent-only ablation.
HpnuHDtvwJ.claimed_gains: PCE achieves 72.1% success on SWE-bench Verified and 96.7% on Polyglot, improving over a group-evolution baseline by 3.2 and 5.9 percentage points.
HpnuHDtvwJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find population-wide experience sharing reasonable and value the matched comparisons and held-out evaluations.
HpnuHDtvwJ.main_concern: Too few independent evolution runs leave the reliability of the reported gains uncertain.

EGeCtN2DNS.one_liner: Draft-plan citation scores select decision-relevant interaction spans for training-free compression of agent histories.
EGeCtN2DNS.problem: Growing interaction histories increase inference costs and dilute attention, while offline compression policies cannot adapt directly to evolving trajectories.
EGeCtN2DNS.method: FOCUS compresses interaction histories at test time by thresholding how often draft plans cite individual spans, retaining selected spans verbatim and adding defensive retention. It attaches to existing agents without offline data collection or fine-tuning.
EGeCtN2DNS.key_idea: Use citation frequencies in draft plans to select historical spans, with defensive retention of additional potentially necessary information.
EGeCtN2DNS.evidence: Evaluations span API and tool-calling, question answering, web tasks, and multi-turn dialogue, with counterfactual comparisons on OfficeBench and AppWorld.
EGeCtN2DNS.claimed_gains: FOCUS cuts peak context by up to 48% and dependency by 73% while improving task success by up to 8.9 percentage points over uncompressed execution.
EGeCtN2DNS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the training-free design as practical and straightforward to integrate into existing agents.
EGeCtN2DNS.main_concern: The evidence does not sufficiently establish that draft-plan citation frequencies track the spans that causally affect the main agent's decisions.

eR96v39azc.one_liner: Learning-rate sweeps map abrupt transitions between learning without forgetting and catastrophic forgetting during language-model finetuning.
eR96v39azc.problem: Single-setting comparisons obscure when continual-learning methods improve knowledge retention beyond well-tuned supervised finetuning.
eR96v39azc.method: The study maps learning-retention Pareto frontiers using learning-rate sweeps across finetuning and continual-learning methods, including two proposed geometry-based baselines. It distinguishes gradual tradeoffs that interventions can sharpen from regimes where baseline finetuning already avoids forgetting.
eR96v39azc.key_idea: Sweep learning rates to compare attainable learning-retention frontiers and identify abrupt forgetting transitions across methods and models.
eR96v39azc.evidence: Experiments cover nine instruction-tuned Qwen2.5, Llama-3, and OLMo-2 models and methods including EWC, MAS, MIGU, NanoAdam, KL regularization, and LoRA.
eR96v39azc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the systematic learning-retention comparison across model families and methods using controlled learning-rate sweeps.
eR96v39azc.main_concern: The proposed loss-landscape explanation for why forgetting cliffs emerge lacks sufficient experimental support.

3gogFGspDb.one_liner: Separate local and global visual conditioning combines with agent-refined prompts for real-world image super-resolution.
3gogFGspDb.problem: Generative super-resolution leaves the roles of visual evidence and semantic guidance implicit, limiting control over structural fidelity and synthesized detail.
3gogFGspDb.method: GRASP uses a diptych for aligned local evidence and a lightweight Vision-Context Bridge for global image context. An inference-time agent iteratively refines semantic prompts to guide detail synthesis in ambiguous regions.
3gogFGspDb.key_idea: Route local evidence through diptych completion, global context through a vision bridge, and semantic detail guidance through iteratively refined prompts.
3gogFGspDb.evidence: Experiments cover multiple real-world super-resolution benchmarks, including DRealSR and RealLR200, with human preference and fidelity assessments.
3gogFGspDb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful separation of conditioning sources and evidence of competitive perceptual performance.
3gogFGspDb.main_concern: The agent's contribution remains unclear without a compute-matched repeated-sampling and best-of-K selection baseline.

EfBuPUMfQ3.one_liner: Process metrics and controlled experience interventions diagnose how research agents frame solutions, execute experiments, and retain progress.
EfBuPUMfQ3.problem: Final task scores conceal research-process failures and do not show whether accumulated experience helps subsequent runs.
EfBuPUMfQ3.method: The framework evaluates Solution Framing, Execution, and Feedback Control using verifier outcomes and execution records. Controlled within-task and across-task comparisons test the effects of reusing experience.
EfBuPUMfQ3.key_idea: Measure intermediate research behavior and intervene on retained experience under matched conditions to distinguish process bottlenecks from final outcomes.
EfBuPUMfQ3.evidence: The study evaluates seven frontier models across long-horizon AI research and development tasks using repeated rollouts and controlled experience-transfer protocols.
EfBuPUMfQ3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a concrete evaluation framework that examines research processes beyond final scores.
EfBuPUMfQ3.main_concern: The process metrics lack sufficient construct validation and sensitivity analysis to establish that they measure the intended abilities.

wva13wlOMY.one_liner: Unifies language and image understanding and generation via flow matching over ordered continuous embedding hyperchunks.
wva13wlOMY.problem: Unified multimodal models either quantize images into discrete tokens—losing visual fidelity—or combine discrete autoregressive text losses with continuous image diffusion losses.
wva13wlOMY.method: Multimodal Flow represents both text blocks (fixed 8-token chunks) and images as ordered continuous embedding hyperchunks inside a shared chunk-causal backbone with modality-specific feed-forward networks. A single Flow Matching objective learns a continuous vector field across hyperchunks, predicting chunks in parallel during training and generating them sequentially at inference.
wva13wlOMY.key_idea: Trains a shared chunk-causal Transformer with a single continuous Flow Matching objective over ordered text-block and image embedding hyperchunks.
wva13wlOMY.evidence: Instantiated as MF-1 across 0.6B, 1.2B, and 1.6B parameter scales pretrained on 150B tokens and evaluated on GenEval, VQA/understanding benchmarks (GQA, MMBench), and captioning.
wva13wlOMY.claimed_gains: With 150B pretraining tokens, MF-1 achieves an average score of 82.8 across GenEval.
wva13wlOMY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the genuinely unified continuous formulation that handles multimodal understanding and generation with a single flow-matching objective and sampling procedure.
wva13wlOMY.main_concern: Continuous text generation requires many ODE/SDE steps per 8-token block (roughly 4x slower than autoregressive decoding), fixed chunk boundaries can split multi-token words, and language understanding benchmarks lag autoregressive LLM baselines.

8CyhoGNtCj.one_liner: Supervises flow matching in decoded perceptual feature space rather than VAE latent space to enable few-step generation without distillation.
8CyhoGNtCj.problem: Standard flow-matching models supervised with velocity regression in VAE latent space require 35-50 sampling steps and suffer from mean-seeking blurriness under coarse few-step integration.
8CyhoGNtCj.method: Perceptual Flow Matching (PFM) replaces VAE latent-space velocity regression with supervision in a perceptual feature space extracted by pretrained perceptual encoders on decoded outputs. This shifts the regression minimizer from mean-seeking to mode-seeking without requiring a teacher model or multi-stage distillation.
8CyhoGNtCj.key_idea: Computes the flow-matching training loss in a pretrained perceptual feature space over decoded predictions to induce mode-seeking trajectories suitable for 4-8 step sampling.
8CyhoGNtCj.evidence: Evaluated on text-to-image generation, image editing, and text-to-video generation benchmarks at 4-8 sampling steps.
8CyhoGNtCj.claimed_gains: Reduces required sampling steps from 35-50 to 4-8 while preserving generation quality.
8CyhoGNtCj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method conceptually simple, easy to implement without teacher distillation, and applicable across image generation, editing, and video tasks.
8CyhoGNtCj.main_concern: Reviewers note that perceptual losses for diffusion/flow models have been studied in prior work not compared against, and quantitative baselines are limited to older few-step methods (LCM, DMD2) rather than recent one/few-step flow models like MeanFlow.

1jLFlYBpy8.one_liner: Compresses dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting models using render-space observability for position quantization and trajectory-aware prune-or-merge reduction.
1jLFlYBpy8.problem: Post-training compression of dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting ignores the mismatch between attribute storage cost and rendered-image sensitivity, as well as when redundant primitives can be merged into persistent neighbors.
1jLFlYBpy8.method: ORDO-GS quantifies render-space observability (expected sensitivity of rendered images to parameter perturbations) to derive a high-precision position quantization prior while aggressively compressing appearance and temporal channels. For structural reduction, a no-fine-tuning probe selects between prune-only and delete-merge branches based on reconstruction importance and projected-trajectory compatibility.
1jLFlYBpy8.key_idea: Allocates bit precision via render-space perturbation sensitivity and selects between pruning and trajectory-compatible Gaussian merging using a lightweight probe.
1jLFlYBpy8.evidence: Evaluated on N3DV and SelfCap dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting benchmarks across multiple primitive budgets.
1jLFlYBpy8.claimed_gains: Improves PSNR over OMG4 by 0.30 dB at matched primitive counts.
1jLFlYBpy8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the rigorous quantization-sensitivity analysis and the well-motivated combination of trajectory-aware structural reduction with attribute-specific coding.
1jLFlYBpy8.main_concern: The structural reduction stage relies on gradient/footprint proxies rather than the formal observability metric, and empirical PSNR gains over OMG4 on N3DV shrink to noise levels (0.08 dB) at larger primitive budgets.

hD0fRFVBdB.one_liner: Maintains event history and saved solution states to update and warm-start multi-objective optimization programs across evolving natural-language requests.
hD0fRFVBdB.problem: Operational optimization plans must adapt to changing natural-language requirements over time while preserving user-specified past commitments and deciding whether to warm-start solvers from prior solutions.
hD0fRFVBdB.method: MAPLE translates natural-language planning problems into a typed program interface solved by numerical and evolutionary solvers. Across sequential updates, it consults an event history and saved plan to enforce preserved decisions as constraints and selectively reuses prior solution populations to initialize the updated search.
hD0fRFVBdB.key_idea: Separates historical event logs for constraint preservation from saved solver populations for selective warm-starting when revising optimization programs across multi-turn language updates.
hD0fRFVBdB.evidence: Evaluated on the newly introduced NLDO benchmark consisting of 15 planning tasks each followed by 12 natural-language updates across five optimization domains.
hD0fRFVBdB.claimed_gains: Completes all 15 NLDO task sequences with a mean online single-objective quality of 0.951 and a mean Pareto hypervolume ratio of 0.875.
hD0fRFVBdB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formulating live dynamic optimization over multi-turn natural-language requirement updates and separating commitment preservation from solver warm-starting is practical and well-designed.
hD0fRFVBdB.main_concern: The evaluation is limited to 15 synthetic trajectories co-designed with the system, baselines regenerate solver code from scratch without access to the same evolutionary state warm-starting, and generated code occasionally misformulates physical constraints.

MtTWQDzv0e.one_liner: Guides scientific idea generation by retrieving successor limitation-strategy transitions from analogous historical research trajectories in other topics.
MtTWQDzv0e.problem: Automated scientific idea generation methods construct literature chains only within the target topic, leading to incremental ideas rather than transferring innovation patterns from other fields.
MtTWQDzv0e.method: CoI-Pro abstracts historical research trajectories across topics into sequences of transitions decomposed into limitation and strategy pairs. Given a target topic's current research trajectory, it retrieves similar historical trajectory prefixes from other topics and adapts their successor innovations to ground new scientific ideas.
MtTWQDzv0e.key_idea: Decomposes historical research progressions into limitation-strategy transitions and retrieves the successor step of analogous cross-topic trajectories to guide idea generation.
MtTWQDzv0e.evidence: Evaluated using three independent LLM judges in order-reversed pairwise comparisons, human evaluation studies, and component ablations against ideation baselines.
MtTWQDzv0e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retrieving what happened next in analogous cross-domain research trajectories via structured limitation-strategy transitions is an intuitive and clearly presented approach.
MtTWQDzv0e.main_concern: Reviewers find the conceptual advance incremental over Chain-of-Ideas (CoI Agent), note the lack of a token-matched baseline prompted to infer trajectories on the fly, and point out heavy reliance on LLM pairwise judges.

dRjFFUs2oU.one_liner: Alternates supervised fine-tuning on rubric-guided self-generated tool trajectories with unhinted reinforcement learning to internalize rubric guidance into research agents.
dRjFFUs2oU.problem: Using a research rubric only as a scalar reward leaves its instructional content unused for training agents that act without rubric hints.
dRjFFUs2oU.method: Rubric-guided self-distillation (RSD) uses criterion-level feedback to select weak queries, generates tool trajectories with targeted rubric guidance using the current policy, and filters demonstrations by a reward threshold. The agent then learns these trajectories under the original unhinted prompt in supervised phases interleaved with fresh-policy reinforcement learning.
dRjFFUs2oU.key_idea: Generates reward-filtered tool trajectories with targeted rubric guidance and trains on them under unhinted prompts in supervised phases interleaved with reinforcement learning.
dRjFFUs2oU.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-8B, 14B, and 32B across ResearchQA, DeepResearch Bench, DeepResearch Bench II, and LSB against rubric-based GRPO.
dRjFFUs2oU.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-8B, RSD improves over rubric-based GRPO by 14.23, 7.61, and 2.84 score points on ResearchQA, DeepResearch Bench, and DeepResearch Bench II, improves LSB from 26.04 to 28.79, and achieves RQA gains over GRPO of 15.07 and 14.47 points at 14B and 32B.
dRjFFUs2oU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the training framework is practical, clearly motivated, and delivers consistent empirical improvements across multiple research benchmarks and model scales.
dRjFFUs2oU.main_concern: Reviewers find the methodological contribution incremental relative to closely related prior work such as RuscaRL, STaR, and EvolveSearch, and note that SFT alone captures most of the gains.

xuJym90sgB.one_liner: Greedily selects KV-cache entries by utility-weighted marginal coverage in key space to reduce redundancy under low cache budgets.
xuJym90sgB.problem: Under tight budgets, static top-k KV cache selection in large vision-language models can favor overlapping content and leave complementary answer details insufficiently represented.
xuJym90sgB.method: FactorKV constructs a pool of high-scoring candidates using a host compressor's budget, protected positions, and utility scores, then greedily selects candidates that provide the greatest utility-weighted marginal coverage of the compressible history in key space. After each selection, it updates represented content so well-covered historical positions contribute less to subsequent gains.
xuJym90sgB.key_idea: Greedily selects KV cache entries by updating each candidate's value after every selection based on utility-weighted marginal coverage in pre-RoPE key space.
xuJym90sgB.evidence: Integrated with existing host compressors including SnapKV, PyramidKV, AdaKV, and SparseMM across multiple backbones and benchmarks including LongBench.
xuJym90sgB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that updating candidate values based on already covered content targets a real failure mode of one-pass top-k selection and integrates cleanly without retraining.
xuJym90sgB.main_concern: Reviewers question whether key cosine similarity reliably implies semantic coverage rather than redundancy, and note that gains are inconsistent across host methods, budgets, and LongBench.

S3ukuEfenO.one_liner: Compresses recurrent states in gated delta-rule linear attention via low-rank factorization and online subspace-aware updates for high-concurrency inference.
S3ukuEfenO.problem: Maintaining dense recurrent state tables per layer and head for every active sequence in gated delta-rule linear attention causes memory usage and bandwidth traffic to grow linearly with concurrency.
S3ukuEfenO.method: FReS is a training-free inference method that uses low-rank matrix factorization to compactly represent recurrent states based on their low effective ranks. It maintains states during incremental decoding via online subspace-aware updates combining factorized rank-one updates with randomized subspace approximation.
S3ukuEfenO.key_idea: Represents dense recurrent attention states via low-rank matrix factorization maintained online through subspace-aware incremental updates during decoding.
S3ukuEfenO.evidence: Evaluated on 27B–48B-scale Gated DeltaNet and Kimi Delta Attention models (including Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) across RULER, LongBench, MMLU-Pro, GPQA-Diamond, and high-concurrency serving workloads.
S3ukuEfenO.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 1.91x the throughput of the dense-state baseline under high concurrency while largely preserving dense-state quality.
S3ukuEfenO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the training-free compression method is supported by spectral analysis of recurrent states and achieves substantial serving throughput gains at high concurrency.
S3ukuEfenO.main_concern: Reviewers note noticeable accuracy degradation on longer generation and reasoning benchmarks such as MMLU-Pro and GPQA-Diamond, alongside limited algorithmic novelty beyond standard low-rank techniques.

qFLgJL8LRX.one_liner: Uses a shared resolution-lifted outcome value function to jointly guide latent refinement and token commitment in hybrid AR-diffusion language models.
qFLgJL8LRX.problem: Autoregressive-diffusion hybrid language models combine revisable latent refinement with irreversible token realization, making it difficult for reinforcement learning post-training to assign outcome credit across both decision types.
qFLgJL8LRX.method: ReLPO learns a Resolution-Lifted Outcome Value (RLOV) soft potential over partially resolved states from completed rollouts and terminal verifier rewards using a consistency relation across refinement and resolution transitions. A coupled policy improvement operator uses this shared potential to coordinate continuous latent refinement and discrete autoregressive token realization.
qFLgJL8LRX.key_idea: Propagates terminal rewards through a shared soft value potential spanning both latent refinement and token commitment transitions in hybrid autoregressive-diffusion generation.
qFLgJL8LRX.evidence: Compared against eight baselines including GRPO and TraDo on a shared backbone at matched training compute.
qFLgJL8LRX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that credit assignment across latent refinement and irreversible token commitment is a well-motivated problem and that using a single shared value potential provides a coherent solution.
qFLgJL8LRX.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the formulation reduces to standard KL-regularized control tilted by a reference-policy value estimate, incurs extra GPU memory overhead from a separate backbone critic, and depends on reference policy coverage.

AzyMEGzxFy.one_liner: Combines variational information bottleneck purification, source-memory priors, and entropy-guided mixup for unsupervised domain adaptation in whole-slide image classification.
AzyMEGzxFy.problem: Applying general unsupervised domain adaptation to gigapixel whole-slide images often causes negative transfer because aggregated slide representations entangle domain confounders with diagnostic semantics and exacerbate pseudo-label bias.
AzyMEGzxFy.method: SMART jointly optimizes across feature, label, and distribution dimensions for cross-institutional WSI classification. It filters domain confounders via a convergence-aware variational information bottleneck, refines pseudo-labels using retrieved non-parametric source priors, and handles asymmetric shifts with an entropy-guided cross-difficulty latent mixup strategy.
AzyMEGzxFy.key_idea: Purifies slide representations with a convergence-aware variational information bottleneck while refining pseudo-labels via source memory retrieval and entropy-guided cross-difficulty mixup.
AzyMEGzxFy.evidence: Evaluated across multiple diseases, binary and five-class tasks, bidirectional transfers including CPTAC-NSCLC to TCGA-NSCLC and EBRAINS, two pathology foundation models, and attention-, transformer-, and graph-based MIL backbones.
AzyMEGzxFy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad empirical evaluation across multiple clinical cohorts, foundation models, and MIL backbones, as well as the practical relevance of cross-institutional WSI adaptation.
AzyMEGzxFy.main_concern: Reviewers note that many baselines collapse to single-class predictions on the main transfer task and that ablations show a standard static variational information bottleneck already accounts for most of the gain.

R1co80WXfa.one_liner: Selects and compiles offline-mined reusable harness primitives into task-specific LLM agent harnesses at test time without generating code.
R1co80WXfa.problem: A single fixed agent harness is suboptimal across heterogeneous tasks, while generating custom harness code per task introduces high generation costs, debugging overhead, and execution risks.
R1co80WXfa.method: The authors mine reusable Harness Primitives with explicit application scopes and composition contracts offline from failed task trajectories. At test time, STITCH selects appropriate primitives based on task information and compiles them into a task-specific harness without synthesizing or repairing mechanism code.
R1co80WXfa.key_idea: Separates offline mining of reusable harness primitives with composition contracts from test-time primitive selection and compilation into task-specific agent harnesses.
R1co80WXfa.evidence: Evaluated on 100 SWE-bench tasks and 45 Terminal-Bench tasks across multiple actor models.
R1co80WXfa.claimed_gains: Boosts task success rates by up to 12 points over fixed harnesses.
R1co80WXfa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating offline primitive validation from online selection and composition is a practical design that avoids the instability and cost of test-time harness code generation.
R1co80WXfa.main_concern: Reviewers find the evaluation limited in sample size and missing direct comparisons against closer adaptive baselines such as conditional fixed pipelines, TTHE, or HarnessX.

LOpTNnUxFm.one_liner: Traces backward dependency cones from requested logits and future KV states to skip redundant prefill operations in local-attention decoders.
LOpTNnUxFm.problem: Standard prefill in local-attention decoders computes intermediate representations across all layers and tokens even when many positions cannot affect the requested prompt logits or future decoding states.
LOpTNnUxFm.method: Cache Complete Cone Prefill (C3P) traces dependencies backward from the requested prompt logits and the cached KV state read by subsequent decoding, then executes only the minimal dependency cone. The authors prove exact reproduction in real arithmetic and derive closed-form token processing counts per layer as a function of prompt length, window size, and model depth.
LOpTNnUxFm.key_idea: Computes only the backward causal dependency cone of operations needed to produce requested prompt logits and local-attention KV cache entries for future decoding.
LOpTNnUxFm.evidence: Proven minimal among deletion-only schedules in real arithmetic and evaluated on BF16 Mistral-7B and synthetic FP32 local decoders on an A100 GPU against a FlashAttention-2 baseline with final-layer slicing.
LOpTNnUxFm.claimed_gains: Reduces BF16 Mistral-7B prefill latency by up to 10.6% over a FlashAttention-2 baseline with final-layer slicing, and achieves up to 10.65x speedup and 80.30% lower peak allocated memory on synthetic FP32 local decoders.
LOpTNnUxFm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing prefill acceleration as backward dependency cone slicing is mathematically clean, technically sound, and training-free.
LOpTNnUxFm.main_concern: Reviewers note that the method relies on strict local-attention windows, yielding modest gains (up to 10.6%) on real models like Mistral-7B and limited applicability to modern frontier LLMs that include global attention layers.

bJ16PBKfss.one_liner: Demonstrates that autoregressive genome language models abruptly compress hidden representations in late blocks, improving next-nucleotide prediction while degrading biological readout.
bJ16PBKfss.problem: Autoregressive genome language models assume that optimizing next-nucleotide prediction yields hidden representations from which biological annotations can be easily read out at the final layer.
bJ16PBKfss.method: The authors analyze layerwise hidden-state geometry and linear probe decodability across five autoregressive genome language models from three families, including Evo 2 (7B and 40B). They perform principal-direction truncation, module perturbation, and late-block retraining interventions to test the trade-off between next-nucleotide prediction and biological readout.
bJ16PBKfss.key_idea: Identifies an abrupt mid-network dimensionality concentration transition and uses directional truncation and retraining interventions to separate next-base prediction from linear biological readout.
bJ16PBKfss.evidence: Evaluated across five autoregressive genomic models from three families, including Evo 2 7B and 40B, using linear probes on BEND gene-structure and phyloP conservation tasks plus directional truncation and retraining interventions.
bJ16PBKfss.claimed_gains: Keeping only 16 of the 4,096 hidden-state directions in Evo 2 after the transition leaves next-nucleotide prediction intact while lowering probe readout.
bJ16PBKfss.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the thorough geometric and layerwise empirical analysis showing actionable guidance for selecting intermediate blocks over final layers in Evo 2.
bJ16PBKfss.main_concern: Reviewers note that the practical finding that intermediate layers outperform final layers for downstream genomic tasks was already documented in prior work such as Nucleotide Transformer and the original Evo 2 paper.

I0mIOOA0M1.one_liner: Unifies subtask termination and adaptive action-chunk prefix selection into a single candidate ranking for hierarchical Vision-Language-Action manipulation.
I0mIOOA0M1.problem: Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action systems typically evaluate subtask termination and action-chunk execution length in separate pathways, ignoring their mutual dependence at re-observation points.
I0mIOOA0M1.method: SparkVLA formulates subtask stopping and action-prefix length selection as a single ranking where a Stop option competes directly against all candidate action-prefix lengths using offline ordinal preferences. It pairs an Anchor-Conditioned Context Encoding module that caches subtask onset memory for visual-token pruning with a Stop-Aware Action-Prefix Selection head that scores candidates via self-attention at chunk boundaries.
I0mIOOA0M1.key_idea: Ranks a subtask Stop decision jointly against candidate action-chunk prefix lengths in a unified candidate set supervised by offline ordinal preferences.
I0mIOOA0M1.evidence: Evaluated on RoboCerebra and compared against adaptive action-chunking baselines including DEHP, ACH, AQC, and AAC alongside factorized and categorical selector ablations.
I0mIOOA0M1.claimed_gains: On RoboCerebra, SparkVLA achieves 36.1% complete-task success and 47.12% transition completion.
I0mIOOA0M1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coupling subtask termination and action-prefix execution length into a single ranking addresses a practical interface problem in long-horizon manipulation and is well supported by controlled comparisons.
I0mIOOA0M1.main_concern: Reviewers consider the unified ranking formulation an incremental advance over recent adaptive action-chunking methods and point out missing operational details for proposal-to-supervision alignment and numerical discrepancies in reported tables.

nAdZPbUFPc.one_liner: Formalizes multi-turn LLM information leakage via per-turn mutual information and introduces an information-theoretic guardrail to bound adversary advantage.
nAdZPbUFPc.problem: Large language models lack sensitivity awareness in multi-turn interactions, allowing adversaries to infer protected data across multiple turns even when the target value is never stated outright.
nAdZPbUFPc.method: The authors define hop information leakage, a per-turn mutual information measure that composes across turns via the chain rule, and derive an upper bound on adversary success probability using average conditional min-entropy. Based on this framework, they propose BayWatch, an information-theoretic guardrail to limit cumulative sensitivity leakage.
nAdZPbUFPc.key_idea: Measures per-turn sensitive disclosure via chain-rule-composable mutual information (hop information leakage) and uses a Bayesian guardrail to cap cumulative leakage across turns.
nAdZPbUFPc.evidence: Supported by theoretical Fano/min-entropy upper bounds on adversary success probability and empirical multi-turn attack evaluations using Crescendo and TAP judged by GLM 5.2.
nAdZPbUFPc.claimed_gains: BayWatch reduces the attacker's success rate by up to 45 percentage points compared to the existing defense.
nAdZPbUFPc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that multi-turn indirect sensitive information leakage is an important security problem and that the information-theoretic formulation is clear and intuitive.
nAdZPbUFPc.main_concern: Reviewers point out a mismatch between the theoretical adaptive belief-updating adversary and the evaluated jailbreak attacks, unverified single-run LLM judge metrics, and an unexplained 45-percentage-point claim not matching the tables.

KhfXFhpz6U.one_liner: Introduces the VSTAT benchmark of 834 video clips and 1,500 questions to diagnose continuous visual state tracking in MLLMs.
KhfXFhpz6U.problem: Existing video benchmarks underexplore continuous visual state tracking of entities, states, and events over time, which cannot be solved from isolated keyframes or short segments.
KhfXFhpz6U.method: The authors construct the Visual STAte Tracking benchmark (VSTAT), comprising 834 synthetic and real-world video clips paired with 1,500 questions categorized by state elements and state structures. They evaluate multimodal large language models and compare model thinking traces against structured text transcriptions of the video streams to isolate failure modes.
KhfXFhpz6U.key_idea: Diagnoses MLLM temporal tracking by pairing multi-event videos with state-tracking queries and comparing video inference against text-transcribed event streams.
KhfXFhpz6U.evidence: Evaluated across MLLMs and answer-prior baselines on 834 synthetic and real-world video clips with 1,500 questions, plus diagnostic text-transcription experiments on three synthetic task families.
KhfXFhpz6U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating continuous visual state tracking over time addresses a meaningful gap in current video understanding benchmarks and that the state element and structure taxonomy is well organized.
KhfXFhpz6U.main_concern: Reviewers note that the paper lacks systematic sparse-frame or keyframe control baselines to verify that questions require full-video tracking, and that the structured text-transcription experiment oversimplifies the task beyond isolating visual perception.

IJP5tphUrE.one_liner: Combines cross-sample DINO-centroid verification with diffusion-inverse view refinement for test-time scaling of multi-view diffusion models.
IJP5tphUrE.problem: In test-time scaling for multi-view diffusion models, set-level selection preserves cross-view consistency but sacrifices individual view quality, whereas independent view-level selection breaks 3D consistency.
IJP5tphUrE.method: The authors propose DINO-centroid, a verifier that uses feature-space consensus across generated multi-view sets to select coherent view sets and identify uncertain views. They pair it with Exploration-Refinement Search (E-R Search), which explores complete view sets and regenerates uncertain individual views by formulating view refinement as a conditional diffusion inverse problem.
IJP5tphUrE.key_idea: Selects multi-view candidate sets and flags uncertain views via DINO feature-space consensus, then refines uncertain views as a diffusion inverse problem.
IJP5tphUrE.evidence: Evaluated primarily on SyncDreamer and MV-Adapter under matched inference budgets up to 64 samples, measuring LPIPS, MEt3R consistency, and downstream 3D reconstruction.
IJP5tphUrE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper clearly identifies the tension between set-level cross-view consistency and view-level image quality in test-time scaling for structured multi-view outputs.
IJP5tphUrE.main_concern: Reviewers note that the empirical gains over Best-of-N are modest at 64x compute, the primary SyncDreamer backbone is dated, and sequential autoregressive view search baselines are omitted.

nZ8sDQf0dN.one_liner: Schedules multi-edge speculative decoding verification requests at a shared central verifier using a queue-aware combinatorial semi-bandit algorithm.
nZ8sDQf0dN.problem: In multi-user cloud-edge speculative decoding, candidate token blocks generated asynchronously by multiple edge nodes contend for limited central target-model verification resources.
nZ8sDQf0dN.method: The authors formulate shared-verifier admission as a queue-aware combinatorial semi-bandit problem and propose Speculative Decoding Pipeline Scheduling (SDPS). In each round, the central verifier selects a subset of edge nodes from pending-verification queues by combining urgency-based Earliest-Deadline-First protection with Upper Confidence Bound estimates of unknown node verification yields and queue backlogs.
nZ8sDQf0dN.key_idea: Selects edge draft-block queues for central verification in each round by combining EDF latency protection, queue backlog weights, and UCB verification-yield estimates.
nZ8sDQf0dN.evidence: Supported by theoretical utility-loss, backlog, and per-block exposure-latency bounds and evaluated on a distributed LLM serving testbed against Exposure-EDF and SLED-inspired baselines.
nZ8sDQf0dN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the closed-loop problem formulation for shared-verifier contention in cloud-edge speculative decoding and the distinction between upload time and scheduler exposure time.
nZ8sDQf0dN.main_concern: Reviewers note that empirical goodput gains over a simple Exposure-EDF baseline are marginal with worse tail latency, theoretical assumptions on stationary independent arrivals are restrictive, and closely related scheduling baselines like WISP are not compared.

iqwRlfbDQJ.one_liner: Optimizes language model policies from multiple verifiers by maximizing a marginalized Plackett-Luce likelihood over Pareto-consistent partial orders.
iqwRlfbDQJ.problem: Aggregating binary outcomes from multiple verifiers into a scalar reward either discards partial progress or imposes arbitrary trade-offs between responses satisfying incomparable subsets of requirements.
iqwRlfbDQJ.method: Partial-Order Likelihood Policy Optimization (POLPO) uses Pareto dominance across multi-verifier outcomes to construct a partial order over sampled responses without scalar reward aggregation. It extends listwise Direct Preference Optimization by using dynamic programming to maximize the total Plackett-Luce probability of all complete rankings consistent with the verifier partial order.
iqwRlfbDQJ.key_idea: Maximizes the marginalized Plackett-Luce likelihood of all complete rankings consistent with the Pareto partial order induced by multiple binary verifiers.
iqwRlfbDQJ.evidence: Evaluated on controlled program synthesis, external coding benchmarks (including MBPP, APPS, HumanEval+, AceCode), and multi-constraint instruction following (IFM5, MathIF) against GRPO, DPO-Pareto, and GraphDPO.
iqwRlfbDQJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning directly from Pareto dominance relations without forcing arbitrary scalar trade-offs across multiple verifiers is well motivated and mathematically clear.
iqwRlfbDQJ.main_concern: Reviewers point out that main coding and synthesis experiments rely on a single training seed with modest absolute improvements, and that marginalized Plackett-Luce likelihoods over partial orders build closely on prior work and GraphDPO.

AX1lxTcmmz.one_liner: Iteratively estimates conditioning-context risk and corrupts unreliable observations during time-frequency diffusion reconstruction for multivariate time-series anomaly detection.
AX1lxTcmmz.problem: In diffusion-based multivariate time-series anomaly detection, anomalies present in the unmasked conditioning context bias the reconstruction toward abnormal patterns and obscure reconstruction-error anomaly scores.
AX1lxTcmmz.method: Self-Correcting Time-Frequency Diffusion (SCTF) treats conditioning reliability as a dynamic variable estimated from complementary temporal and wavelet-frequency views. It uses estimated context risks to adaptively corrupt unreliable conditioning observations during diffusion generation and refines the risk estimates iteratively using reconstruction residuals.
AX1lxTcmmz.key_idea: Couples multi-view context risk estimation with risk-adaptive context corruption and iterative residual-based risk refinement during time-frequency diffusion reconstruction.
AX1lxTcmmz.evidence: Evaluated on multivariate time-series anomaly detection datasets including SMAP, SMD, PSM, MSL, SWaT, and STEAD under both point-adjusted and no-point-adjustment protocols.
AX1lxTcmmz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing anomalous contamination in the conditioning context via dynamic risk-adaptive corruption is a well-motivated framing supported by thorough ablations and no-point-adjustment comparisons.
AX1lxTcmmz.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the initial risk estimator alone achieves nearly identical F1/AUPRC to the final diffusion detector on STEAD and PSM, questioning whether running diffusion at inference adds value beyond the risk predictor.

CzwnhuTaBw.one_liner: Uses an analytical FP4 rounding-breakpoint scale oracle to design a fixed-candidate block-scale search for NVFP4 quantized LLM training.
CzwnhuTaBw.problem: Existing NVFP4 quantized pre-training recipes exhibit a quality gap relative to BF16 due to forward weight-activation quantization error under the sparse FP4 codebook and shared block scale.
CzwnhuTaBw.method: SCOPE derives a closed-form piecewise analytical per-block scale oracle based on FP4 rounding breakpoints to quantify recoverable reconstruction error, and approximates it online via a fixed-candidate scale search per block. It pairs this forward candidate search with lightweight stochastic rounding and Hadamard backward estimators diagnosed via gradient-to-quantization-noise ratios.
CzwnhuTaBw.key_idea: Approximates an analytical FP4 rounding-breakpoint scale oracle with a compact online candidate scale sweep to minimize per-block forward reconstruction error.
CzwnhuTaBw.evidence: Evaluated on LLaMA-family PTQ/pre-training and NanoChat pre-training up to 1.9B parameters and 38B tokens on GB200 hardware against Quartet-II and the NVIDIA NVFP4 recipe.
CzwnhuTaBw.claimed_gains: On NanoChat pre-training up to 1.9B parameters and 38B tokens, SCOPE reduces the BF16 bits-per-byte gap to 1.01%, a relative gap reduction of ~30% over Quartet-II and ~47% over the NVIDIA NVFP4 recipe.
CzwnhuTaBw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the closed-form analytical scale oracle analysis and the end-to-end NVFP4 pre-training evaluation up to 1.9B parameters and 38B tokens.
CzwnhuTaBw.main_concern: Reviewers note that the deployable runtime algorithm reduces to a small candidate scale sweep similar to prior work like 4over6 and introduces nontrivial runtime overhead (12.7% slower than the NVIDIA baseline).

S8IQya30jR.one_liner: EGO combines difficulty-aware sampling and event-level reinforcement-learning feedback for temporal grounding with zero or multiple matching segments.
S8IQya30jR.problem: Single-segment grounding assumptions and sequence-level rewards poorly handle absent events and responses mixing correct and incorrect event predictions.
S8IQya30jR.method: AnyMoment supplies queries with zero, one, or multiple matching segments. EGO jointly samples by occurrence-recognition and temporal-localization difficulty and assigns fine-grained event-level feedback during reinforcement learning.
S8IQya30jR.key_idea: Assign event-level advantages within multi-segment responses and sample training instances by recognition and localization difficulty.
S8IQya30jR.evidence: Reviews describe evaluations on AnyMoment and OMTG and event-count diagnostics comparing local advantages for single- and multi-event queries.
S8IQya30jR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value coverage of absent and repeated events and find event-level learning feedback well motivated.
S8IQya30jR.main_concern: Missing strong recent baselines on AnyMoment and incompletely specified comparison conditions limit assessment of benchmark difficulty and method advantage.

WjjXW0nQ2T.one_liner: K-Shield learns local activation subspaces and routes inputs to region-specific refusal steering maps with null-space constraints.
WjjXW0nQ2T.problem: Globally protecting benign activation directions can suppress directions needed for refusal elsewhere in activation space.
WjjXW0nQ2T.method: K-Shield uses optimal transport to learn local subspaces and routes inputs to corresponding steering maps and refusal targets. Local null-space constraints protect benign behavior while reducing refusal-target reconstruction error.
WjjXW0nQ2T.key_idea: Apply null-space preservation constraints locally and route each input to a region-specific steering map and refusal target.
WjjXW0nQ2T.evidence: The paper analyzes reconstruction error and evaluates three language models against seven jailbreak attacks and four utility benchmarks.
WjjXW0nQ2T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that local preservation constraints are intuitively motivated and clearly presented.
WjjXW0nQ2T.main_concern: The theoretical and methodological contribution relies heavily on established least-squares, null-space projection, and optimal-transport techniques.

dBGXDpcMra.one_liner: iBOLT fits a one-step Gaussian-mixture policy to a value-induced Boltzmann target using density-corrected weighted likelihood.
dBGXDpcMra.problem: Expressive generative reinforcement-learning policies face a trade-off between multimodal action fidelity and training or inference cost.
dBGXDpcMra.method: A network maps state and latent variables to truncated-Gaussian component parameters, defining a continuous-mixture policy. A finite-mixture approximation reweights sampled actions toward the Boltzmann distribution, and weighted mixture-likelihood maximization trains single-evaluation action generation.
dBGXDpcMra.key_idea: Use finite-mixture density correction to weight action samples for likelihood fitting of a continuous-mixture Boltzmann policy.
dBGXDpcMra.evidence: MuJoCo benchmarks, multimodal tasks, and matched-architecture distribution-fitting comparisons assess control performance and target recovery.
dBGXDpcMra.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a simple expressive policy with one-step sampling and experiments probing both distribution fitting and control.
dBGXDpcMra.main_concern: The GMM40 proposal distribution and its density correction are unclear because the reported proposal variance differs from the actor's permitted variance.

Gge7ejM3wC.one_liner: Experience Harness distills trajectories into bottleneck-specific success skills for initial guidance and failure modes for targeted runtime correction.
Gge7ejM3wC.problem: Generic experience reuse can miss sequentially emerging task bottlenecks or provide corrective advice at the wrong stage.
Gge7ejM3wC.method: The harness decomposes successful and failed trajectories into bottleneck-aware atoms across four dimensions. Success skills guide task starts, while detected failure modes trigger corrective prompts during execution and release them after resolution.
Gge7ejM3wC.key_idea: Separate initial success-skill guidance from failure-mode corrections activated only when the corresponding bottleneck appears during execution.
Gge7ejM3wC.evidence: Experiments on AppWorld and BFCL-V3 compare multiple base agents and memory baselines, with ablations of skills, failure modes, runtime detection, and dimension-aware selection.
Gge7ejM3wC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers report improvements across agents and benchmarks and value evidence that the timing of experience injection matters.
Gge7ejM3wC.main_concern: Fixed bottleneck categories and benchmark-specific API memories leave transfer to unseen tasks and environments insufficiently established.

Kr9yL2i3YQ.one_liner: BEHAVIOR-Spatial links spatial question answering, target grounding, and robot actions while probing changed instructions in fixed scenes.
Kr9yL2i3YQ.problem: Robot task success alone cannot establish whether policies follow spatial instructions or use their models' spatial understanding.
Kr9yL2i3YQ.method: The benchmark aligns spatial questions, point-grounding queries, and action evaluations on shared scenes and targets. It changes requested targets within fixed training layouts and compares held-out configurations, adapted models, and oracle target cues.
Kr9yL2i3YQ.key_idea: Hold the physical scene fixed while changing the requested target, and jointly evaluate perception, point grounding, and action success.
Kr9yL2i3YQ.evidence: BEHAVIOR-1K evaluations include 3,256 questions across 49 activities, 1,240 grounding queries across 14 manipulation tasks, and action tests on those tasks and 10 navigation tasks.
Kr9yL2i3YQ.claimed_gains: Oracle visual target cues raise held-out-configuration success from 41.4% to 60.3% and changed-instruction success from 16.1% to 38.0%.
Kr9yL2i3YQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value aligned perception, grounding, and action tests and the changed-target probe as diagnostics of instruction following.
Kr9yL2i3YQ.main_concern: Correlations across a small task set and closely related policies lack uncertainty analysis and do not establish transfer of a backbone's spatial understanding to actions.

4uOOa74j7a.one_liner: RFI masks scene text, delegates crop reading to an untrusted VLM, and delays text insertion until trusted reasoning finishes.
4uOOa74j7a.problem: Wearable assistants receive useful text and prompt injections through the same visual channel, while blanket text removal destroys task utility.
4uOOa74j7a.method: RFI redacts detected text regions while retaining their locations and crops; a trusted VLM reasons over the request and redacted frame. An untrusted VLM answers narrow crop questions, whose values a non-language mediator hides behind opaque symbols until a renderer inserts them after response completion.
4uOOa74j7a.key_idea: Keep crop-derived text outside the trusted model's context by passing opaque symbols and binding their stored values only after reasoning completes.
4uOOa74j7a.evidence: Experiments compare four systems across six VLMs on 60 scenes with digitally composited attack carriers, reporting clean utility and runtime costs.
4uOOa74j7a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of scene reasoning from text reading clear and relevant to physical prompt injection.
4uOOa74j7a.main_concern: Protecting trusted-model response structure does not eliminate attacker influence through substituted values or availability-state channels.

dDOVEnTWGd.one_liner: SocialBench combines social-perception tasks with supervised adaptation and activation probes to compare generated answers against decodable social information.
dDOVEnTWGd.problem: Final-answer scores alone do not distinguish social cue perception, contextual understanding, and implicit-intention reasoning.
dDOVEnTWGd.method: SocialBench organizes existing datasets into Perception, Understanding, and Theory of Mind tasks across image, video, audio, and text inputs. It compares multimodal model answers, single-task and joint fine-tuning, and linear probes of pre- and post-training activations.
dDOVEnTWGd.key_idea: Compare generated task answers with supervised adaptation and linear decodability to separate response behavior from available social-task information.
dDOVEnTWGd.evidence: The benchmark combines 16 datasets into 30 task variants, evaluates five multimodal models, and conducts fine-tuning and probing on Qwen3-Omni.
dDOVEnTWGd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value broad social-task coverage and the complementary diagnostics from generated answers, adaptation, and linear probes.
dDOVEnTWGd.main_concern: Strict field extraction conflates semantic answer quality with output-format compliance and materially distorts reported model comparisons.

mgGQCUszbS.one_liner: A covariance-informed proximal method applies inner and outer momentum to accelerate single-pass stochastic generalized linear prediction.
mgGQCUszbS.problem: It remains unclear how momentum can accelerate non-quadratic streaming optimization when each update receives only one fresh sample.
mgGQCUszbS.method: The algorithm uses fresh data to construct covariance-informed proximal updates and accelerates both inner subproblem solving and the outer trajectory. Its analysis separates optimization error, statistical error, and higher-order model-misspecification error.
mgGQCUszbS.key_idea: Use covariance-informed proximal subproblems with momentum in both the inner solver and outer update sequence.
mgGQCUszbS.evidence: Excess-risk theory uses stationary inner-update and two-phase outer-loop analyses, with synthetic and logistic experiments and momentum comparisons.
mgGQCUszbS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the covariance geometry and two levels of acceleration promising for improving streaming optimization in the intended condition-number regime.
mgGQCUszbS.main_concern: The logistic-regression experiments do not clearly satisfy the theory's global positive-curvature assumption.

2hZPXVXyTI.one_liner: Perturbation-aware exogenous RL bounds regret when actions weakly affect otherwise external transition dynamics.
2hZPXVXyTI.problem: Exact independence between actions and exogenous variables fails in systems where actions weakly perturb external dynamics.
2hZPXVXyTI.method: The paper models bounded action-dependent perturbations and introduces tabular optimistic learning and Exogenous Value-Targeted Regression for linear-mixture dynamics. It also analyzes no-bonus predict-then-optimize and constructs lower bounds for specified exogenous planners.
2hZPXVXyTI.key_idea: Model bounded deviations from exogenous transitions and account for their accumulated impact in tabular and linear-mixture value estimation.
2hZPXVXyTI.evidence: High-probability regret proofs, planner-class lower bounds, and a two-stage construction accompany experiments on execution families, clipping, and optimism.
2hZPXVXyTI.claimed_gains: The algorithms achieve high-probability regret of the form Õ(√K) + Õ(εK), with tabular no-bonus predict-then-optimize attaining the same order.
2hZPXVXyTI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value studying approximate exogeneity and the theoretical insights about retaining exogenous structure under weak action dependence.
2hZPXVXyTI.main_concern: The statistical-plus-linear-misspecification regret form is already established, leaving the theoretical advance beyond existing robust RL insufficiently clear.

zprcZx62NY.one_liner: Complex KDA combines signed channel gates with expanded delta coefficients to realize rotations using diagonal-plus-rank-one transitions.
zprcZx62NY.problem: Single low-rank delta-rule updates limit state-tracking expressivity, while composing extra updates increases computational cost.
zprcZx62NY.method: Complex KDA extends channel gates to [-1,1] and the delta coefficient to [0,2], allowing a gate-supplied reflection to combine with a delta-rule transformation. The resulting non-expansive diagonal-plus-rank-one transitions preserve KDA's computational structure.
zprcZx62NY.key_idea: Combine a signed channel-gate reflection with a single delta-rule transformation to realize rotations without increasing transition rank.
zprcZx62NY.evidence: Proofs characterize orthogonal diagonal-plus-rank-one transitions and finite-group tracking, alongside synthetic length-extrapolation, language-modeling, and recall experiments.
zprcZx62NY.claimed_gains: Many state-tracking results use one fewer layer for CKDA than for other diagonal-plus-rank-one linear RNNs.
zprcZx62NY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the expressivity analysis of signed gating and diagonal-plus-low-rank recurrent transitions.
zprcZx62NY.main_concern: Expressivity guarantees do not establish practical learnability or reliable gains on real-world language-modeling tasks.

jshdk5V7Ti.one_liner: SCoPE sparsely selects event labels within each modality and exchanges priors that adjust the other's selection costs.
jshdk5V7Ti.problem: Thresholded audio-visual similarity scores cannot separate correct event labels from equally scoring related false activations.
jshdk5V7Ti.method: SCoPE makes labels compete to explain each modality's evidence through sparse selection. Cross-modal priors adjust class-specific costs, after which each target modality reselects labels against its own embedding, including in causal streaming.
jshdk5V7Ti.key_idea: Exchange sparse event priors as selection-cost adjustments, then refit each modality's labels using its own evidence.
jshdk5V7Ti.evidence: Experiments cover three audio-visual event datasets and multiple encoder configurations, with ablations of independent selection, direct fusion, and prior-guided reselection.
jshdk5V7Ti.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the interpretable training-free design and consistent gains across datasets with modality-specific evidence preserved.
jshdk5V7Ti.main_concern: Matched dense-prior and score-calibration controls are missing, leaving the sparse cross-modal mechanism's advantage over simpler alternatives uncertain.

XQGNmgRz8U.one_liner: Tests lie-detection probes with same-persona truth comparisons and confounder datasets, then augments training to separate truth from shortcuts.
XQGNmgRz8U.problem: Lie-detection probes may follow persona beliefs or contextual shortcuts rather than factual correctness.
XQGNmgRz8U.method: The authors evaluate probes on anti-factual persona responses with correct and incorrect answers under the same prompt. They construct confounder datasets and add training examples that separate truth from confounding concepts.
XQGNmgRz8U.key_idea: Hold persona prompts fixed and reverse correlations between truth and contextual cues to expose probe shortcuts.
XQGNmgRz8U.evidence: Evaluation covers 8,916 human-reviewed responses from three LLMs, nine existing probes, three confounder datasets, and training ablations.
XQGNmgRz8U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that same-persona comparisons remove prompt-label shortcuts and provide a useful probe evaluation.
XQGNmgRz8U.main_concern: The diagnostic interventions do not sufficiently isolate which confounders explain same-persona failures.

fsthGnds8N.one_liner: Distills corrective reasoning guidance only from the first erroneous sentence of an on-policy rollout.
fsthGnds8N.problem: Full-solution supervision and full-response distillation can suppress reasoning diversity and destabilize on-policy self-distillation.
fsthGnds8N.method: ROSD contrasts incorrect and correct rollouts to extract a corrective idea and locate the first erroneous sentence. It guides the self-teacher with that idea and masks distillation loss on the valid prefix.
fsthGnds8N.key_idea: Use rollout-specific corrective ideas to guide a teacher while restricting token-level distillation to the erroneous suffix.
fsthGnds8N.evidence: Experiments cover multiple reasoning benchmarks and backbones, including Qwen3 and Llama, with component ablations and extended-training comparisons.
fsthGnds8N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the selective-supervision design concrete and practical without additional trainable parameters.
fsthGnds8N.main_concern: ROSD freezes its teacher while SDPO uses EMA updates, confounding the central training-stability comparison.

XW1JjEfZPb.one_liner: Builds weighted data shards from observed training losses to balance worker objectives under infrequent synchronization.
XW1JjEfZPb.problem: Data heterogeneity across workers slows convergence when distributed training synchronizes models less frequently.
XW1JjEfZPb.method: The algorithm stratifies and weights data using objective values observed during training to reduce discrepancies between worker objectives. Its analysis relates convergence to objective approximation error.
XW1JjEfZPb.key_idea: Use historical losses to construct weighted shards that approximate the full training objective on each worker.
XW1JjEfZPb.evidence: Objective-approximation and convergence guarantees accompany image-classification and math continual-pretraining experiments, including CIFAR-10 and TinyLlama.
XW1JjEfZPb.claimed_gains: Compared with random partitioning, convergence is up to 1.45 times faster in training steps, with gains persisting under nearly 80% fewer synchronization rounds.
XW1JjEfZPb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value loss-informed data assignment and its empirical gains without more frequent model synchronization.
XW1JjEfZPb.main_concern: The practical benefit remains unclear at industrial scale once data access and repeated shard-transfer costs are considered.

aUgq0XEAt1.one_liner: Introduces comparison-specific scale inside DPO logits to separate preference ambiguity from latent utility gaps.
aUgq0XEAt1.problem: A single comparison scale forces standard DPO scores to absorb pair-dependent ambiguity and distort utility gaps.
aUgq0XEAt1.method: A random-utility taxonomy distinguishes forms of heterogeneity in preference optimization. H-DPO retains the utility-gap parameterization while adding comparison-specific observation scale inside the logit.
aUgq0XEAt1.key_idea: Parameterize utility gaps and comparison-specific logit scales separately instead of absorbing scale into preference scores.
aUgq0XEAt1.evidence: Restricted-family local-identifiability analysis and synthetic experiments compare utility recovery against DPO and oracle loss reweighting.
aUgq0XEAt1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the distinction between preference-probability fitting and utility recovery, including observation scale versus loss reweighting.
aUgq0XEAt1.main_concern: The restricted identifiability theory does not establish utility recovery for the implemented neural H-DPO model.

qBJb1RwCjO.one_liner: Combines frozen VLM local scores with task-specific constrained solvers to assemble global visual structures.
qBJb1RwCjO.problem: VLMs can answer local visual questions accurately yet fail to combine them into correct global structures.
qBJb1RwCjO.method: Local+solve extracts local decision scores from a frozen VLM and feeds them to a solver with task-defined constraints. Its outputs also supply pseudo-labels for post-training.
qBJb1RwCjO.key_idea: Separate local visual scoring from constrained global assembly using a task-specific solver.
qBJb1RwCjO.evidence: Experiments span RecipeQA, six controlled structural families, five public-benchmark tasks, GUI settings, model scales, and post-training transfer.
qBJb1RwCjO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that broad experiments make the local-global assembly gap measurable and demonstrate useful gains.
qBJb1RwCjO.main_concern: The method largely applies established decomposition and structured-inference techniques, limiting its methodological originality.

WFwOOToW9B.one_liner: Evolves whole skeletal trajectories with graph-structured flow matching on spherical bone directions to preserve bone lengths.
WFwOOToW9B.problem: Human motion prediction must generate diverse futures while respecting skeletal geometry and coordinated spatial-temporal motion.
WFwOOToW9B.method: GSFM transports a complete future trajectory through a conditional velocity field on a spatiotemporal skeleton graph. Geodesic flow matching and tangent evolution of spherical bone directions preserve prescribed bone lengths.
WFwOOToW9B.key_idea: Couple spherical bone-direction flows through spatial and temporal attention across the complete future skeleton trajectory.
WFwOOToW9B.evidence: AMASS experiments assess accuracy, diversity, and motion statistics, with attention ablations and transfer to Human3.6M without retraining.
WFwOOToW9B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that spherical bone directions provide a clear mechanism for preserving bone lengths.
WFwOOToW9B.main_concern: Experiments do not adequately isolate the predictive value of graph structure and spherical flow from existing alternatives.

Izymd9xrGG.one_liner: Contextualizes candidate tokens separately, then fuses their attention Values at selected layers during a single decoding trajectory.
Izymd9xrGG.problem: Embedding-level candidate mixing can collapse toward one candidate as processing proceeds through model layers.
Izymd9xrGG.method: DIVER independently processes candidate tokens under the same reasoning prefix before computing a probability-weighted mixture of their attention Values. It substitutes these mixtures at selected internal layers and stores them in the KV cache.
Izymd9xrGG.key_idea: Delay candidate aggregation until internal attention Values, after each candidate has received its own contextual processing.
Izymd9xrGG.evidence: Layerwise analyses, ablations, and math, science, and code evaluations cover seven backbones from 1.7B to 32B.
Izymd9xrGG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize broad empirical coverage and a simple, interpretable approach to retaining alternative-candidate information.
Izymd9xrGG.main_concern: The comparisons leave the reliability of gains under alternative temperature settings, layer calibration, and computational budgets uncertain.

bAgpuKXLzk.one_liner: Models dissent withholding and answer internalization to predict when multi-agent discussion improves on majority voting.
bAgpuKXLzk.problem: Multi-agent discussion sometimes improves accuracy and sometimes reinforces an incorrect consensus.
bAgpuKXLzk.method: A behavioral model combines dissent withholding, internalization, reconsideration, and correction to derive a recovery threshold. Bayesian estimates from conversation logs place LLM teams relative to that threshold.
bAgpuKXLzk.key_idea: Compare dissent-withholding rates with a critical rate determined by correction and answer internalization.
bAgpuKXLzk.evidence: The model is evaluated across LLMs on hidden-profile tasks, HiddenBench, and MedEInst, including dissent instructions and reasoning interventions.
bAgpuKXLzk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard explaining inconsistent multi-agent discussion outcomes through measurable behavior as a relevant contribution.
bAgpuKXLzk.main_concern: Restrictive behavioral assumptions and imperfect empirical fit leave the proposed threshold's general validity unclear.

830ludqBPR.one_liner: Pretrains a router to infer anonymous model capabilities from behavioral context and adapt to new routing environments without retraining.
830ludqBPR.problem: Routers fitted to fixed workloads and candidate pools require new supervision when deployment conditions change.
830ludqBPR.method: RouteFM uses episodic pretraining across heterogeneous routing environments to infer candidate capabilities from behavioral observations. A frozen router adapts to new tasks and candidate pools through context alone.
830ludqBPR.key_idea: Represent candidate models through behavioral evidence rather than fixed identities and learn routing across varied environments.
830ludqBPR.evidence: Experiments test transfer across domains, modalities, candidate pools, and context budgets, including held-out MMR-Bench and architecture/data ablations.
830ludqBPR.claimed_gains: On MMR-Bench, RouteFM exceeds the strongest baseline by 2.23 quality points with only eight observations per candidate.
830ludqBPR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see practical value in reusable routing, particularly when few observations are available for new models.
830ludqBPR.main_concern: Gains diminish with more candidate observations, and evidence for broad transfer beyond the evaluated environments remains limited.

xl658eb0KC.one_liner: Localizes LLM backdoor trigger channels in shallow MLPs using 500 clean samples and applies Fisher-protected soft pruning.
xl658eb0KC.problem: Post-training LLM backdoor defenses intervene uniformly across all layers without localizing where backdoor computation occurs, damaging benign parameters.
xl658eb0KC.method: BadScalp leverages the observation that trigger recognition concentrates in shallow-layer MLPs and uses 500 clean samples with a simulated trigger objective to attribute each shallow MLP channel's contribution toward poisoned states. It repairs identified backdoor channels using soft pruning combined with Fisher-guided protection to preserve clean-task utility without knowing the trigger, target label, or a clean reference model.
xl658eb0KC.key_idea: Attribute poisoned-state shifts to individual channels within shallow-layer MLPs using clean samples and apply Fisher-protected soft pruning only there.
xl658eb0KC.evidence: Causal layer- and component-swapping analyses alongside defense evaluations across multiple LLMs (including Llama and DeepSeek), datasets (such as SST-2 and WebQ), and backdoor attacks (including BadNets).
xl658eb0KC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating shallow-MLP trigger recognition from deep-layer output generation offers a practical mechanistic rationale for localized defense using only 500 clean samples.
xl658eb0KC.main_concern: Reviewers identify unvalidated assumptions that simulated triggers recover true backdoor channels, numerical contradictions between main tables and hyperparameter sweep plots at default settings, and limited adaptive-attack evaluation.

v84x63IV61.one_liner: Generates synthetic human mobility trajectories conditioned on persistent traits and daily intentions via closed-loop multi-day decoding.
v84x63IV61.problem: Synthetic human mobility generators optimize aggregate day-level trajectory realism while failing to realize specific intended multi-day behavioral traits at the individual level.
v84x63IV61.method: CTGTrace specifies individuals using 19 persistent characteristics and 16 daily intentions and realizes them through structured spatial generation, multi-day planning, and closed-loop trajectory decoding that tracks behavioral targets. The framework supports partial trait specifications, scenario transfer, and synthetic generation without underlying real individuals.
v84x63IV61.key_idea: Condition multi-day spatial planning and closed-loop trajectory decoding on explicit individual profiles of 19 persistent characteristics and 16 daily intentions.
v84x63IV61.evidence: Evaluated across five heterogeneous mobility populations against eleven published mobility generators, testing request-realization error, population-level realism, partial specifications, and scenario transfer.
v84x63IV61.claimed_gains: Across five mobility populations, CTGTrace achieves a mean normalized request-realization error of 0.175 with correlation r = 0.925.
v84x63IV61.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing person-level behavioral alignment from aggregate trajectory realism is well motivated and supported by a structured multi-scale trait formulation and broad evaluation.
v84x63IV61.main_concern: Reviewers flag unsupported headline claims (citing an 87% next-location Acc@1 absent from tables), internal numerical inconsistencies, baseline degradation from discretized grid conversion, and circular evaluation on input traits.

vDTSGZzRrc.one_liner: Detects single reasoning tokens causing sharp success-probability drops and applies single-token preference optimization at uncertain cliff positions.
vDTSGZzRrc.problem: Step- and sentence-level error localization in mathematical reasoning identifies regions after failure has occurred rather than pinpointing the exact token that triggers divergence.
vDTSGZzRrc.method: The authors estimate per-token rollout success probabilities to identify cliff tokens where success probability drops past an adaptive threshold, classifying them by greedy selection and token entropy into deterministic, uncertain, and sampled-off cliffs. They then apply single-token Direct Preference Optimization at identified cliff positions (Cliff-DPO) to steer models away from failure triggers.
