vDTSGZzRrc.key_idea: Localize single tokens where estimated rollout success probability drops sharply, classify them by entropy and greedy choice, and apply single-token DPO there.
vDTSGZzRrc.evidence: Analyzed across seven LLMs and three mathematical reasoning benchmarks (GSM1K, MATH500, AIME 2025) using prefix resampling before versus after cliff tokens and Cliff-DPO training experiments.
vDTSGZzRrc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the token-level cliff definition, prefix-resampling analysis, three-way cliff taxonomy, and released per-token rollout dataset informative for studying mathematical reasoning failures.
vDTSGZzRrc.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the quadratic rollout cost of estimating per-token success probabilities, mathematical doubts about how greedy deterministic cliffs exceed the drop threshold, and inconsistent gains over critical-token cDPO.

XBZnOHUDxC.one_liner: Quantizes LLM KV caches with folded-rotation short-block joint codebooks, precomputed candidate lists, and asymmetric KV bit allocation.
XBZnOHUDxC.problem: Per-coordinate scalar KV-cache quantization sacrifices block-level geometric efficiency, while naive vector quantization adds prohibitive online encoding and serving overhead during decoding.
XBZnOHUDxC.method: HayateQuant applies an offline-materialized folded rotation (combining Hadamard, sign, and per-block Haar transforms into one dense matrix) to equalize within-block directions and quantizes short blocks using compact joint codebooks with precomputed candidate lists. It pairs this codec with role-specific scaling, distinct key and value bit allocation, and a packed attention serving implementation.
XBZnOHUDxC.key_idea: Apply a single dense folded rotation to equalize block directions and quantize KV-cache entries with short-block joint codebooks and precomputed candidate lists.
XBZnOHUDxC.evidence: Evaluated across seven LLM families at 3-bit and 4-bit KV-cache rates for perplexity, downstream quality, and end-to-end packed-kernel decoding throughput against a scalar reference codec.
XBZnOHUDxC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that materializing the folded rotation into a single dense transform cleanly integrates short-block joint codebooks with packed serving kernels and improves 3-bit quality over the scalar baseline.
XBZnOHUDxC.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the absence of comparisons against closely related vector and block KV-cache codecs (such as PolarQuant, FibQuant, and BlockQuant) and bundled changes that leave the isolated benefit of block geometry unproven.

CpaRN5Yqoo.one_liner: Steers late-decoder video-LLM activations along Jacobian-projected temporal contrast directions to improve training-free event end-time grounding.
CpaRN5Yqoo.problem: Video large language models localize event start times reasonably well but struggle to discriminate event end times without costly temporal post-training or extra inference passes.
CpaRN5Yqoo.method: The method computes endpoint-score Jacobians to identify late-decoder directions that directly shift numerical end-time predictions and projects activation differences from temporal perturbations onto this endpoint-sensitive subspace. At inference time, it applies training-free activation steering along the aggregated projected directions to refine predicted end timestamps.
CpaRN5Yqoo.key_idea: Project temporal-perturbation activation contrasts onto endpoint-score Jacobian directions to construct a late-decoder steering subspace targeting event end-time boundary predictions.
CpaRN5Yqoo.evidence: Causal subspace diagnostics and training-free steering ablations (against native decoding, temporal-only, gradient-only, and shuffled controls) on video temporal grounding benchmarks using Qwen3-VL backbones.
CpaRN5Yqoo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the empirical finding that visual evidence discriminates start times better than end times and find the controlled Jacobian-filtered steering ablations informative.
CpaRN5Yqoo.main_concern: Reviewers cite dense, undefined terminology that impedes readability, dataset-specific calibration sensitivity under custom splits, and small gains (0.67–0.72 mIoU) over an endpoint-gradient-only baseline.

ExYRh1M2CM.one_liner: Decomposes multi-agent debate outputs into structured epistemic nodes and builds a conflict graph to route targeted verification.
ExYRh1M2CM.problem: Trajectory-level multi-agent debate sways toward fluent or confident arguments and obscures specific intermediate reasoning errors inside long plausible traces.
ExYRh1M2CM.method: GCL-MAD prompts role-specialized agents to output structured epistemic fields (answers, assumptions, skeptical points, and boundary conditions) as nodes and uses a graph-construction agent to connect conflicting claims with rationale-annotated edges in an Epistemic Conflict Graph. Verification and adjudication are selectively routed only to conflict-linked components rather than re-evaluating entire trajectories.
ExYRh1M2CM.key_idea: Organize multi-agent debate claims into structured epistemic nodes connected by rationale-labeled conflict edges to focus verification on disputed reasoning components.
ExYRh1M2CM.evidence: Evaluated across two LLM backbones and six mathematical, knowledge, and commonsense QA benchmarks (including MATH and GPQA), with matched-budget verification routing and answer-transition analyses.
ExYRh1M2CM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing agent trajectories into structured epistemic components for selective conflict verification is intuitive and well examined through matched-budget routing and answer-transition diagnostics.
ExYRh1M2CM.main_concern: Reviewers note minimal accuracy gains over baselines and flat LLM conflict ranking (under 1 percentage point), lack of multi-hop graph computation, and narrow evaluation across only two backbones and short-answer tasks.

tj74nTn0z5.one_liner: Removes reverse-step stochastic noise in pretrained diffusion models to converge arbitrary seeds onto sharp population atlases.
tj74nTn0z5.problem: Constructing anatomical or population templates typically requires dedicated deformable registration optimization or retraining task-specific template-generation networks for each domain or subpopulation.
tj74nTn0z5.method: The authors modify reverse DDPM sampling into a deterministic noise-free posterior-mean iteration that collapses arbitrary random initializations onto a single central image—termed the intrinsic atlas—in one inference pass without retraining. Conditioning an existing pretrained diffusion model on attributes such as age directly yields subpopulation-specific atlases.
tj74nTn0z5.key_idea: Drop injected stochastic noise during reverse diffusion transitions so posterior-mean iteration converges from any seed to a population template.
tj74nTn0z5.evidence: Evaluated across 3D brain MRI, chest X-ray, face (CelebA), and 3D shape pretrained diffusion models, including age-conditioned brain atlases and registration-target comparisons on held-out MRI cohorts.
tj74nTn0z5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it simple, training-free, and empirically consistent that removing reverse-diffusion noise collapses arbitrary seeds onto sharp population templates across diverse imaging domains.
tj74nTn0z5.main_concern: Reviewers note the lack of subject-to-atlas deformation fields needed for downstream registration tasks, imprecise mathematical definitions of whether the output represents a mean or mode, and missing deterministic ODE or sample-mean controls from the same generator.

Nqfm7aH56G.one_liner: Generates object point addresses autoregressively then decodes all aerial bounding boxes in parallel under instance-isolated attention masks.
Nqfm7aH56G.problem: Remote-sensing vision-language models decode bounding-box coordinates sequentially one object at a time, causing high inference latency in dense aerial scenes with many targets.
Nqfm7aH56G.method: Parallel Instance Decoding (PID) decouples language-guided aerial localization into autoregressive discovery of per-instance reference point addresses followed by a single parallel decoding pass that regresses all bounding boxes simultaneously. An instance-isolated attention mask lets each box query attend to the full image and its own point address while blocking cross-instance box attention.
Nqfm7aH56G.key_idea: Separate autoregressive point-address discovery from single-pass parallel bounding-box decoding using an instance-isolated attention mask that blocks inter-box attention.
Nqfm7aH56G.evidence: Evaluated on remote-sensing localization, detection, grounding, and pointing benchmarks including DIOR and DOTAv2 against a controlled direct-box baseline with density-stratified latency analyses.
Nqfm7aH56G.claimed_gains: Under matched training data and setup, PID improves F1@0.50 over the direct-box baseline by 8.3 points on DIOR and 7.3 points on DOTAv2 while reducing complete-response latency by 22.4%.
Nqfm7aH56G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling sequential center-point discovery from parallel bounding-box decoding is well suited to dense aerial imagery and improves both localization F1 and latency under controlled training.
Nqfm7aH56G.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the instance-isolated attention mask is not directly ablated and that accuracy gains are confounded with extra box-center point supervision absent from the direct-box baseline.

6WsGHOtGMQ.one_liner: Relays target-verifier hidden states from rejected draft suffixes into subsequent block-diffusion speculative decoding rounds via self-conditioned training.
6WsGHOtGMQ.problem: Block-diffusion speculative decoding discards target-model representations computed at rejected suffix positions, forcing the drafter to rebuild future-token representations from scratch in the next round.
6WsGHOtGMQ.method: DFlow aligns and reuses hidden states produced by the target verifier over rejected draft suffix positions to condition the drafter in subsequent drafting rounds without extra target forward passes. A multi-round self-conditioning training procedure exposes the drafter to verifier representations from earlier rejected predictions so it learns to exploit this cross-round relay signal.
6WsGHOtGMQ.key_idea: Reuse target-model hidden states at rejected draft positions across speculative decoding rounds using boundary-conditioned alignment and multi-round self-conditioned training.
6WsGHOtGMQ.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3 models across benchmarks including MATH500 and HumanEval against DFlash and EAGLE-3 baselines, with relay and self-conditioning ablations.
6WsGHOtGMQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing already-computed target verifier states from rejected draft suffixes is a clean, low-overhead mechanism that improves acceptance length in controlled ablations.
6WsGHOtGMQ.main_concern: Reviewers question the unquantified multi-round online-verification training cost, substantially weaker reproduced DFlash baseline numbers compared to prior reports, and limited end-to-end validation on newer block drafters.

29IKC8vAri.one_liner: JtT diffuses per-frame point velocities in coordinate space to forecast diverse rigid motion.
29IKC8vAri.problem: Trajectory generators struggle to produce diverse, physically plausible rigid futures from one image without geometric inputs.
29IKC8vAri.method: JtT is an approximately 50M-parameter diffusion transformer that predicts per-frame velocities, supports arbitrary dense queries, and conditions on full-resolution RGB at query points.
29IKC8vAri.key_idea: Per-frame velocity diffusion with a matched timestep schedule preserves rigidity without explicit rigid-body constraints or trajectory VAEs.
29IKC8vAri.evidence: Systematic ablations and training-dynamics analyses evaluate model sizes and design choices, primarily on synthetic Kubric scenes with qualitative real-world results.
29IKC8vAri.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the model is simple and that the design ablations and rigidity–diversity analysis provide useful empirical evidence.
29IKC8vAri.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite limited real-world quantitative evaluation and unclear support for the claimed memorization and mode-collapse explanation.

yC9G7LCefF.one_liner: Bridge-Duplex links persistent semantic memory to streaming speech generation through selective bridge attention.
yC9G7LCefF.problem: Full-duplex speech dialogue must keep evolving dialogue semantics coordinated with continuous frame-wise generation.
yC9G7LCefF.method: A dual-stream architecture shares a causal timeline through bridge attention, trains semantic evolution with dialogue next-latent prediction, and selectively retrieves semantic memory during inference.
yC9G7LCefF.key_idea: Selective bridge attention exposes persistent semantic states to frame-wise generation without attending to all semantic memory.
yC9G7LCefF.evidence: Experiments use F-Actor and a LoRA-adapted Moshi across multi-turn semantic evaluations, generated dialogues, multiple judges, and inference-cost measurements.
yC9G7LCefF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the shared causal timeline is well motivated and semantic gains recur across two backbones and several evaluation settings.
yC9G7LCefF.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the added architecture insufficiently isolated from simpler semantic-processing and memory-access alternatives.

3aOcfmRo96.one_liner: TIDE assigns delayed recommendation outcomes to memories, then evolves them through reinforcement and editing.
3aOcfmRo96.problem: Delayed, noisy recommendation feedback is confounded by context and jointly influenced memories, making memory-fitness attribution difficult.
3aOcfmRo96.method: TIDE estimates temporal, semantic, and responsibility credit for a capacity-constrained memory population, then reinforces, crosses over, mutates, or evicts entries; MEG measures later-task utility gains.
3aOcfmRo96.key_idea: Responsibility credit distributes delayed outcomes among memories referenced during generation before evolutionary memory updates.
3aOcfmRo96.evidence: Evaluation uses an e-commerce membership marketing content agent with offline temporal replay and controlled future-task studies.
3aOcfmRo96.claimed_gains: TIDE achieves a +7.75-percentage-point MEG in offline temporal replay.
3aOcfmRo96.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that feedback-driven memory evolution addresses an understudied practical problem and that responsibility attribution is a sensible mechanism.
3aOcfmRo96.main_concern: Reviewers most often report that ablations other than responsibility credit have confidence intervals including zero, leaving most components' independent benefits uncertain.

1w18Pt1d0h.one_liner: Coordinate-size analysis derives Gated Delta Network scaling rules for width-transferable learning rates.
1w18Pt1d0h.problem: Maximal Update Parametrization lacks established scaling rules for recurrent linear models with structured state transitions and gates.
1w18Pt1d0h.method: The authors propagate coordinate-size estimates through forward computation, gating, and recurrent state dynamics to derive parameterization and initialization rules for Gated Delta Networks.
1w18Pt1d0h.key_idea: Coordinate-size propagation through recurrent gates determines width exponents that preserve feature learning and learning-rate transfer.
1w18Pt1d0h.evidence: Language-model pretraining experiments sweep learning rates across model widths using both AdamW and SGD under standard and proposed parameterizations.
1w18Pt1d0h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that hyperparameter transfer for Gated Delta Networks is practically useful and empirically supported across widths and optimizers.
1w18Pt1d0h.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the rigor of the derivations and whether architectural simplifications preserve the analyzed scaling exponents.

NqKMGp6N98.one_liner: State-Jac selects flow-matching data using endpoint coverage and local velocity-response sketches.
NqKMGp6N98.problem: Static representations and sample scores miss differences in state-dependent velocity supervision when pruning conditional flow-matching data.
NqKMGp6N98.method: State-Jac combines endpoint distances with proxy-based local-response sketches in a one-shot selector while leaving final CFM training unchanged.
NqKMGp6N98.key_idea: Endpoint geometry represents zero-order supervision and local velocity response represents first-order sensitivity for sample redundancy.
NqKMGp6N98.evidence: Experiments span balanced, long-tailed, class-conditional, and larger-scale latent benchmarks, with CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-100 cost and quality measurements.
NqKMGp6N98.claimed_gains: At 20% retention, State-Jac reduces mean FID relative to random selection by 8.44% on CIFAR-10 and 6.98% on ImageNet-100, using 22.89 GPU-hours or 24.61% of full-data training cost on ImageNet-100.
NqKMGp6N98.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that CFM-specific redundancy is well motivated and that gains over random selection are consistent with low selector overhead.
NqKMGp6N98.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that the theoretical analysis does not connect the selection coverage criterion to the retrained model's field error.

OyEHqqDpeO.one_liner: TaP replays executable agent trajectories to resume verified states and allocate later attempts.
OyEHqqDpeO.problem: Text-based reuse makes agents regenerate earlier actions, so failed attempts cannot preserve exactly completed partial progress.
OyEHqqDpeO.method: TaP stores attempts as executable programs, verifies recovery points by replay, and uses cheap probes to allocate full attempts toward promising states on resettable environments.
OyEHqqDpeO.key_idea: Executable replay restores verified environment states, while probe feedback ranks recovery points for budgeted continuation.
OyEHqqDpeO.evidence: Experiments evaluate multiple models on AppWorld and BFCL-V3, including budget-matched comparisons and probe-allocation analyses.
OyEHqqDpeO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that executable recovery preserves useful work without model retraining and produces substantial gains on both benchmarks.
OyEHqqDpeO.main_concern: Reviewers most often question applicability beyond resettable, deterministic environments with partial-progress checkers, the regime used by both benchmarks.

6esPh0zPcM.one_liner: VGenST-Bench synthesizes controlled videos and hierarchical questions to diagnose spatio-temporal reasoning.
6esPh0zPcM.problem: Static images and passively curated videos limit controlled, fine-grained evaluation of spatio-temporal reasoning in MLLMs.
6esPh0zPcM.method: A multi-agent generation pipeline with human quality control produces videos and QA pairs across a 3 × 2 × 2 taxonomy of spatial scale, perspective, and scene dynamics.
6esPh0zPcM.key_idea: Scene specifications actively generate controlled visual evidence and ground truth for tasks separated into perception and reasoning levels.
6esPh0zPcM.evidence: The benchmark contains 1,200 generated videos and evaluates models with blind, single-frame, shuffled-frame, text-oracle, and answer-option controls.
6esPh0zPcM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that controllable video synthesis enables useful diagnostics, especially the answer-option tests exposing option ranking rather than video verification.
6esPh0zPcM.main_concern: Reviewers most often find validity weakly established because real-video ranking correlations use eight models and generated scenarios lack matched real-video comparisons.

Ni8Xe7OvQf.one_liner: BeliefGraph-JEPA rolls typed latent effects under future drivers and graph-routes them to targets.
Ni8Xe7OvQf.problem: Direct action conditioning leaves delayed, persistent driver effects and target-specific influences implicit in multi-target forecasting.
Ni8Xe7OvQf.method: The model factorizes driver influence into typed latent-effect states, evolves them with future drivers, routes them through a graph, and adds a capacity-controlled direct-driver residual within a JEPA predictor.
Ni8Xe7OvQf.key_idea: Future rollout of typed latent effects followed by graph routing makes driver influence target-specific and temporally explicit.
Ni8Xe7OvQf.evidence: Experiments cover four clinical, agricultural, environmental, and industrial systems with supervised and pretrained known-future-covariate baselines and matched component controls.
Ni8Xe7OvQf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that future rollout and graph routing are well motivated and supported by broad datasets and extensive matched ablations.
Ni8Xe7OvQf.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the many components insufficiently disentangled, with small gains and limited evidence for the explicit graph's contribution.

bUsa1smD4p.one_liner: Derives closed-form degree-2 density-ratio OOD detectors from unlabeled test-batch mean and covariance under a whitened Gaussian model.
bUsa1smD4p.problem: Single-sample OOD detectors ignore population-level distributional evidence present in an unlabeled test batch.
bUsa1smD4p.method: Modeling finite-resolution density-ratio estimation as deflection-maximizing polynomial readouts under a whitened Gaussian model, the paper derives a closed-form degree-2 detector using only test-batch mean and covariance.
bUsa1smD4p.key_idea: Uses closed-form degree-2 batch-mean and anisotropic batch-covariance readouts to approximate finite-resolution density ratios for OOD detection.
bUsa1smD4p.evidence: Evaluates across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet benchmarks on multiple backbones against density-ratio estimators.
bUsa1smD4p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the batch-level density-ratio formulation well motivated and the degree-2 detector simple and effective.
bUsa1smD4p.main_concern: Whitening does not guarantee Gaussian higher-order moments needed for theoretical optimality, and evaluation omits recent OOD baselines and ID class-imbalance tests.

tpLf4arC3k.one_liner: Evaluates LLM long-horizon memory organization and reuse across interactive gamified environments with linear, temporal, and graph structures.
tpLf4arC3k.problem: Static QA benchmarks measure information retention over fixed histories rather than how agents discover, organize, update, and reuse evidence interactively.
tpLf4arC3k.method: MemGround introduces gamified long-horizon environments spanning linear, temporal, and graph-structured memory, paired with a two-stage evaluation combining end-to-end task progress (QA Overall, MFU, MFCO) and process-level diagnosis.
tpLf4arC3k.key_idea: Probes interactive memory organization and reuse across evolving game states using linear, temporal, and graph-structured puzzle dependencies.
tpLf4arC3k.evidence: Evaluates frontier LLMs (including GPT 5.2, Gemini, Qwen, GLM 5.1) and agent memory systems (Mem0, A-MEM) alongside human baselines.
tpLf4arC3k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree interactive memory behavior is an important gap and value the structured dependency-graph puzzle design.
tpLf4arC3k.main_concern: Reported MFU scores mix hint-unlocked and self-unlocked fragments, QA judges are unstable, and confounding game-specific reasoning with memory structure limits diagnosis.

H3TuFiW7UB.one_liner: Formulates minimax-regret proximal policy learning via a convex observed-moment dual when outcome confounding bridges are nonunique.
H3TuFiW7UB.problem: Proximal causal inference admits nonunique outcome confounding bridges that can imply conflicting policy rankings under unmeasured confounding.
H3TuFiW7UB.method: The paper characterizes when policy value contrasts are invariant across admissible bridges and, when they are not, minimizes worst-case regret over the joint bridge set via an observed-moment dual and convex empirical program over finite policy mixtures.
H3TuFiW7UB.key_idea: Minimizes minimax regret over nonunique proximal confounding bridges using a finite-radius observed-moment dual program.
H3TuFiW7UB.evidence: Establishes root-n excess-regret bounds under finite-feature rank and interior conditions, validated on synthetic and semi-synthetic policy-learning experiments.
H3TuFiW7UB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value addressing policy choice under nonunique proximal bridges and deriving a tractable dual with root-n regret guarantees.
H3TuFiW7UB.main_concern: Minimax regret depends on an untestable user-chosen bridge norm bound B and unknown population dual radius, with large gaps between bridge regret and true causal effects.

XgsVElfyvZ.one_liner: Constructs Riemannian-geometry supernodes on clients and aggregates secure quotient-graph statistics for federated graph clustering.
XgsVElfyvZ.problem: Federated graph clustering struggles to share cross-client structural information without exposing node-level representations or assignments.
XgsVElfyvZ.method: FedSuCo learns local Riemannian node embeddings and coarsens them into supernodes via geometric renormalization, then securely aggregates supernode connectivity into a server quotient graph to send structural guidance back to clients for spherical clustering.
XgsVElfyvZ.key_idea: Coarsens local Riemannian node embeddings into supernodes and aggregates secure quotient-graph statistics for server-guided federated clustering.
XgsVElfyvZ.evidence: Evaluates on five real-world graph datasets against 13 federated baselines, including client-count, supernode-scale, and feedback ablations.
XgsVElfyvZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-motivated supernode collaboration unit, explicit semi-honest threat model, and strong performance across five benchmarks.
XgsVElfyvZ.main_concern: Server feedback causes negative transfer on CiteSeer (+5.58 ACC when removed), vMF hits OOM on few clients, and Riemannian supernode construction lacks non-Riemannian controls.

oaQb4SqHIw.one_liner: Fuses neural decoder evidence with physical motion-primitive Bayesian priors via uncertainty weighting and ELBO optimization.
oaQb4SqHIw.problem: Neural decoders for brain-computer interfaces degrade sharply under neuron dropout, noise, or missing recordings.
oaQb4SqHIw.method: MaPIC pairs a neural evidence encoder with a dynamic Bayesian prior over physical motion primitives (e.g., translation and rotation), optimizing an ELBO with a primitive-guided KL regularizer and weighting motion priors against neural observations by coordinate-wise uncertainty.
oaQb4SqHIw.key_idea: Combines a frozen or plug-and-play neural evidence encoder with a physical motion-primitive Bayesian prior weighted by predicted uncertainty.
oaQb4SqHIw.evidence: Evaluates on simulated circular/toroidal dynamical systems and rat hippocampal neural recording datasets under neuron dropout.
oaQb4SqHIw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the plug-and-play combination of neural decoding with physical motion priors appealing and effective under observation dropout.
oaQb4SqHIw.main_concern: Novelty over prior Bayesian-dynamical neural decoders is incremental, conditional independence in fusion is unjustified, and experiments rely on artificial dropout without significance tests.

RpglT9k6pU.one_liner: Infers budget-dependent dataset-pruning difficulty allocations from a single difficulty-balanced probing run instead of trial-and-error search.
RpglT9k6pU.problem: Optimal example difficulty for dataset pruning varies with budget, forcing existing methods into costly trial-and-error search over prescribed preference shapes.
RpglT9k6pU.method: Difficulty Preference Scoring (DPS) runs a single training probe on a difficulty-balanced subset and extracts training-dynamics signals (budget-conditioned difficulty and excess fitting) to infer how the pruning budget should be allocated across difficulty strata.
RpglT9k6pU.key_idea: Replaces prescribed preference search with a single difficulty-balanced probing run that infers budget-dependent stratum allocations from training dynamics.
RpglT9k6pU.evidence: Evaluates across 1%-50% budgets on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, QNLI, and SQuAD 1.1 alongside a linearized theoretical model.
RpglT9k6pU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value modeling budget-dependent difficulty preferences and replacing repeated tuning sweeps with a single probing run.
RpglT9k6pU.main_concern: Computing initial difficulty scores still requires full-dataset training, diminishing net pruning savings, and theoretical analysis relies on a simplified linear model.

j3km1Tegog.one_liner: Introduces the Real-ZAC benchmark and a cross-instance comparison baseline for zero-shot counting of intact versus defective industrial parts.
j3km1Tegog.problem: Existing object counters ignore defect states while anomaly detectors fail in dense multi-instance scenes and on unseen component classes.
j3km1Tegog.method: The paper defines Zero-shot Anomaly-Aware Counting, releases Real-ZAC with instance-level intact/defective labels and class-disjoint splits, and proposes a baseline that detects defects by comparing each instance against neighboring instances within the same image.
j3km1Tegog.key_idea: Compares each detected instance against peer instances within the same image to classify and count intact versus defective parts zero-shot.
j3km1Tegog.evidence: Evaluates on Real-ZAC across mixed-state, all-intact, and all-defective test images of unseen industrial component classes.
j3km1Tegog.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical manufacturing task and appreciate the large-scale Real-ZAC benchmark with homogeneous-state edge cases.
j3km1Tegog.main_concern: Within-image peer comparison fails when all instances are defective, headline pooled F1 hides weak defective-class F1, and mutual-matching novelty is limited.

LNDn6Nbr2h.one_liner: Amortizes causal sensitivity analysis via in-context learning on prior-data fitted networks trained with Lagrangian scalarized bounds.
LNDn6Nbr2h.problem: Existing causal sensitivity analysis methods require expensive per-instance optimization whenever the dataset, query, treatment, or sensitivity level changes.
LNDn6Nbr2h.method: The authors train a prior-data fitted network for in-context sensitivity analysis across generalized treatment sensitivity models, generating training labels via Lagrangian scalarization of effect extrema and sensitivity violations.
LNDn6Nbr2h.key_idea: Generate synthetic sensitivity-bound training labels via Lagrangian scalarization to amortize partial identification across queries and models in a single prior-data fitted network.
LNDn6Nbr2h.evidence: Convexity/linearity Pareto-frontier theory and synthetic experiments comparing against NeuralCSA across queries, sensitivity levels, and out-of-prior settings support the method.
LNDn6Nbr2h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that amortizing causal sensitivity analysis via PFNs and Lagrangian label generation is well motivated and technically sound.
LNDn6Nbr2h.main_concern: Reviewers point out that evaluation relies solely on synthetic data with weak baselines (only NeuralCSA), omits closed-form validation of label quality, and degrades outside the training prior.

vjlySubLoj.one_liner: Couples neural subsystem macromodels with physics-based subsystems inside a Newton-Raphson solver via shared boundary variables.
vjlySubLoj.problem: Pure physics solvers are slow on nonlinear or exogenous subsystems, while black-box neural surrogates violate conservation laws and fail under topology changes.
vjlySubLoj.method: PHySIM partitions networked systems into physics-based and DNN-based subsystems coupled at inference through shared boundary state variables inside a Newton-Raphson loop.
vjlySubLoj.key_idea: Embed modular device-level neural surrogates alongside first-principles models inside a unified Newton-Raphson solver enforcing boundary conservation.
vjlySubLoj.evidence: Experiments across power grids, gas pipeline networks, and analog circuits, plus theoretical stability analyses in the appendix, support the framework.
vjlySubLoj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical engineering motivation and broad multi-domain evaluation across power, gas, and circuit networks.
vjlySubLoj.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over prior solver-embedded neural constitutive models, note weak global baselines, and point out gaps in Newton convergence and runtime profiling claims.

VDdXI0OSRx.one_liner: Jointly calibrates rotation matrices, differentiable 2:4 sparse masks, and quantization parameters using Probability-aware Balanced Group Separation.
VDdXI0OSRx.problem: Rotation-based quantization smooths weights to reduce outliers, which destroys the local weight contrast needed for stable N:M semi-structured pruning.
VDdXI0OSRx.method: The authors propose SparRotQuant, incorporating N:M sparsity into rotation calibration by learning differentiable masks while adapting rotations and quantization parameters, guided by Probability-aware Balanced Group Separation (PBGS) combining retention probability and Hessian sensitivity.
VDdXI0OSRx.key_idea: Optimizing differentiable N:M masks jointly with rotation matrices under a group-separation loss aligns sparse support with rotated low-bit weights.
VDdXI0OSRx.evidence: Evaluations across four LLM families under W4A4KV16 and W4A4KV4 settings plus RTX 4090 kernel speedup benchmarks.
VDdXI0OSRx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the tension between rotation smoothing and N:M contrast well-motivated and observe consistent improvements over sparse SpinQuant across models.
VDdXI0OSRx.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about missing comparisons to related rotation-pruning methods (DenoiseRotator, RotPruner), incomplete PBGS ablations, limited pruning scope, and unexplained kernel speedup details.

tn62XO1hig.one_liner: Unifies long-horizon tool-agent data synthesis, SFT filtering, and RL rewards using executable environments and exact state-change targets.
tn62XO1hig.problem: Synthesizing long-horizon tool-use training data is hindered by unreachable goals and action-matching metrics that reject valid alternative trajectories.
tn62XO1hig.method: StateForge builds executable state-space environments, executes dependency-guided workflows to establish reachable state-change targets across Direct, Progressive, and Recovery modes, and uses exact state-change matching for SFT filtering and RL rewards.
tn62XO1hig.key_idea: Derives reachable final state-change targets from executable workflows to unify task synthesis, trajectory filtering, and outcome-based RL rewards.
tn62XO1hig.evidence: Produces 544 environments and 1,697 tasks (averaging 69 tool calls) and evaluates a 4B model on tau^2-Bench and DeepPlanning Shopping.
tn62XO1hig.claimed_gains: With 4B parameters, attains 91.17% macro-average success on tau^2-Bench and 43.33% accuracy on DeepPlanning Shopping.
tn62XO1hig.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value unifying synthesis, filtering, and RL around outcome-based state changes across realistic Progressive and Recovery modes.
tn62XO1hig.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental novelty over prior graph/state synthesis works and missing ablations comparing exact state-change filtering/rewards against simpler alternatives.

zfaD5BrWmv.one_liner: Factorizes object slots into geometry, occupancy, and appearance with adaptive fusion for latent-action world modeling.
zfaD5BrWmv.problem: Homogeneous object slots entangle geometry, shape, and appearance, forcing inverse dynamics models to extract action-relevant cues implicitly.
zfaD5BrWmv.method: FOCWM decomposes each object slot into spatial geometry, occupancy, and appearance factors, and uses an action-oriented adaptive fusion mechanism to weight factors for latent-action inference. The inferred latent actions and factorized states predict future object states.
zfaD5BrWmv.key_idea: Decomposes object slots into spatial geometry, occupancy, and appearance factors and adaptively fuses them per object for latent-action inference.
zfaD5BrWmv.evidence: Video prediction and downstream behavior learning experiments across four synthetic and real-world manipulation datasets against PlaySlot and LPWM, plus factor ablations.
zfaD5BrWmv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that FOCWM improves video prediction metrics and inference efficiency over PlaySlot and LPWM with a clean design.
zfaD5BrWmv.main_concern: Reviewers note that holistic-slot ablations already beat baselines, adaptive fusion gains are small, and pixel metrics do not isolate object geometry or motion.

KZ3uDb9WXb.one_liner: Trains local direct feedback pathways with orthogonality regularization so feedback weights track transposed forward weights.
KZ3uDb9WXb.problem: Direct feedback alignment (DFA) uses fixed random feedback weights that fail to adapt to evolving forward weights, hurting deep network accuracy.
KZ3uDb9WXb.method: Direct Feedback Propagation (DFP) introduces local losses on feedback connections whose equilibrium matches the chain of transposed forward weights under timescale separation, paired with an orthogonality loss on forward weights to bound nonlinear error.
KZ3uDb9WXb.key_idea: Updates direct feedback matrices via local losses toward the transposed forward-weight product while regularizing forward weights to be orthogonal.
KZ3uDb9WXb.evidence: Supported by timescale-separation equilibrium and error-bound theory, plus five-seed experiments across VGG/other architectures (including Tiny ImageNet) and multi-GPU wall-clock measurements.
KZ3uDb9WXb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear mathematical formulation, parallel activity-independent feedback updates, and strong Tiny ImageNet and multi-GPU runtime results.
KZ3uDb9WXb.main_concern: Reviewers note narrow comparisons limited to direct-feedback variants (omitting Forward-Forward, FOTON, and blockwise local learning) and unisolated effects of initialization and orthogonality regularization.

rGJ3ng2Yv4.one_liner: Introduces the UAVReason aerial reasoning-and-generation dataset and adapts Bagel as a unified baseline.
rGJ3ng2Yv4.problem: Vision-language models remain brittle on high-altitude nadir-view UAV scenes with tiny, dense objects, repetitive textures, and ambiguous orientations.
rGJ3ng2Yv4.method: The authors build UAVReason, aligning aerial RGB, depth, segmentation, captions, and VQA pairs, and fine-tune UAVReason-Bagel jointly on language reasoning and dense visual generation objectives.
rGJ3ng2Yv4.key_idea: Constructs an aligned multi-modal UAV dataset (RGB, depth, segmentation, VQA) and jointly fine-tunes a unified VLM/generator baseline on aerial reasoning and synthesis.
rGJ3ng2Yv4.evidence: Evaluated on UAVReason across single-frame VQA, two-frame temporal VQA, heading-aware VQA, segmentation, and conditional RGB synthesis.
rGJ3ng2Yv4.claimed_gains: UAVReason-Bagel increases VQA-1F F1 from 0.394 to 0.711, VQA-2F F1 from 0.427 to 0.822, heading-aware VQA F1 from 0.798 to 0.973, improves segmentation mIoU to 0.143, and reduces KID from 0.078 to 0.048.
rGJ3ng2Yv4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree UAV aerial understanding is an important challenge and value the unified, geometrically grounded UAVReason dataset.
rGJ3ng2Yv4.main_concern: All reviewers flag that the claimed bidirectional synergy between reasoning and generation is unsupported because joint training underperforms reasoning-only training on all VQA F1 metrics; one reviewer also notes missing human audit of generated QA.

SycfZ4UmJD.one_liner: Applies block-wise randomized Hadamard transforms across the token dimension to improve low-bit activation quantization in diffusion LLMs.
SycfZ4UmJD.problem: Diffusion language model activations vary across token positions and denoising states, limiting the effectiveness of channel-only quantization transforms.
SycfZ4UmJD.method: BTT applies invertible block-wise randomized Hadamard transforms across simultaneously processed tokens before activation quantization and restores coordinates after linear projection, selecting transforms per operator via calibration reconstruction loss with an identity fallback.
SycfZ4UmJD.key_idea: Applies invertible block-wise Hadamard transforms across the token dimension before activation quantization, selected per layer by reconstruction loss.
SycfZ4UmJD.evidence: W4A4 quantization experiments adding BTT to QuaRot and DuQuant on diffusion language models including Dream.
SycfZ4UmJD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the token-dimension orthogonal transformation simple, mathematically sound, and compatible with existing channel-wise quantization methods.
SycfZ4UmJD.main_concern: The adaptive selection and identity fallback are inconsistently validated at the full-model level, and experiments omit comparisons with recent dLLM-specific quantization methods.

87sRhZs4hM.one_liner: Detects LLM hallucinations by summarizing six activation streams into under 1,000 leading-digit, Benford, and moment coordinates.
87sRhZs4hM.problem: Neuron-aligned activation probes require tens of thousands of model-specific coordinates that lack cross-model meaning for hallucination detection.
87sRhZs4hM.method: DigitTrace reduces six activation streams at every fourth layer into leading-digit frequencies, Benford-reference statistics, and activation moments, accumulating them across generation into a permutation-invariant trace under 1,000 coordinates.
87sRhZs4hM.key_idea: Summarizes LLM activation streams during generation via leading-digit distributions, Benford statistics, and moments into a <1,000-coordinate probe trace.
87sRhZs4hM.evidence: Evaluated against seven detectors across three models, eight benchmarks, and 50 splits with shared generations.
87sRhZs4hM.claimed_gains: Comes within 0.55 AUROC points of the best neuron-aligned detector using one tenth as many coordinates, and gains 10.37 points from early to late generation.
87sRhZs4hM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the careful, well-controlled 50-split evaluation protocol and the compact, one-pass, permutation-invariant representation.
87sRhZs4hM.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations show activation moments alone achieve 76.16 vs. 76.68 AUROC for full DigitTrace (and tuned raw probes reach 78.75-81.2), meaning leading digits add ~0.5 AUROC.

C9LBK4Wcqc.one_liner: Trains visual backbones with source-discriminative, destylized-triplet, and style-confusion losses to trace stylized images to exact sources.
C9LBK4Wcqc.problem: Pretrained visual encoders are sensitive to artistic style shifts, hindering exact-source retrieval for generatively stylized images.
C9LBK4Wcqc.method: The authors build MSIR-Bench (56K images from 5,500 sources across 25 styles and 5 editors) and propose Destylized Feature Learning (DFL), combining Source Discriminative Loss, Destylized Triplet Loss, and Style Confusion Regularization.
C9LBK4Wcqc.key_idea: Jointly optimizes source discrimination, destylized triplet margins, and style confusion regularization on visual backbones to retrieve exact sources under restyling.
C9LBK4Wcqc.evidence: Evaluated across seven visual backbones on MSIR-Bench under seen, unseen-source, unseen-style, and degraded-gallery settings.
C9LBK4Wcqc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree MSIR-Bench is a valuable, well-designed provenance benchmark and that DFL consistently improves Top-1 accuracy across all seven tested backbones.
C9LBK4Wcqc.main_concern: Reviewers view DFL as an incremental metric-learning recipe (with small per-component gains) and note missing modern encoders like DINOv3, qualitative examples, and multi-photo identity controls.

2aNaaxtGMB.one_liner: Decodes LDPC codes via iterative weight-tied factorized gated message passing with source emission and destination acceptance gates.
2aNaaxtGMB.problem: Recent neural LDPC decoders require large parameter counts and incur high computational cost during test-time scaling.
2aNaaxtGMB.method: They propose Iterative Factorized Gated Message Passing (I-FGMP), which decomposes adaptive message passing into source-side emission modulation, graph-structured aggregation, and destination-side acceptance gating, trained via finite-depth weight-tied unrolling.
2aNaaxtGMB.key_idea: Decomposes graph message passing into source-side emission modulation and destination-side acceptance gating within a weight-tied iterative unrolling loop.
2aNaaxtGMB.evidence: Evaluations on short LDPC codes and medium/long codes comparing against Transformer-based decoders and conventional belief propagation.
2aNaaxtGMB.claimed_gains: I-FGMP trained for 12 iterations outperforms recent Transformer-based decoders with less than 1/10 the parameters and at most 4/5 the FLOPs of all baselines.
2aNaaxtGMB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree I-FGMP achieves lower error rates with fewer parameters and FLOPs on short LDPC codes and supports test-time iteration scaling.
2aNaaxtGMB.main_concern: Evaluations focus mainly on short codes without comparing neural baselines on medium/long codes or reporting hardware latency and standard FER/BER curves.

LjMXwTk8Xy.one_liner: Prunes structured groups at factorization depth two for KKT-certified selection before lifting to deeper multiplicative gating.
LjMXwTk8Xy.problem: Deep multiplicative gating traps zeroed weights as stationary points regardless of data justification, preventing certification of whether a structured group removal was warranted.
LjMXwTk8Xy.method: The authors prove that data gradients enter the Hessian at a zeroed group only at factorization depth D=2 (matching group-lasso KKT optimality), whereas D>=3 creates a data-independent local minimum. Certified Progressive Gating (CPG) trains at D=2 to decide and certify removals, then exactly rewrites the network to deeper D for aggressive sparsification.
LjMXwTk8Xy.key_idea: Exploits the depth-two Hessian dichotomy to certify group-lasso KKT optimality of zeroed groups before re-lifting the factorization to deeper gating.
LjMXwTk8Xy.evidence: Theoretical proofs and controlled experiments on synthetic data, convolutional networks (including ResNet-56 on CIFAR-10), and BERT.
LjMXwTk8Xy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical depth dichotomy explaining optimization geometry at zeroed groups across factorization depths is clean and correct.
LjMXwTk8Xy.main_concern: Reviewers point out the certificate is a passive label that is not enforced in the default algorithm (enforcing it hurts accuracy) and fails to accurately reflect correct removals under SGD.

CCYqFKiO5V.one_liner: Analyzes factorization depth L in mergeable deep LoRA as an implicit spectral regularization dimension.
CCYqFKiO5V.problem: Deep low-rank adaptations treat factorization depth as a fixed choice rather than a tunable regularization dimension.
CCYqFKiO5V.method: The authors study a mergeable L-factor LoRA parameterization through representation cost, optimization geometry, and singular-mode dynamics, predicting that depth slows weak singular directions and concentrates the spectrum.
CCYqFKiO5V.key_idea: Uses L-factor matrix factorization depth in LoRA to slow gradient learning of weak singular directions under a fixed training budget.
CCYqFKiO5V.evidence: Tested via capacity-controlled comparisons (parameter-matched LoRA r8 and rank-matched LoRA r4), depth ablations, spectral diagnostics, and synthetic experiments.
CCYqFKiO5V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the perspective of factorization depth as a non-monotonic regularization dimension interesting and appreciate the dual capacity controls.
CCYqFKiO5V.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparison to Deep LoRA, single shared learning-rate tuning across tasks, and poor readability of figures and convoluted prose.

7UXKgr1Akp.one_liner: Allocates tasks for alternating model and harness co-evolution using counterpart update effects and intervention-weighted failure attribution.
7UXKgr1Akp.problem: In long-horizon model-harness co-evolution, feeding all trajectories to both updates causes collapse while static attribution rules saturate.
7UXKgr1Akp.method: CoEvo-RSI alternates model post-training and harness evolution, scoring each task for the receiving component based on the measured effect of the counterpart's latest update and failure attribution weighted by prior intervention outcomes.
7UXKgr1Akp.key_idea: Routes trajectories to model or harness updates by scoring counterpart update effects and intervention-weighted failure attribution.
7UXKgr1Akp.evidence: Evaluated over 40 rounds across four benchmarks against existing co-evolution and recursive self-improvement baselines, plus allocation-rule and replay ablations.
7UXKgr1Akp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that long-horizon model-harness co-evolution is an important problem and appreciate the 40-round empirical evaluation.
7UXKgr1Akp.main_concern: Reviewers note unclear presentation lacking an overview figure, missing matched-budget sequential baselines, small gains from adaptive weighting over fixed replay (44.6 vs 43.8), and lack of convergence justification.

ACtRUJQqsP.one_liner: Calibrates merged models by learning low-dimensional linear bridges between fixed SVD error subspaces derived from expert-merged weight differences.
ACtRUJQqsP.problem: Post-merging representation calibration improves multi-task merged models, but standard alignment objectives do not specify which feature directions to correct.
ACtRUJQqsP.method: ESCal computes fixed error-subspace bases from the SVD of weight differences between individual experts and the merged model. At each intermediate block boundary, a learned linear Bridge module projects representations onto the next block's input error subspace and adds a correction in the current block's output error subspace using small per-task calibration sets.
ACtRUJQqsP.key_idea: Using fixed SVD subspaces of expert-merged weight differences to parameterize low-rank cross-layer linear calibration bridges.
ACtRUJQqsP.evidence: Evaluated across ViT and RoBERTa architectures, multiple merging methods (Task Arithmetic, TIES, WUDI), and vision/NLU benchmarks.
ACtRUJQqsP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using weight-difference SVD subspaces for parameter-efficient calibration is intuitive and shows consistent gains across architectures and merging methods.
ACtRUJQqsP.main_concern: Reviewers view the method as an incremental extension of SURGERY/SURGERYV2 with modest accuracy gains over strong calibration baselines and insufficient validation of the cross-layer pairing.

gyhj8oCfNR.one_liner: Introduces a 257-QA multimodal scientific fact-checking benchmark annotating premise-conclusion dependency graphs and Invalid Support errors.
gyhj8oCfNR.problem: Atomic claim-level fact-checking evaluates claims independently, missing Invalid Support where a locally supported conclusion relies on a contradicted or unverifiable premise.
gyhj8oCfNR.method: The authors curate MMSciFact from 45 mostly computer-science papers, comprising 257 MLLM-generated QA pairs and 2,737 sentences annotated by experts with grounding labels, sentence roles, and dependency graphs. They evaluate 12 MLLM fact-checkers across single-page, cross-page, and full-paper evidence settings.
gyhj8oCfNR.key_idea: Annotating natural MLLM long-form scientific answers with premise-conclusion dependency graphs to detect Invalid Support failures.
gyhj8oCfNR.evidence: Evaluated 12 MLLM fact-checkers across three verification settings and three evidence scopes on 257 QA pairs (2,737 sentences).
gyhj8oCfNR.claimed_gains: Comprises 257 question-answer pairs and 2,737 sentences from 45 papers.
gyhj8oCfNR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that MMSciFact targets a genuine blind spot in atomic fact-checking with high-quality expert annotations on uncorrupted model answers.
gyhj8oCfNR.main_concern: Reviewers question whether Invalid Support measures reasoning rather than factuality, note that its two sub-causes are conflated in main tables, and point out a missing deterministic rule-propagation baseline.

sN2eYUoWvb.one_liner: Shows spiking LLM scaling laws hold under static accumulate-then-fire conversion but become conditional under online charge-and-fire dynamics.
sN2eYUoWvb.problem: It remains unclear whether Spiking LLMs follow universal scaling laws like standard LLMs or break down under asynchronous neuromorphic temporal dynamics.
sN2eYUoWvb.method: The authors separate Spiking LLMs into static accumulate-then-fire (ATF) conversion, which acts as a static quantizer, and temporal online charge-and-fire (OCF) dynamics. They derive representation-plus-temporal error bounds and sweep models up to 30B parameters across three neuron families and three corpora.
sN2eYUoWvb.key_idea: Distinguishing static accumulate-then-fire quantization from asynchronous online charge-and-fire dynamics to characterize conditional scaling laws in spiking LLMs.
sN2eYUoWvb.evidence: Theoretical error decomposition and empirical sweeps across models up to 30B, three corpora, and three neuron/encoding families.
sN2eYUoWvb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating static ATF quantization from temporal OCF dynamics is a clear, healthy framing for studying spiking LLM scaling.
sN2eYUoWvb.main_concern: Reviewers note that power laws are fitted in broken high-perplexity regimes (5–7 nats excess loss), single-neuron MSE proofs lack a rigorous link to global cross-entropy, and Theorem 3.1 only gives a sufficient condition.

GrDr8yJVxM.one_liner: Formulates generative trajectory learning as a path-dependent McKean-Vlasov control problem solved via an FBSDE neural solver.
GrDr8yJVxM.problem: Generative dynamics models supervised only by marginal distributions cannot distinguish path-dependent temporal structures in discretely observed trajectories.
GrDr8yJVxM.method: The authors formulate a path-dependent McKean-Vlasov control problem combining continuous-time marginal soft-law constraints with discrete-time MMD path-law supervision. The resulting optimality system is a McKean-Vlasov FBSDE with conditional adjoint jumps at observation dates, solved by a sample-based neural solver with causal history compression.
GrDr8yJVxM.key_idea: Solving a path-dependent McKean-Vlasov FBSDE with adjoint jumps at observation times to jointly enforce marginal and path-law constraints.
GrDr8yJVxM.evidence: Local well-posedness proof for MMD path-law constraints and proof-of-concept experiments on synthetic transport, latent face transport, and AMASS human motion.
GrDr8yJVxM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formulating generative dynamics with both marginal and path-law constraints via McKean-Vlasov control is a valuable, underexplored direction.
GrDr8yJVxM.main_concern: Reviewers note limited proof-of-concept experiments lacking comparisons to modern baselines, unclear algorithmic convergence guarantees, and dense, symbol-heavy presentation.

VziUqXGo5c.one_liner: Trains a question-conditioned image warp proposer and native-relative candidate selector using frozen MLLM answer likelihoods.
VziUqXGo5c.problem: MLLMs with fixed visual-token budgets undersample question-relevant details, while attention-guided warping and cropping fail to predict which deformation improves decoded answers.
VziUqXGo5c.method: QGVR uses a two-stage pipeline without modifying the frozen MLLM: Stage I trains a warp proposal network on ViT features supervised by answer likelihoods, and Stage II learns a candidate selector over the native image, base warp, and eight fixed edits to rank warps or fall back to the native image.
VziUqXGo5c.key_idea: Using frozen MLLM answer likelihoods to supervise a full-frame image warp proposer and a native-relative fallback candidate selector.
VziUqXGo5c.evidence: Evaluated on five InternVL benchmarks and five LLaVA benchmarks with paired bootstrap intervals and online-cost measurements.
VziUqXGo5c.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest reported scores on all five InternVL benchmarks and four of five LLaVA benchmarks in the paper's comparison.
VziUqXGo5c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reallocating visual sampling density via answer-supervised warping with native fallback is an interesting alternative to cropping under fixed token budgets.
VziUqXGo5c.main_concern: Reviewers question the marginal end-to-end benefit of VJP-guided supervision (+0.64% Oracle@10 over random), the necessity of a learned selector over training-free rules, and formatting/clarity issues.

X2Wo0zeGy5.one_liner: Alternates graph probability propagation with mass-preserving node-wise sharpening to refine frozen node classifiers without retraining.
X2Wo0zeGy5.problem: Post-hoc graph propagation of frozen classifier outputs suffers from over-smoothing at large depths and degrades under severe feature corruption.
X2Wo0zeGy5.method: Motivated by decomposing the relaxed Potts energy into Dirichlet smoothness and Gini indecision terms, Propagate, Then Sharpen (PtS) alternates class-probability propagation with a mass-preserving node-wise sharpening step that has a local KL-Gini descent guarantee and one validation-tuned hyperparameter.
X2Wo0zeGy5.key_idea: Interleaves graph probability propagation with a single-parameter, mass-preserving node-wise sharpening update motivated by Potts Dirichlet-plus-Gini decomposition.
X2Wo0zeGy5.evidence: Local majorization proof and evaluations across nine homophilic graphs with frozen MLP, GCN, and GraphSAGE backbones under clean and Gaussian-corrupted features, plus depth and heterophilic controls.
X2Wo0zeGy5.claimed_gains: Across nine homophilic graphs with a frozen MLP backbone, PtS improves mean test accuracy over independently tuned APPNP by 1.71 percentage points on clean inputs and 3.90 under severe Gaussian feature corruption, dropping 2.2 points between 2 and 100 steps without restart versus 33.8 for APPNP.
X2Wo0zeGy5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the simplicity, clear input requirements, honest reporting of negative results (e.g., heterophilic graphs and ogbn-products), and systematic ablations.
X2Wo0zeGy5.main_concern: Reviewers question the Potts-energy motivation since PtS does not minimize the global energy, note missing controls against simple temperature sharpening or thresholding, and cite overlap with prior propagation-sharpening methods.

3Tk6smNAk5.one_liner: Analyzes how covariance-power preconditioning induces a controllable spectral bias in neural feature learning and generalization.
3Tk6smNAk5.problem: While preconditioning is widely used to speed up empirical risk minimization, its effect on feature learning and expected-risk generalization is underexplored.
3Tk6smNAk5.method: The authors show that input information enters training only through the preconditioner-induced Gram matrix, and prove for a single ReLU neuron with p-th power input-covariance preconditioning that increasing p shifts learned sensitivity toward higher-variance eigenspaces despite identical limiting population loss. They empirically test how this bias interacts with task features across noise robustness, OOD generalization, and transfer.
3Tk6smNAk5.key_idea: Characterizes preconditioning as a metric-induced Gram-matrix spectral bias and proves monotonic eigenspace sensitivity shifts under p-th power covariance preconditioners.
3Tk6smNAk5.evidence: Single-ReLU-neuron theory and controlled experiments on label-noise robustness, OOD generalization, and forward knowledge transfer including CNN checks.
3Tk6smNAk5.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers value the clear intuition and controlled experiments showing how covariance-power preconditioning shifts spectral feature preference depending on task alignment.
3Tk6smNAk5.main_concern: Reviewers point out restrictive theoretical assumptions (input-only preconditioners independent of gradients/parameters, single-eigenvector targets, and inconsistent initialization assumptions) that leave a gap to practical adaptive optimizers.

QgV5Og4pbL.one_liner: Routes internal LLM activations across localized cognitive-function heads during prefill to match human-derived reasoning order.
QgV5Og4pbL.problem: Chain-of-Thought leaves an LLM's latent computation constrained by a fixed layer-wise order that may misalign with the functional dependencies of a reasoning task.
QgV5Og4pbL.method: Chain-of-Cognition (CoC) derives a cognitive ordering from human-verified reasoning decompositions, localizes internal regions associated with each cognitive function, and dynamically routes representations across regions at inference time without updating model parameters. For instance, it routes deeper semantic-understanding activations back to mathematical-calculation regions.
QgV5Og4pbL.key_idea: Localizes attention heads per cognitive function and selectively feeds deeper activations back to earlier layers at prefill to follow a human-derived cognitive ordering.
QgV5Og4pbL.evidence: Training-free inference experiments across multiple LLMs (8 models) and vision-language models on diverse reasoning benchmarks, plus permutation ablations.
QgV5Og4pbL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the training-free, prefill-only cross-layer routing idea interesting and note consistent average accuracy gains across multiple models and modalities.
QgV5Og4pbL.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the role of human cognitive ordering is not isolated from generic activation feedback, citing weak random-permutation controls, fragile head localization ties, and unsubstantiated mapping of human sub-steps to single-pass layer depth.

RPCQEuqhrz.one_liner: Compresses differentially private images by combining an extended Poisson private representation with DiffC diffusion coding.
RPCQEuqhrz.problem: Releasing high-dimensional differentially private data such as images requires prohibitive storage because existing compressors lack formal privacy guarantees.
RPCQEuqhrz.method: DP-DiPP extends the Poisson private representation (PPR) with a step-limited variant and Laplace targets to stochastically encode outputs of privacy mechanisms. It integrates this coder with DiffC, a diffusion-based lossy compressor, giving direct control over the rate-privacy-utility trade-off.
RPCQEuqhrz.key_idea: Encodes differentially private diffusion trajectories using a step-limited Poisson private representation combined with DiffC lossy image compression.
RPCQEuqhrz.evidence: Formal local differential privacy proofs and privatized image classification experiments on CIFAR-10.
RPCQEuqhrz.claimed_gains: On privatized CIFAR-10 image classification, DP-DiPP achieves 10–30 times better compression than the baseline while retaining comparable privacy guarantees and utility.
RPCQEuqhrz.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers credit the meaningful complexity-reducing extension of PPR, formal LDP framework, and favorable compression-utility results against baselines.
RPCQEuqhrz.main_concern: Reviewers question whether per-pixel local DP provides meaningful image privacy when compression exploits cross-pixel correlations, and note a proof gap and fixed calibration KL-budget mismatch in Theorem 3.1.

ZCJ8N4y9BC.one_liner: Improves low-bit image restoration PTQ by shifting a persistent token-shared activation direction outside the quantizer and optimizing residual bounds.
ZCJ8N4y9BC.problem: Ultra-low-bit post-training quantization of image restoration models—especially Mamba-based ones—suffers severe fidelity drops from channel-wise outliers that cannot simply be clipped without losing quality.
ZCJ8N4y9BC.method: The authors show that activation outliers form a persistent, token-shared dominant direction (the pedestal) that is highly sensitive to quantization error. PSG combines Pedestal Shifting, which keeps this directional component outside the quantizer to shrink the activation range, with GRILL, which calibrates residual activation and weight quantization bounds via closed-form updates.
ZCJ8N4y9BC.key_idea: Extracts and shifts a persistent token-shared outlier direction (pedestal) outside the quantizer while using closed-form updates (GRILL) to calibrate residual quantization bounds.
ZCJ8N4y9BC.evidence: Evaluated at 2 and 3 bits across three Mamba backbones, SwinIR, and three image restoration tasks with perturbation diagnostics.
ZCJ8N4y9BC.claimed_gains: PSG delivers up to 3.73 dB higher PSNR at 2 bits over existing PTQ methods across evaluated image restoration tasks.
ZCJ8N4y9BC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying the quantization-sensitive persistent activation direction is an interesting observation and that PSG achieves strong 2- and 3-bit restoration gains.
ZCJ8N4y9BC.main_concern: Multiple reviewers argue that Pedestal Shifting is closely related to existing per-channel shifting (such as OS+ and DFQ) and lacks a direct per-channel mean-shifting baseline to justify the single-direction constraint.

2xmLYTBSiF.one_liner: Coordinates on-policy self-distillation targets and token weights using a task-conditioned privileged residual and a conflict-bounded KL projection.
2xmLYTBSiF.problem: On-policy self-distillation performance depends jointly on constructing transferable privileged targets and allocating training weights across response tokens without destabilizing student behavior.
2xmLYTBSiF.method: TransCAP computes a shared task-conditioned residual contrasting task-plus-privilege predictions against a privilege-only reference to reweight a task-only anchor and set initial position priorities. A constrained KL projection then adjusts token weights to bound local directional conflict at the current student distribution while preventing over-concentration.
2xmLYTBSiF.key_idea: Uses a task-conditioned privileged residual to jointly form token supervision targets and initial weights, then projects weights under KL constraints bounding local directional conflict.
2xmLYTBSiF.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, and Qwen3.5-27B across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and function-calling benchmarks with ablation studies.
2xmLYTBSiF.claimed_gains: On Qwen3.5-9B, TransCAP reaches 80.65% reasoning and 72.22% code averages, outperforming the strongest baselines by 6.58 and 4.32 percentage points.
2xmLYTBSiF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly optimizing what to distill and where to allocate token weight in on-policy self-distillation is well motivated and yields promising empirical gains across scales.
2xmLYTBSiF.main_concern: Reviewers criticize dense, hard-to-follow presentation, lack of general-capability preservation tests (e.g., MMLU/IFEval) and multi-seed runs, and weak evidence that output-space conflict prevents parameter interference.

k3yYqtCFkm.one_liner: Accelerates pretrained raster-scan autoregressive image generators via post-training adaptation with a branched vertical head and learned fusion gate.
k3yYqtCFkm.problem: Sequential raster-scan autoregressive image generators are slow at inference, while existing parallel alternatives often require costly pretraining from scratch or alter prediction objectives.
k3yYqtCFkm.method: FlashAR adapts pretrained raster-scan autoregressive models to two-way diagonal parallel decoding by retaining the original horizontal head and branching a lightweight vertical head from a pre-final layer to avoid horizontal bias. A learnable fusion gate combines horizontal and vertical predictions across target positions.
k3yYqtCFkm.key_idea: Branches a column-wise vertical prediction head from a pre-final layer of a pretrained raster-scan AR model and combines it with the original horizontal head via a learned fusion gate.
k3yYqtCFkm.evidence: Evaluated across four LlamaGen scales and two large text-to-image models (including 34B Emu3.5-Image) with branching, gating, and schedule ablations.
k3yYqtCFkm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adapting existing large pretrained AR image models to achieve ~13× speedup at much lower cost than training from scratch has strong practical value.
k3yYqtCFkm.main_concern: All three reviewers note heavy architectural overlap with NAR (two-way diagonal decoding), missing comparisons against direct baselines like ZipAR and DiDA, and incomplete accounting of 34B adaptation cost.

GhX94hapxT.one_liner: Uses bilevel optimization over simulated conversion to implant backdoors that stay dormant in ANNs and activate after ANN-to-SNN conversion.
GhX94hapxT.problem: Security analyses of ANN-to-SNN conversion are lacking, leaving open whether an ANN that passes clean and backdoor screening can become malicious after conversion to an SNN.
GhX94hapxT.method: A2S-Attack formulates a bilevel optimization problem where the upper level trains the released ANN weights and the lower level simulates ANN-to-SNN conversion on surrogate calibration data. The objective preserves clean accuracy in both models while suppressing trigger activation in the ANN and activating the target backdoor in the converted SNN.
GhX94hapxT.key_idea: Optimizes released ANN weights through a bilevel objective simulating ANN-to-SNN conversion so the same trigger remains dormant in the ANN but activates in the converted SNN.
GhX94hapxT.evidence: Evaluated across four image datasets, four CNN/ViT architectures, and four MTH conversion configurations under matched, unknown-configuration, private-calibration, and ANN-screening settings.
GhX94hapxT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that demonstrating backdoors that remain dormant in ANNs and activate upon ANN-to-SNN conversion is an interesting security threat backed by consistent empirical results.
GhX94hapxT.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to existing transformation-activated backdoors (quantization, distillation, fine-tuning) and note limited generalization since all experiments only test MTH conversion.

Ko5cJnKWcP.one_liner: Performs CAD panoptic symbol spotting via bidirectional multiscale point-image fusion and combined radius-bounded primitive and window image attention.
Ko5cJnKWcP.problem: Vector-only CAD panoptic symbol spotting methods miss complementary raster visual context needed to recognize countable instances and uncountable stuff from strokes and layouts.
Ko5cJnKWcP.method: The framework combines Hierarchical Point-Image Fusion (HPIF), which exchanges spatially aligned geometric point features and multiscale image features bidirectionally across backbones, with Primitive-Oriented Context Enhancement (POCE). POCE pairs radius-bounded attention over same-layer primitives with regular and shifted window attention on image features.
Ko5cJnKWcP.key_idea: Exchanges multiscale vector-primitive and raster-image features bidirectionally (HPIF) before enhancing local context via same-layer radius-bounded primitive attention and shifted-window image attention (POCE).
Ko5cJnKWcP.evidence: Evaluated on FloorPlanCAD and ArchCAD-Public benchmarks with module-wise and directional ablation studies.
Ko5cJnKWcP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that fusing vector geometry with raster context is well aligned with CAD drawings and delivers consistent PQ improvements on FloorPlanCAD and ArchCAD-Public.
Ko5cJnKWcP.main_concern: All three reviewers cite limited novelty over existing fusion/attention modules, small gains from POCE (0.37 PQ) and bidirectional fusion (0.17 PQ) without multi-run variance, and missing computational cost comparisons.

URDLFvUFiF.one_liner: Improves post-hoc OOD detection by selecting the intermediate layer with the sharpest entropy-density drop and concatenating it with penultimate features.
URDLFvUFiF.problem: Distance-based post-hoc OOD detectors typically rely only on penultimate features, where class-discriminative optimization suppresses lower-level cues useful for detecting distribution shifts.
URDLFvUFiF.method: Layer Selection and Fusion (LSF) computes layer-wise entropy density using only in-distribution data, selects the intermediate layer exhibiting the largest consecutive drop in entropy density, and concatenates its features with the penultimate layer for distance-based scoring.
URDLFvUFiF.key_idea: Selects an intermediate layer via maximum consecutive in-distribution entropy-density drop and concatenates it with penultimate features to preserve distinct feature spaces for OOD scoring.
URDLFvUFiF.evidence: Theoretical analysis plus post-hoc OOD detection experiments across ViT, Swin, and ConvNeXt backbones on OpenOOD near-OOD, far-OOD, and covariate-shift benchmarks.
URDLFvUFiF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that LSF is a clean, lightweight post-hoc layer-selection and concatenation method requiring only in-distribution data and minimal overhead.
URDLFvUFiF.main_concern: Reviewers raise weak theoretical justification for the entropy-density criterion, framing issues around treating LSF+Mahalanobis as a standalone detector, and treating semantically ID covariate-shifted sets (ImageNet-C/R/V2) as OOD.

XjhvjWjujT.one_liner: Enables memory-efficient decentralized full-parameter LLM fine-tuning on non-IID data via sequential block-wise Adam with consensus-corrected moments.
XjhvjWjujT.problem: Decentralized full-parameter LLM fine-tuning is memory-prohibitive on billion-scale models and prone to client drift on non-IID data, forcing prior methods to rely on parameter-efficient updates.
XjhvjWjujT.method: DECA partitions LLM parameters into disjoint blocks and performs sequential block-wise Adam updates across peer-to-peer clients, storing gradients and optimizer states only for the active block. To counter non-IID drift, it stabilizes first- and second-order block moments using fresh local gradients and consensus-derived discrepancy signals.
XjhvjWjujT.key_idea: Partitions parameters for sequential block-wise decentralized Adam updates and stabilizes block moments with local gradients and neighbor-consensus discrepancy signals.
XjhvjWjujT.evidence: Theoretical convergence analysis plus decentralized fine-tuning experiments (including Llama-3.1-8B) across tasks, client counts, and network topologies.
XjhvjWjujT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decentralized full-parameter LLM fine-tuning under non-IID data is an important problem and that DECA reduces memory while achieving competitive classification results.
XjhvjWjujT.main_concern: Reviewers flag unclear training-budget alignment and block-granularity inconsistencies between text and tables, limited LLM-specific novelty over general decentralized optimization, and ambiguity in constructing the final global model.

yPlFKWdec6.one_liner: Reframes LLM unlearning as token rendering and freezes the base model while tuning a shared cluster-level relation-transmittance matrix (T3-Unlearning).
yPlFKWdec6.problem: Output-based LLM unlearning objectives suppress target predictions without explicitly parameterizing the attention-mediated token relations that generate them.
yPlFKWdec6.method: The authors propose a token-rendering perspective characterizing unlearning losses as renderability control and introduce T3-Unlearning. Keeping the base LLM frozen, it learns a small shared relation-depth transmittance matrix over semantic token clusters across layers and heads to attenuate forget-sensitive relations while constraining retain-sensitive ones.
yPlFKWdec6.key_idea: Freezes the base LLM and tunes a shared semantic-cluster relation-transmittance bias matrix in attention to attenuate forget-sensitive token pathways.
yPlFKWdec6.evidence: First-order theoretical analysis and experiments on TOFU and WMDP across multiple LLMs and forgetting ratios.
yPlFKWdec6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree freezing the base LLM to train a compact relation matrix is a modular, parameter-efficient design that outperforms compared baselines across models and forget ratios.
yPlFKWdec6.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the volume-rendering framing as renaming standard log-probabilities and attention logit biases, under-specified semantic clustering robustness, small outdated models, and weak adversarial/relearning tests.

TRDHmxKKa2.one_liner: Tests whether LLM agents confuse prior isolated-environment rehearsal success for production completion and evaluates copying scope metadata beside tool receipts.
TRDHmxKKa2.problem: When LLM agents retain history from pre-production test environments, they may falsely conclude that required production actions are already complete.
TRDHmxKKa2.method: The authors evaluate 13 model deployments on controlled transformations of 60 tasks from tau-bench and AppWorld, checking native environment state alongside human-validated completion-claim annotations. They compare separating environment mappings in a header versus copying environment scope directly beside each receipt or wrapping receipts in JSON.
TRDHmxKKa2.key_idea: Isolates execution-scope confusion by comparing identical histories where environment mappings sit in a separate header versus being copied directly beside each tool receipt.
TRDHmxKKa2.evidence: Evaluations of 13 LLM deployments on 60 tasks (36 tau-bench, 24 AppWorld) with native state checks, post-execution controls, and repeated-run panels.
TRDHmxKKa2.claimed_gains: Rehearsal history raises false completion claims from 1.9% to 79.9% on tau-bench and 7.7% to 69.9% on AppWorld; copying scope beside receipts drops these to 18.8% and 24.7%.
TRDHmxKKa2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study cleanly isolates a striking, practical execution-scope failure mode across all 13 deployments using controlled information-equivalent renderings.
TRDHmxKKa2.main_concern: Reviewers question the realism of mixing rehearsal and target calls in one trajectory with header-only mappings, note only 60 tasks with single rollouts per cell, and find custom terminology hard to read.

inuj5eRE9C.one_liner: Assigns action-level PPO credit in agentic workflows via an auxiliary training-time counterfactual tree search (ASCT) using cost-aware AgentUCT.
inuj5eRE9C.problem: Terminal rewards in multi-step agentic workflows fail to identify which individual decisions helped or hurt task performance.
inuj5eRE9C.method: The authors propose ASCT, where an auxiliary evaluator runs counterfactual multi-step continuations from legal actions at actor-visited states using Uniform, UCT, or cost-aware AgentUCT budget allocation. Centering estimated action values by the actor's frozen probabilities yields PPO advantages on actor-sampled trajectories, with no search needed at deployment.
inuj5eRE9C.key_idea: Uses an auxiliary training-time counterfactual tree search (AgentUCT) at actor-visited states to estimate centered action-level PPO advantages without deploying search.
inuj5eRE9C.evidence: Three-seed experiments on HotpotQA agentic RAG comparing against trajectory-return PPO and VinePPO, plus auxiliary token accounting, transfer, and continuation controls.
inuj5eRE9C.claimed_gains: Across three seeds on HotpotQA, ASCT-AgentUCT achieves 0.6187 mean held-out utility versus 0.5939 for VinePPO while using 50.1% fewer tokens for auxiliary evaluation.
inuj5eRE9C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree decoupling auxiliary training-time search from actor behavior sampling and deployment is clean and consistently outperforms VinePPO across three seeds.
inuj5eRE9C.main_concern: Reviewers question reliance on search continuations rather than the actor's own policy, unisolated allocation versus continuation ablations, small fixed action spaces, and unclear end-to-end training speedup.

N4bHM9GNt1.one_liner: Applies negative parameter extrapolation after self-training to steer world models toward diverse synthetic experience.
N4bHM9GNt1.problem: Training world models for model-based reinforcement learning requires substantial real interaction data, while naive self-training on generated experience amplifies concentration tendencies.
N4bHM9GNt1.method: The authors formulate self-improvement for both unconditional generative replay and conditional latent dynamics models by self-training on generated experience and then reversing the resulting parameter displacement via negative extrapolation.
